I not only knew that it had been on the New York Times best-seller list for fifteen weeks; I had also kept running into Feynman in books by scientist-writers, like Jeremy Bernstein, who revere him as one of the giants of twentieth-century theoretical physics.

声音和语调。读完《冥王星共和国》不久，我又买了一本另一位诺贝尔奖得主的书：《费曼先生，您肯定是在开玩笑吧！》（Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman!），作者是理查德·费曼，由拉尔夫·莱顿口述。我不仅知道这本书曾连续十五周登上《纽约时报》畅销书榜单，而且还经常在像杰里米·伯恩斯坦这样的科学家作家的书中看到费曼的身影，他们都将费曼奉为二十世纪理论物理学的巨匠之一。

The book is an autobiography, and from about page three I had no trouble believing that Feynman is one of the smartest people in the world. But that’s not what he primarily wants me to believe. The subtitle of his book is “Adventures of a Curious Character,” and the blurbs make much of Feynman’s reputation for being “irrepressible,” “uninhibited,” “outrageous,” “zany” and an all-around funny fellow. The result is exhausting—Henny Youngman in a lab coat.

这本书是费曼的自传，从第三页左右我就开始相信他是世界上最聪明的人之一。但这并非他主要想让我相信的。这本书的副标题是“一个古怪人物的冒险”，宣传语也大肆渲染费曼“精力充沛”、“无拘无束”、“惊世骇俗”、“古怪滑稽”以及他是个十足的幽默人物。结果令人疲惫不堪——简直就像穿着白大褂的亨尼·扬曼。

Maybe it’s not fair to compare a book that is “told,” like Feynman’s, with one that is written, like Medawar’s. Still, both purport to be books: They are how two great scientists chose to present themselves to the reading public. Medawar knew that how we write is how we define ourselves—our style is who we are—and his style reflects a mind that is strong and supple. Feynman’s mind is no less strong and supple, but his style is strenuously breezy—he wants to be the life of the party. The two words he routinely uses for his colleagues are “guy” and “fella,” even when the fella is an Oppenheimer or a Fermi or a Bohr.

或许将费曼的“讲述式”著作与梅达沃的“写作式”著作相提并论并不公平。然而，两者都自诩为书籍：它们代表了两位伟大科学家向读者展现自我的方式。梅达沃深谙写作之道，他明白我们如何写作就是如何定义自我——我们的风格就是我们是谁——而他的风格也体现了他思维的敏锐与灵活。费曼的思维同样敏锐灵活，但他的风格却轻松诙谐——他渴望成为聚会的焦点。他经常用“伙计”和“老兄”来称呼他的同事，即便这位“老兄”是奥本海默、费米或玻尔这样的人物。

I don’t want Feynman to be the life of the party; I want him to be the smartest scientist in the world. In talking down to me he degrades not only me but himself. I finally had to stop reading his book. I can’t handle an A-plus mind expressing itself in C-minus sentences. I believe too strongly that mind and language are inseparable. If we violate our language we violate ourselves.

我不想让费曼成为派对上的焦点；我希望他成为世界上最聪明的科学家。他居高临下地跟我说话，不仅贬低了我，也贬低了他自己。我最终不得不停止阅读他的书。我无法接受一个才华横溢的人用平庸的语言表达自己。我坚信，思想和语言密不可分。如果我们违背了语言的原则，就是在违背我们自身。

My guess is that Feynman was persuaded that a book by the smartest scientist in the world wouldn’t sell unless he purveyed himself as the lovable fella next door, and certainly a fifteen-week run on the best-seller list is hard to argue with. Still, I think his writer and his editor did him a disservice. Long after Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman! has come and gone, books like Lewis Thomas’s Lives of a Cell and Douglas Hofstadter’s Gödel, Escher, Bach will still be around, their authors remembered as men of wisdom and stature. Thomas and Hofstadter aren’t trying to be a pal to the reader; they’re trying to write good English. They know that the English language, reverently used, will carry any load.

我猜想，费曼当时被说服了，除非他把自己塑造成邻家大哥那样平易近人，否则这位世界上最聪明的科学家写的书是卖不出去的。当然，连续十五周位居畅销书榜单确实难以反驳。不过，我认为他的作者和编辑对他并不公平。即便《你肯定是在开玩笑吧，费曼先生！》早已过时，像刘易斯·托马斯的《细胞的生命》和道格拉斯·霍夫施塔特的《哥德尔、埃舍尔、巴赫》这样的书依然会流传下去，它们的作者也会被人们铭记为智慧和地位的象征。托马斯和霍夫施塔特并非想和读者套近乎，他们只是想写出优美的英文。他们深知，只要运用得当，英语本身就能承载任何意义。

Moral: There are no cheap substitutes for the best.

寓意：最好的东西没有廉价的替代品。

B REVITY . In writing, short is usually better than long. Short words and sentences are easier for the eye and the mind to process than long ones, and an article that makes its case succinctly is the highest form of courtesy to the reader. Somehow it never occurs to sloppy writers that they are being fundamentally rude. Most pieces can be cut by 50 percent without losing any substance.

简洁。写作中，短小精悍通常胜过冗长繁复。短词短句比长词短句更容易被读者阅读和理解，一篇条理清晰、言简意赅的文章是对读者最高的尊重。然而，那些写作马虎的人似乎从未意识到，他们的行为从根本上来说是一种失礼。大多数文章删减一半也不会损失任何实质内容。

Brevity is one sign of a well-organized mind. As evidence let me present a letter by A. L. Rowse, the eminent Oxford don, that ran in the New York Times on December 8, 1985, at the height of the furor over an American scholar’s claim that he had discovered a “lost” poem by William Shakespeare. As proof the American cited similar words and phrases that his computer had found in the new poem and in the body of Shakespeare’s known works. Rowse demurred:

简洁是思维缜密的标志之一。作为佐证，请允许我引用牛津大学著名学者A·L·罗伊斯的一封信。这封信于1985年12月8日发表在《纽约时报》上，当时正值一位美国学者声称发现了莎士比亚一首“遗失”的诗作，引发轩然大波。这位美国学者列举了他的电脑在新诗作和莎士比亚已知作品中发现的相似词句作为证据。罗伊斯对此表示异议：

To the Editor:

致编辑：

I have been requested from several quarters to give my opinion on the supposed discovery of a new Shakespeare poem (front page, Nov. 24). It is utterly improbable for the following reasons:

有好几方都请我谈谈所谓发现莎士比亚新诗一事（11月24日头版）。这件事完全不可能，原因如下：

• It is quite unlike any poem that Shakespeare ever wrote.

• 这首诗与莎士比亚以往写过的任何一首诗都截然不同。

• We know quite well from the early poems “A Lover’s Complaint” and “Venus and Adonis” what Shakespeare’s early style was; and this poem is utterly unlike it.

• 从莎士比亚早期的诗歌《恋人的怨诉》和《维纳斯与阿多尼斯》中，我们已经很清楚地了解了莎士比亚早期的风格；而这首诗与他的早期风格截然不同。

• Shakespeare was so famous in his own time that people would not have overlooked anything of his. Quite the reverse. They published under his name, to exploit it, poems that are definitely known not to be his.

莎士比亚在世时名声显赫，人们绝不会忽视他的任何作品。恰恰相反，为了牟利，有人以他的名义出版了许多明知并非出自他之手的诗作。

The conclusion is clear—impossible that this ordinary poem is his. There are scores like it in manuscript collections.

结论显而易见——这首普通的诗不可能是他写的。手稿集中有很多类似的诗。

Those who would like to think it is Shakespeare’s are quite good, conventional scholars, but academic. One needs to be a practicing poet, and these scholars have no ear for poetry. A computer is no judge of what is poetry.

那些认为这首诗是莎士比亚作品的人，都是相当优秀的传统学者，但他们过于学院派。诗歌需要实践才能评判，而这些学者缺乏对诗歌的鉴赏力。电脑无法判断什么是诗歌。

That’s the case stated in 133 words. Granted, Rowse’s letter has none of the high umbrage and malediction that make most academic squabbles such enjoyable reading, but that’s a whole other sport.

这就是用133个字概括的案情。诚然，罗伊斯的信中没有大多数学术争论中那种令人读来津津乐道的愤慨和诅咒，但这完全是另一回事了。

J ARGON . Jargon is the lingo of people in specialized fields who have infected each other with their private terminology and don’t think there’s any other way to say what they mean. Somewhere they forgot about the mother tongue. There’s almost no subject that can’t be made accessible in good English.

行话。行话是特定领域人士使用的术语，他们彼此之间互相灌输这种私密的词汇，并且认为除了这些术语之外，没有其他表达方式。他们似乎忘记了母语。几乎没有哪个主题是无法用流利的英语表达清楚的。

A few years ago I was shanghaied onto an advisory panel at a major corporation, and at our first meeting someone asked the chairman what the committee had been formed to do. He said, “It’s an umbrella group that interacts synergistically to platform and leverage cultural human resources strategies company-wide.” That pretty much ended my interest in the committee, and when it subsequently experienced viability deprivation (went down the tubes) I was overjoyed. God was in his heaven after all. There’s no place for such garbage in the working world.

几年前，我被强行拉进一家大公司的一个顾问委员会。第一次开会时，有人问主席，这个委员会是做什么的。他回答说：“这是一个统筹协调的机构，旨在协同运作，在全公司范围内推广和运用文化人力资源战略。” 这句话几乎让我对这个委员会彻底失去了兴趣。后来，当它彻底失败（彻底解散）时，我欣喜若狂。上帝终于眷顾了我。职场上根本不应该有这种垃圾存在。

But I was lucky; most Americans get that kind of junk inflicted on them year after year by their executives and managers. Here’s how one of New York’s biggest banks recently started—and continued for twelve pages—a memo to the staff:

但我很幸运；大多数美国人年复一年地遭受着高管和经理们强加给他们的这类垃圾信息。以下是纽约一家大型银行最近写给员工的一份备忘录的开头——而且这份备忘录长达十二页：

While our efforts cannot be characterized as having had a profoundly strategic horizon, the methodology utilized to identify strategy statements was not sufficiently program oriented for implementation.

虽然我们的努力不能被描述为具有深刻的战略远见，但用于确定战略声明的方法对于实施而言，其项目导向性还不够强。

No wonder so many Americans hate their jobs. Who wants to work for bosses who deal with the help in such dehumanizing language? The people writing and talking most pompously in America today are people in authority.

难怪这么多美国人讨厌自己的工作。谁愿意为那些用如此不人道的语言对待员工的老板工作呢？如今在美国，那些说话和写作最傲慢自大的人，正是那些身居要职的人。

Here’s a letter that a school superintendent sent to his teachers at the start of the new school year:

以下是一位学校校长在新学年开始时写给老师们的一封信：

In the spirit of collegiality with a commitment toward maximizing faculty involvement in the exploration and resolution of issues and needs confronting this Division in response to its multi-dimensional challenges, I suggest that the departments target representatives to begin the divisional identification of the issues and needs considered most relevant to determine what formats would be most convenient.

本着同僚精神，致力于最大限度地让教职工参与探索和解决本部门面临的各种问题和需求，以应对其多方面的挑战，我建议各系选派代表，开始确定本部门认为最相关的问题和需求，以确定最方便的形式。

Spare me such collegial colleagues.

饶了我吧，别让我遇到这种好同事。

Jargon, of course, takes a multitude of forms. The two preceding examples are typical of the buzzwords—mostly nouns—that infest such fields as management, banking, insurance, education and government. They are words that make the insider feel important when he uses them but that don’t really mean anything. What is a profoundly strategic horizon? Just what are those formats that it would be most relevant to determine? An outsider can only try to translate and hope for the best—a task made harder by the tendency of fad nouns to attach themselves to other fad nouns. Recently I sighted this brilliant cluster: “communication facilitation skills development intervention.” Five nouns, but no human activity that I could visualize. I went at the problem like a code breaker. “Intervention” = “help” or “teach”; “development” + “facilitation” = “improve”; “communication skills” = “writing.” Solution: a program to help kids write better.

当然，行话的形式多种多样。前面两个例子就是典型的流行语——大多是名词——充斥着管理、银行、保险、教育和政府等领域。这些词让内部人士在使用时感觉自己很重要，但实际上却毫无意义。什么是深远的战略视野？究竟哪些形式最值得确定？局外人只能尝试翻译，然后祈祷一切顺利——而流行名词往往会与其他流行名词捆绑在一起，这使得翻译工作更加困难。最近，我发现了一个绝妙的词组：“沟通促进技能发展干预”。五个名词，但我却想象不出任何具体的人类活动。我像破译密码一样着手解决这个问题。“干预”=“帮助”或“教学”；“发展”+“促进”=“改进”；“沟通技能”=“写作”。答案：一个帮助孩子提高写作能力的项目。

More often jargon consists of special terms that every occupation has found it necessary to invent. Used with restraint, they aren’t jargon; they are the working tools of a particular field, and if they serve a specific need we have no trouble learning new ones overnight: words like “amniocentesis” and “gentrification” and “superconductivity.” The trouble arises when jargon becomes a crutch—when its users become so dependent on their private terminology that they claim they can’t express themselves in any other way. Social scientists, for instance, are addicted almost beyond mortal help.

行话通常指的是各行各业为了生存而创造的特殊术语。如果使用得当，它们就不是行话，而是特定领域的工作工具。如果它们服务于某种特定需求，我们也能很快学会新的术语，比如“羊膜穿刺术”、“中产阶级化”和“超导性”。问题在于，当行话变成拐杖时——当使用者过度依赖自己的专属术语，以至于声称无法用其他方式表达自己时。例如，社会科学家对行话的依赖几乎到了无可救药的地步。

Consider these two sentences from a book by a famous sociologist. I didn’t choose them as exceptions; the whole book is in this style.

请看以下两句话，它们出自一位著名社会学家的著作。我并非特意挑选这两句话；整本书都是这种风格。

The third major component of modeling phenomena involves the utilization of symbolic representations of modeled patterns in the form of imaginal and verbal contents to guide overt performances. It is assumed that reinstatement of representational schemes provides a basis for self-instruction on how component responses must be combined and sequenced to produce new patterns of behavior.

建模现象的第三个主要组成部分涉及利用以想象和语言形式呈现的建模模式的符号表征来指导外在行为。人们认为，表征图式的重建为自我指导提供了基础，使个体能够了解如何组合和排序各种反应，从而产生新的行为模式。

That’s either 86-proof jargon, preposterous and unnecessary, or it’s one sociologist talking to another in language as clear to them both as “hop on Pop” or “see Spot run.” I like to think that even those two sentences could be turned into relatively plain English, but I’ll buy the sociologist’s argument (the one he would surely make) that he is entitled to write in his tribal language if he is addressing other sociologists—for instance, in a journal of sociology. But any specialist who doesn’t clean up his jargon when he’s writing for the general population deserves to be, if not tarred, at least feathered by the mob.

这要么是晦涩难懂的专业术语，荒谬且毫无必要；要么就是一位社会学家在用彼此都听不懂的语言交流，比如“上爸爸的车”或者“看小狗跑”。我倒觉得，即使是这两句话也能用相对简单的英语表达出来，但我接受这位社会学家的论点（他肯定会这么说）：如果他是在和其他社会学家交流——比如在社会学期刊上——那么他有权使用自己的专业术语。但是，任何专家如果在面向大众写作时仍然使用晦涩难懂的专业术语，那他就算不被泼焦油，至少也应该被大众唾弃。

T HE I LLITERACY OF THE E LITE . Whenever you see in the newspaper or hear someone say that writing in America has gone to the dogs, you can bet that it’s the educated classes who are doing the bewailing and the uneducated classes and the young who are being bewailed. But which of these two sentences is more illiterate:

精英阶层的文盲。每当你在报纸上看到或听到有人说美国的写作水平已经一落千丈时，你都可以肯定，哀叹的总是受过教育的阶层，而哀叹的对象则是未受过教育的阶层和年轻人。但是，以下哪句话更文盲呢？

1. The ongoing reconfiguration positions Barbara offsite to hopefully identify growth and profitability potentials beyond what is currently being realized.

1. 正在进行的重新配置将芭芭拉安排到异地，希望能够发现目前尚未实现的增长和盈利潜力。

2. Barbara will try to find out why we ain’t doing better.

2. 芭芭拉会努力找出我们做得不够好的原因。

Number one—a corporate memo I found in my in-box last year—is scandalous in its flatulence. Yet it’s typical corporation-speak. Number two is a little uneducated but a lot more helpful. If clear writing is one of the foundations of a democratic society, don’t count on getting it from men and women with a college degree. Ivy League alumni magazines are awash with letters so grammatically squalid that they barely make sense. Clean-up time at this toxic dump has to start at the top.

第一份——去年我在收件箱里发现的一份公司备忘录——简直荒谬至极，令人作呕。然而，这却是典型的公司用语。第二份虽然略显粗俗，但却更有帮助。如果说清晰的写作是民主社会的基础之一，那么就别指望能从那些拥有大学学历的人那里得到它。常春藤盟校的校友杂志上充斥着语法糟糕透顶、几乎让人不知所云的信件。清理这个“毒瘤”必须从高层开始。

K ILLER N OUNS . Probably there isn’t a writing teacher (including me) who hasn’t assailed his students with George Orwell’s rendering into modern sludge of the verse from Ecclesiastes about the race not being to the swift. That’s not going to stop me from citing it again. The verse goes like this:

杀手级名词。大概没有哪个写作老师（包括我）没用乔治·奥威尔对《传道书》中“赛跑不是快跑的”那句诗的现代改编来“轰炸”过学生。但这并不会阻止我再次引用它。这句诗是这样的：

I returned and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

我又见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢，力战的未必能胜，智慧的未必能得粮食，明哲的未必能得财富，灵巧的未必能得喜悦；所临到众人的，乃是在乎时间和机会。

That’s a wonderful sentence. The words are refreshingly short; they instantly appeal to the eye and make us want to read them. More important, all the nouns are working nouns: they denote objects (bread) or activities (race, battle) or attainments (riches, favor) or conditions of fate (time, chance) that we can relate to our own lives.

这是一个绝妙的句子。用词简洁明了，令人耳目一新，忍不住想要读下去。更重要的是，所有名词都是动词性名词：它们指代我们可以与自身生活联系起来的物品（面包）、活动（比赛、战斗）、成就（财富、恩惠）或命运（时间、机遇）。

This is how Orwell said the passage would come out in the pompous bureaucratic language of our times:

奥威尔说，这段文字用我们这个时代浮夸的官僚语言会是这样呈现的：

Objective consideration of contemporary phenomena compels the conclusion that success or failure in competitive activities exhibits no tendency to be commensurate with innate capacity, but that a considerable element of the unpredictable must invariably be taken into account.

对当代现象的客观考察迫使我们得出这样的结论：竞争活动中的成功或失败与先天能力并不成正比，而必须始终考虑相当大的不可预测因素。

That’s also a wonderful sentence. Please remember that sentence: it’s the enemy. Just at a glance it repels us—we don’t want to spend any time with a mind that expresses itself in such bloated words. What makes the words so ponderous is that they don’t have any people in them; they only have concepts—“consideration,” “conclusion,” “capacity,” “tendency.” Nouns that denote concepts are the death of vigorous writing. Good writing is specific and concrete.

那也是一句绝妙的句子。请记住这句话：它是敌人。它乍一看就令人反感——我们不想浪费时间在一个用如此冗长词藻表达思想的人身上。这些词语之所以如此沉重，是因为它们没有具体的人；它们只有概念——“考虑”、“结论”、“能力”、“倾向”。指代概念的名词扼杀了流畅的写作。好的写作是具体而明确的。

Here’s a more recent example: the Port Huron Statement, which became the manifesto of the New Left and of the Students for a Democratic Society—and thus a prime document of the counterculture—in 1960. It was drafted by Tom Hayden, whose first version began like this:

以下是一个更近期的例子：《休伦港宣言》，它于1960年成为新左派和争取民主社会学生会的宣言，从而成为反主流文化的重要文献。该宣言由汤姆·海登起草，其初稿如下：

Every generation inherits from the past a set of problems—and a dominant set of insights and perspectives by which the problems are to be understood and, hopefully, managed.

每一代人都会从过去继承一系列问题，以及一套主导性的见解和视角，通过这些见解和视角，人们可以理解并（希望）解决这些问题。

For a manifesto, that’s well above the acceptable limit in concept nouns, generalized ideas and passive verbs, and someone told Hayden it wouldn’t do. Rewriting it on the spot, he got personal and specific and created a classic:

作为一份宣言，它使用了远超可接受范围的概念名词、概括性观点和被动语态，有人告诉海登这样不行。他当场重写，使其更具个人色彩和针对性，最终创作出了一部经典之作：

We are people of this generation, bred in at least modest comfort, housed now in universities, looking uncomfortably to the world we inherit.

我们是这一代人，成长于至少还算舒适的环境中，如今身处大学校园，却不安地看着我们即将继承的世界。

L IFESAVING V ERBS . One way to take the mush out of concept nouns is to turn them into active verbs. Verbs are the strongest tools a writer is given, because they embody an action. Active verbs are stronger than passive verbs, because they propel a sentence forward. They also enable us to picture who did what, because they require a pronoun or a noun: “I,” “we,” “she,” “you,” “boy,” “girl.” Seeing a pronoun or a noun and an active verb together, we visualize a specific event that occurred at a specific moment. Passive verbs have no such energy or precision:

动词是救命稻草。摆脱概念名词的晦涩难懂的一个方法是将它们转化为主动动词。动词是写作者最强大的工具，因为它们体现了动作。主动动词比被动动词更有力，因为它们推动句子向前发展。它们还能让我们想象出谁做了什么，因为它们需要代词或名词：“我”、“我们”、“她”、“你”、“男孩”、“女孩”。当代词或名词与主动动词结合在一起时，我们就能想象出在特定时刻发生的特定事件。被动动词则缺乏这种活力和精确性：

A CTIVE: I saw the boys skating on the pond.

活跃：我看到男孩们在池塘上滑冰。

P ASSIVE: The boys were seen skating on the pond. [By whom? When? How often?]

被动语态：有人看到男孩们在池塘上滑冰。[谁看到的？何时看到的？多久一次？]

In the following paragraph—from Norman Mailer’s ringside account of the death of the welterweight boxer Benny Paret in the twelfth round of a championship fight with Emile Griffith in Madison Square Garden on March 25, 1962—notice the tremendous punch that active verbs deliver:

在以下段落中——摘自诺曼·梅勒对次中量级拳击手本尼·帕雷特在1962年3月25日于麦迪逊广场花园与埃米尔·格里菲斯进行的冠军赛第十二回合中丧生的现场报道——请注意主动动词所带来的巨大冲击力：

Paret died on his feet. As he took those eighteen punches something happened to everyone who was in psychic range of the event. Some part of his death reached out to us. One felt it hover in the air. He was still standing in the ropes, trapped as he had been before, he gave some little half-smile of regret, as if he were saying, “I didn’t know I was going to die just yet,” and then, his head leaning back but still erect, his death came to breathe about him. He began to pass away. As he passed, so his limbs descended beneath him, and he sank slowly to the floor. He went down more slowly than any fighter had ever gone down, he went down like a large ship which turns on end and slides second by second into its grave. As he went down, the sound of Griffith’s punches echoed in the mind like a heavy ax in the distance chopping into a wet log.

帕雷特站着死去。当他承受那十八记重拳时，所有在场的人都仿佛感受到了某种异样。他死亡的一部分触及了我们，仿佛悬浮在空中。他仍然像之前那样被困在拳台绳索中，脸上浮现出一丝遗憾的微笑，仿佛在说：“我没想到自己会这么快死去。”然后，他的头向后仰，但依然挺直，死亡的气息开始在他周围弥漫。他开始消逝。随着他的消逝，他的四肢也随之垂落，他缓缓地沉入地面。他下沉的速度比任何拳击手都慢，就像一艘巨轮翻转，一秒一秒地滑入坟墓。在他倒下的同时，格里菲斯的重拳声在脑海中回荡，如同远处一把沉重的斧头劈开一根湿漉漉的木头。

Imagine that paragraph written with passive verbs and concept nouns: “A sensation of Paret’s mortality was experienced by the audience. The feeling was retained as an ongoing presence in the atmosphere.”

想象一下用被动语态和概念名词写成的这段话：“观众感受到了帕雷特终有一死。这种感觉持续地萦绕在空气中。”

Active verbs are a writer’s best friend. Not every concept noun can be turned into an active verb. But how many people are even trying?

主动动词是作家的好朋友。并非所有概念名词都能转化为主动动词。但又有多少人尝试过呢？

V ISIBLE D ETAIL . Writing is not unlike the schoolroom period called “show and tell.” The writer should not only tell a story; he should try to make the reader see what he is writing about. As Mailer demonstrates, active verbs are ideal for this kind of work; they force us to witness an event.

可见的细节。写作与课堂上的“展示与讲述”环节颇为相似。作者不仅要讲述故事，更要努力让读者看到他所描写的事物。正如梅勒所展示的那样，主动语态的动词非常适合这类写作；它们能迫使我们亲眼目睹事件的发生。

But nouns are equally pictorial and helpful. I’m not talking (needless to say) about concept nouns. I mean the thousands of simple nouns, like “house” and “chair” and “earth” and “tree,” that denote the objects of everyday life and the properties of the world we live in. Unlike the long concept nouns, which tend to be of Latin origin and to end in “ion,” these are Anglo-Saxon words—short, blunt, homely and infinitely old. They are words that are in our bones and that resonate with emotions, whether we want them to or not. A writer who uses these nouns makes instant contact with the humanity of his reader by giving him a familiar picture.

但名词同样具有形象性和实用性。我指的并非（毋庸置疑）概念名词。我指的是成千上万个简单的名词，比如“房子”、“椅子”、“土地”和“树”，它们指代日常生活中的物品以及我们所居住的世界的属性。与那些往往源自拉丁语并以“ion”结尾的冗长概念名词不同，这些名词是盎格鲁-撒克逊语词汇——简短、直白、朴实，而且历史悠久。它们早已融入我们的骨髓，无论我们是否愿意，都能引起我们的情感共鸣。一位作家如果运用这些名词，就能通过赋予读者熟悉的画面感，瞬间与读者建立起情感上的联系。

The following 184-word sentence by Virginia Woolf, which begins an essay called “On Being Ill,” runs counter to everything I’ve said about brevity. In fact, it’s one of the longest sentences I’ve ever seen. But I like it. Its length is no problem because the author has her material under control from start to finish, and it stays in the mind’s eye long afterward because of all its vivid and surprising nouns:

弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在题为《论疾病》的文章开头写下了这句184个字的句子，这与我之前所说的简洁原则完全背道而驰。事实上，这是我见过的最长的句子之一。但我很喜欢它。它的长度不成问题，因为作者从头到尾都掌控着她的素材，而且由于其中生动而又出人意料的名词，这句话在读完之后会长时间留在我的脑海中：

Considering how common illness is, how tremendous the spiritual change that it brings, how astonishing, when the lights of health go down, the undiscovered countries that are then disclosed, what wastes and deserts of the soul a slight attack of influenza brings to view, what precipices and lawns sprinkled with bright flowers a little rise of temperature reveals, what ancient and obdurate oaks are uprooted in us by the act of sickness, how we go down into the pit of death and feel the waters of annihilation close above our heads and wake thinking to find ourselves in the presence of the angels and the harpers when we have a tooth out and come to the surface in the dentist’s arm-chair and confuse his “Rinse the mouth—rinse the mouth” with the greeting of the Deity stooping from the floor of Heaven to welcome us—when we think of this, as we are so frequently forced to think of it, it becomes strange indeed that illness has not taken its place with love and battle and jealousy among the prime themes of literature.

考虑到疾病的普遍性，它带来的精神改变又是多么巨大，当健康的光芒熄灭时，那些未知的领域又会展现在世人面前，一次轻微的流感就能让我们看到灵魂的荒芜和沙漠，气温稍稍升高就能让我们看到悬崖峭壁和鲜花盛开的草坪，疾病会将我们内心深处那些古老而顽强的橡树连根拔起，我们坠入死亡的深渊，感受到毁灭之水在我们头顶合拢，醒来时却以为自己置身于天使和竖琴演奏家的面前——当我们拔完牙，从牙医的扶手椅上浮出水面，把牙医“漱口——漱口”的叮嘱误认为是神从天上俯身迎接我们的问候——当我们想到这些，就像我们经常被迫想到的那样，疾病竟然没有像爱、战斗和嫉妒一样，成为人类社会的主要主题，这确实令人感到奇怪。 文学。

E NJOYMENT . Achieving a decent piece of writing is such a difficult task that it often strikes the reader as having been just that: a task. It accomplishes its purpose, and perhaps we shouldn’t ask for anything more. But we do. We wish the writer had had a better time—or at least had given us that impression. Here’s the opening paragraph of a recent biography of the illustrious man who was, among many other things, Great Britain’s last viceroy of India. It’s by Philip Ziegler and it’s called, appropriately, Mountbatten .

享受。写出一篇像样的文章如此困难，以至于读者常常觉得它仅仅是一项任务。它达到了目的，或许我们不该再奢求更多。但我们还是会奢求。我们希望作者能更享受写作的过程——或者至少能给我们留下这样的印象。以下是菲利普·齐格勒最近撰写的一部关于这位杰出人物的传记的开头段落，他曾担任过众多职务，其中包括英国最后一任印度总督。这本书的书名恰如其分地叫做《蒙巴顿传》。

Admiral of the Fleet, the Earl Mountbatten of Burma, was a man who, for his own amusement, rarely took up any book unless it were one of genealogy, most especially one relating to his own forebears. During the reaches of the night in the Viceroy’s House in Delhi, when his predecessors might have diverted themselves with the verses of Macaulay or the latest detective story by Mrs. Christie, Mountbatten would relax over the tapestry of his ancestry, enumerating the generations that divided him from the Emperor Charlemagne and marveling at the intricate web of cousinship which bound him many times over to the Wittelsbachs and the Romanoffs, the Habsburgs and the Hohenzollerns. His studies both gave him the satisfaction that attends the solution of a complex jigsaw puzzle and gratified that pride in family that was one of the most prominent of his characteristics.

海军元帅、缅甸蒙巴顿伯爵，除了家谱之外，鲜少翻阅其他书籍，尤其钟爱研究自己的祖先。在德里总督府的夜深人静之时，当他的前辈们或许会沉浸于麦考利的诗歌或克里斯蒂夫人的最新侦探小说中消遣时，蒙巴顿却会仔细研读家族谱系，细数自己与查理曼大帝之间的世代传承，并惊叹于错综复杂的亲缘关系，这些关系将他与维特尔斯巴赫家族、罗曼诺夫家族、哈布斯堡家族和霍亨索伦家族等众多家族紧密相连。他的研究既带给他如同完成复杂拼图般的满足感，也满足了他最显著的性格特征之一——对家族的自豪感。

What a lift that opening gives us. We’re off on a trip with a writer who savors his material, and no element in writing is quite so contagious. My favorite statement of this idea came from the humorist S. J. Perelman. I became a Perelman addict at sixteen and never got cured. In 1978, near the end of his life, I invited him to Yale to talk to my students. One of them asked him what it took to be a humor writer. “Comic writing,” he said, “needs audacity and exuberance and gaiety—and the most important of these is audacity.”

这段开篇真是令人振奋。我们仿佛跟随一位细细品味素材的作家踏上了一段旅程，而写作中没有哪个元素比这更具感染力。我最喜欢的关于这个观点的阐述来自幽默作家S·J·佩雷尔曼。我十六岁时就成了佩雷尔曼的忠实读者，至今仍无法自拔。1978年，在他生命的最后阶段，我邀请他来耶鲁大学为我的学生们演讲。其中一位学生问他，成为一名幽默作家需要具备哪些条件。“喜剧写作，”他回答说，“需要大胆、热情和欢乐——而其中最重要的是大胆。”

Then he said: “The reader has to believe that the writer is feeling good.”

然后他说：“读者必须相信作者心情很好。”

The sentence hit with me tremendous force, especially when he added, almost as an afterthought, “even if he isn’t.” I knew that Perelman’s life had had more than the usual share of days when he wasn’t feeling good—days of depression and emotional travail. Yet for fifty years he went to his typewriter every morning and took his readers on roller coaster rides of such dizzying swoops that they blew all our troubles away. Surely a writer having such a good time was a man without a care in the world.

这句话深深触动了我，尤其是当他几乎像是脱口而出地补充道：“即便他并非如此。”我知道佩雷尔曼的人生中经历过比常人更多的低谷——抑郁和情感折磨的日子。然而，五十年来，他每天早晨都坚持敲击键盘，带领读者体验跌宕起伏、令人目眩神迷的文字之旅，仿佛所有的烦恼都被抛诸脑后。一个如此享受写作乐趣的作家，想必是无忧无虑、无所畏惧的人。

Now, thinking of that feat, I realize that audacity was only part of what Perelman was talking about. He was also talking about courage. Humor is the most perilous of writing forms, full of risk; to make a vocation of brightening the reader’s day is an act of continuing gallantry. He was also talking about energy. Energy is the divine spark in creative work. We know right away when we are in its presence—we can’t hold Bach or Mozart down, or Picasso, or Mark Twain, or Frank Lloyd Wright, or Louise Nevelson, or Fred Astaire, or Lucille Ball, or Toscanini or Norman Mailer or Tom Wolfe. They sweep us along in the current of their life force. We seldom stop to think about the effort they made to switch it on and crank it up every morning.

现在回想起来，我意识到佩雷尔曼所说的只是大胆，而勇气只是其中的一部分。他还谈到了勇气。幽默是最危险的写作形式，充满了风险；以取悦读者为职业，本身就是一种持续的英勇行为。他还谈到了活力。活力是创作中神圣的火花。我们一眼就能感受到它的存在——我们无法束缚巴赫、莫扎特、毕加索、马克·吐温、弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特、路易丝·内维尔森、弗雷德·阿斯泰尔、露西尔·鲍尔、托斯卡尼尼、诺曼·梅勒或汤姆·沃尔夫。他们用生命力的洪流裹挟着我们前行。我们很少停下来思考，他们每天早上为了启动并激发这种活力付出了多少努力。

But what Perelman was finally talking about was craft. Writing is a craft, and a writer is someone who goes to work every day with his tools, like the carpenter or the television repairman, no matter how he feels, and if one of the things he wants to produce by 6 P.M . is a sense of enjoyment in his writing, he must generate it by an act of will. Nobody else is going to do it for him.

但佩雷尔曼最终谈论的是技艺。写作是一门技艺，作家就像木匠或电视修理工一样，每天都带着工具去工作，无论感觉如何。如果他想在下午六点前获得写作的乐趣，就必须通过意志力去创造这种乐趣。没有人会替他完成这件事。

I N S HORT . In short, these are some of my crotchets and convictions. Look for the convictions in Part II of this book, soon to begin. All the passages I’ve assembled there are the work of men and women who wrote with clarity, simplicity, warmth and enjoyment. In each case I’ve tried to explain why I think the piece is well written and why I like it. On the surface, therefore, Part II is an explicit lesson in how to write.

简而言之，这些就是我的一些怪癖和信念。敬请期待本书第二部分，即将开始。我收集的所有段落都出自文笔清晰、简洁、热情洋溢且充满乐趣的作家之手。在每篇文章中，我都试图解释我为何认为它写得好，以及我为何喜欢它。因此，从表面上看，第二部分是一堂关于如何写作的实用课程。

If it’s also about writing to learn (and it is), I’ve left that mostly implicit, not wanting to numb you with repetition of the same obvious point. Only two chapters—9 and 11—specifically demonstrate writing as a method of learning. But all the writers represented in Part II wrote clearly because the act of writing and rewriting made them think clearly, organized their ideas, told them what they knew and what they still needed to know, and pushed them to new areas of knowledge.

如果写作也关乎学习（而它确实如此），我并没有过多赘述，以免用显而易见的观点重复让你感到麻木。只有第九章和第十一章专门论述了写作作为一种学习方法。但第二部分中所有作者的写作都条理清晰，因为写作和修改的过程让他们思路清晰，组织思路，明确已知和未知，并推动他们探索新的知识领域。

It can do the same for you.

它也能为你做到这一点。

# ↩

PART II

第二部分

# ↩

6. Earth, Sea and Sky

6. 地球、海洋和天空

One of the few other adults who lived in our Gothic quadrangle when I was master of Branford College at Yale was a distinguished professor of geology, fast approaching the emeritus years, named John Rodgers. He had been a resident Fellow since 1948, and he was still there when I left, in 1979; he had seen masters come and go, mere ripples in the river of time. Being a geologist, he took a longer view than most people and was unruffled by such surface disturbances as families moving in and out of the master’s house every five or six years.

在我担任耶鲁大学布兰福德学院院长期间，我们哥特式庭院里除了我之外，只有少数几位成年人居住。其中一位是杰出的地质学教授，名叫约翰·罗杰斯，他即将荣休。自1948年以来，他一直是学院的常驻研究员，直到1979年我离开时，他仍然在那里。他见证了院长们的来来往往，如同时间长河中的涟漪。作为一名地质学家，他比大多数人看得更远，对于诸如每隔五六年院长官邸有人搬进搬出这种表面现象，他并不在意。

But he was also a humanist. Amid the detritus of his apartment, which was cluttered with old scientific journals and papers, he had a Steinway grand piano, on which he played Bach fugues and Chopin etudes very beautifully with his strong geologist’s fingers. Once he shyly asked if I would mind if he prepared and gave a recital in the college dining hall of the complete piano works of Scriabin. He thought it would be an instructive way—perhaps never tried in a concert before—of tracing how Scriabin explored different composing styles at different stages of his life.

但他同时也是一位人文主义者。在他那堆满旧科学期刊和论文的杂乱公寓里，摆放着一架斯坦威三角钢琴。他用那双地质学家般灵巧的手指，将巴赫的赋格曲和肖邦的练习曲弹奏得格外优美。有一次，他腼腆地问我，他是否介意在大学餐厅里准备并演奏斯克里亚宾的全部钢琴作品。他认为这将是一个富有启发性的方式——或许以前从未在音乐会上尝试过——来追溯斯克里亚宾在其人生不同阶段探索不同作曲风格的过程。

The recital (I didn’t mind) was a gem of both music and scholarship, for the geologist-pianist had also written graceful program notes to guide us on our trip. That part of the evening didn’t surprise me; I knew that good writing was as important to John Rodgers as good geology. One year he was so maddened by a fuzzy student dissertation that he wrote and distributed to his classes a manifesto called “The Rules of Bad Writing.” These were a few of its entries:

这场音乐会（我并不介意）堪称音乐与学术的双重瑰宝，因为这位地质学家兼钢琴家还撰写了优美的节目单，为我们讲解了相关知识。当晚的这一部分并没有让我感到意外；我知道，对于约翰·罗杰斯来说，好的写作与好的地质学研究同样重要。有一年，他被一篇含糊不清的学生论文气得火冒三丈，于是撰写了一份名为《糟糕写作规则》的宣言，并分发给了他的学生们。以下是其中的一些内容：

• Never use the same word twice for the same idea. Thus you make sure that the reader never knows whether it’s the same idea or not.

• 永远不要用同一个词两次表达同一个意思。这样可以确保读者永远无法判断它们是否表达的是同一个意思。

• Never use the first person where you can use ambiguous phrases like “the writer” (especially when you’ve just mentioned some other writer) or, better still, “it is thought” or “it is considered,” so that the reader can’t be exactly sure who thinks what, or what—if anything—you do think.

• 永远不要使用第一人称，而应该使用像“作者”这样的含糊不清的短语（尤其是在你刚刚提到其他作者的时候），或者更好的是，使用“人们认为”或“人们考虑”这样的短语，这样读者就无法确切地确定是谁在想什么，或者你到底在想什么（如果有的话）。

• Never use an active verb where a passive verb will do. It pads out the sentence nicely and puts more distance between you and the facts—and the reader.

• 能用被动语态就不要用主动语态。主动语态会让句子显得冗长，反而拉大了你和事实——以及读者——之间的距离。

Every June, when the Yale college year was over, I knew I could expect a formal call some evening from John Rodgers—as formal, at any rate, as a call can be when the visitor is wearing mountain boots and the host is wearing sneakers. He had the punctilio of an old-fashioned don and wouldn’t think of leaving for the summer without letting me know. It was the only time I felt that I was living in a novel by C. P. Snow; otherwise the life of a college master had a way of slipping imperceptibly between the ceremonial and the janitorial.

每年六月，耶鲁大学学年结束之时，我都知道某个晚上会接到约翰·罗杰斯的正式电话——当然，这电话也只能算是正式，毕竟来访者穿着登山靴，而主人穿着运动鞋。他一丝不苟，像个老派的大学教授，绝不会在暑假离开前不告诉我一声。只有那时，我才觉得自己仿佛置身于C·P·斯诺的小说之中；否则，大学教授的生活总是在礼仪和琐事之间悄然游走。

“Where are you off to?” I would say when he sat down.

他坐下后，我会问他：“你要去哪儿？”

“I’m going to the Urals,” he would say. “I’ve never done the Urals. I didn’t want to go until I had learned Russian.” The previous summer it had been a range in western Australia. He was a man who collected mountain ranges; they were like old friends to him, as distinctive as stamps or coins or cats or any other collectible.

“我要去乌拉尔山脉，”他会说。“我从没去过乌拉尔山脉。我本来想等学会俄语后再去。”前一个夏天，他去的是西澳大利亚的山脉。他喜欢收集山脉；对他来说，山脉就像老朋友一样，如同邮票、硬币、猫或其他任何收藏品一样独具特色。

Now I called and asked him whether he had done any writing about mountain ranges. He said he had written articles only for scientific journals. I told him that was good enough for me; I had a feeling that even in a scientific paper John Rodgers could make his subject clear to anybody. He sent me an article called “The Life History of a Mountain Range—The Appalachians.” It began like this:

我打电话问他是否写过关于山脉的文章。他说他只为科学期刊写过文章。我告诉他这对我来说已经足够了；我觉得即使是科学论文，约翰·罗杰斯也能把他的主题讲得通俗易懂。他寄给我一篇题为《山脉的生命史——阿巴拉契亚山脉》的文章。文章开头是这样的：

I strongly suspect that my interest in the subject I am to discuss here was awakened when as a schoolboy I picked up in a second-hand bookshop a copy of James Geikie’s book: Mountains, Their Origin, Growth and Decay (1913). I read it through fascinated, though of course not comprehending half of it, and despite disparaging remarks from members of my family, who dubbed it Mountains, Their Cause and Cure , I have been fascinated by the subject ever since.

我强烈怀疑，我对即将探讨的主题的兴趣，源于我学生时代在一家二手书店偶然发现的詹姆斯·盖基（James Geikie）的著作《山脉：起源、生长与衰败》（1913）。我如痴如醉地读完了这本书，当然，其中有一半内容我根本没看懂。尽管我的家人对此嗤之以鼻，甚至戏称它为《山脉：成因与解药》，但我从此便对这个主题着迷不已。

Mountain ranges are of course not living organisms, but we geologists have long believed with Geikie that they go through a sequence of stages over geologic time, from a period when nothing hints that a range will develop in the future, through a stage of origin (the geosyncline) and a period in which mountains grow (the orogeny), to a stage of decay ending in their dissection and obliteration, often in their interment beneath a cover of younger sediment. Here I shall not attempt a generic description of a life applicable to all mountain ranges, but rather a specific one, that of the range best known to me, the Appalachians of eastern North America, and at first I shall concentrate on their northern half, especially New England, beside which I grew up (reading Geikie’s book) and in which I have spent the largest part of my own life history.

山脉当然不是生物体，但我们地质学家长期以来都和盖基一样认为，山脉在地质时期会经历一系列阶段：从没有任何迹象表明未来会形成山脉的时期，到起源阶段（地槽），再到山脉生长阶段（造山运动），最终到衰败阶段，最终被切割和消亡，往往被埋没在较新的沉积物之下。在这里，我不会尝试对所有山脉进行普遍适用的描述，而是着重介绍我最熟悉的山脉——北美东部的阿巴拉契亚山脉。首先，我将重点放在其北部，特别是新英格兰地区，我正是在那里长大（读了盖基的书），并且我人生的大部分时间也都在那里度过。

Could we ask for a more humane beginning? It brushes aside our apprehension that this is a discipline too dry and distant for us to comprehend. Another one of John Rodgers’s articles, “The Geological History of Connecticut,” written for a journal of Yale’s Peabody Museum, began like this:

我们还能要求更人性化的开篇吗？它消除了我们对这门学科过于枯燥和遥远而难以理解的疑虑。约翰·罗杰斯为耶鲁大学皮博迪博物馆期刊撰写的另一篇文章《康涅狄格州的地质史》的开头是这样的：

Geology is the science of the earth, and what particularly characterizes it is the sense of the length of the time the earth has existed. Geologists think of the long history of the earth in terms of millions of years (units of 10 6 years), just as astronomers think of immense interstellar distances in terms of light years (units of 10 13 kilometers), and they find it convenient to divide that history into broad divisions called eras. Indeed the divisions they use are curiously like those used by historians to describe European history and can reasonably be translated as Modern, Medieval and Ancient times, plus Prehistory. (Actually they are defined in terms of the life of the times, for the relative ages of rock strata are determined principally by the fossil remains of life that they contain.) Even the proportions are not too dissimilar; as in history, each older era is longer than the next younger, and the oldest, the prehistory, dwarfs all the others in duration, although least is known about it. Connecticut, as we know it today, is the result of processes taking place through all these millions of years, and it preserves at least some record of each of the eras.

地质学是研究地球的科学，其最显著的特征在于对地球存在时间长度的感知。地质学家以百万年（10⁶ 年为单位）来思考地球漫长的历史，正如天文学家以光年（10¹³ 公里为单位）来思考浩瀚的星际距离一样。他们为了便于理解，将这段历史划分为若干个时期，称为“时代”。事实上，他们使用的划分方式与历史学家用来描述欧洲历史的划分方式非常相似，可以合理地翻译为：近代、中世纪、古代，再加上史前时期。（实际上，这些划分是根据各个时期的生物活动来定义的，因为岩层的相对年龄主要取决于其中所含的生物化石。）甚至比例也颇为相似；正如历史一样，每个较老的时代都比下一个较新的时代更长，而最古老的时代——史前时期——在持续时间上远远超过其他所有时代，尽管我们对它的了解最少。我们今天所知的康涅狄格州，是数百万年来各种进程的结果，它至少保留了每个时代的一些记录。

The process that produced the features we see in the Connecticut landscape today are processes still operating on the surface of the earth. I will pass by the plant cover—forests, pastures, lawns—and the animal inhabitants, and also man and his works, although he has already notably modified the landscape. The chief inorganic process that has shaped the hills and valleys as we see them is the work of water, especially running water, washing away the soil—eroding it—as it still does in big storm-floods, and of soil water, gradually seeping into the solid rocks beneath and converting them—weathering them, we say—into clay, mud and loam by reacting chemically with them or breaking them down physically, as when it freezes in their cracks.

康涅狄格州今日地貌特征的形成过程，至今仍在地表上持续发生。我将略过植被——森林、牧场、草坪——以及动物居民，当然也略过人类及其活动，尽管人类已经显著地改变了地貌。塑造我们所见山丘和山谷的主要无机过程是水的作用，尤其是流水，它冲刷土壤——侵蚀土壤——就像如今在暴雨洪水中依然发生的那样；还有土壤中的水分，它逐渐渗入下方的坚硬岩石，并通过化学反应或物理作用（例如在岩石缝隙中冻结）将其转化为粘土、泥土和壤土——我们称之为风化作用。

The two kinds of water work together; the soil water weakens the rocks and converts them into loose material that the running water can easily wash away, and the running water carries away the debris so prepared and thus makes it possible for the soil water to penetrate still deeper. They work unevenly; some rocks are more resistant to weathering and to erosion than others, although none are completely immune, and the resistant rocks therefore remain as hills or mountains rising above the lower lands where the rocks are weaker, like East Rock and West Rock in New Haven, the Hanging Hills of Meriden, or Talcott Mountain west of Hartford.

这两种水相互作用：土壤水削弱岩石，将其转化为易于被流水冲走的松散物质；流水带走这些松散的碎屑，从而使土壤水能够进一步渗透到更深的土壤层。它们的作用并不均衡；有些岩石比其他岩石更能抵抗风化和侵蚀，但没有一种岩石能够完全免疫。因此，那些抗风化的岩石会形成山丘或山脉，耸立在岩石较为脆弱的低洼地带之上，例如纽黑文的东岩和西岩、梅里登的悬山，以及哈特福德西部的塔尔科特山。

I like the thoughtfulness that gives me East Rock and West Rock—two framing landmarks for anyone who has ever lived in New Haven—in the midst of the scientific explanation of what caused them. No science writer should be “above” pointing to anything that relates his knowledge to our lives. Professor Rodgers continues in the next paragraph to orient his Connecticut readers:

我喜欢作者在解释东岩和西岩成因的科学解释时，巧妙地将这两处地标——对于任何在纽黑文生活过的人来说都意义非凡的地标——融入其中。任何科学作家都不应该“高高在上”，而应该指出任何与我们生活息息相关的知识。罗杰斯教授在下一段继续为他的康涅狄格州读者们介绍相关背景：

The running water runs downhill, of course, and gathers itself into watercourses, creeks and rivers, bigger and bigger downstream. Because its power to erode and especially to transport debris increases rapidly with the velocity and volume, the watercourses become valleys, and the rivers can even cut gorges through ridges of resistant rock, as the Farmington has cut through Talcott Mountain at Tariffville and the Connecticut through the highland east and southeast of Middletown on its way to Long Island Sound.

水流自然是向下流淌，汇聚成水道、溪流和河流，下游的水量越来越大。由于水流的流速和流量越大，其侵蚀能力，尤其是搬运碎屑的能力，就越发显著，水道逐渐形成山谷，河流甚至可以像法明顿河在塔里夫维尔切割塔尔科特山，以及康涅狄格河在流向长岛海峡的途中穿过米德尔敦东部和东南部的高原那样，在坚硬的岩脊上切割出峡谷。

Cenozoic or Modern time has lasted about 60 million years so far, and water has been able to weather, erode and transport a great deal of rock; during that time probably some hundreds of meters of rock has been stripped off the surface of Connecticut. The eroded material has all been transported out into the Atlantic Ocean, where it has accumulated and is still accumulating on the continental shelf and off the continental edge. Thus the shapes we see in our present landscape are all the result of this ceaseless erosion; in Connecticut we have no mountains or other landforms built up by recent volcanic activity or uplifted along earthquake faults, such as one finds in some parts of the western United States. As the Atlantic Ocean has been there throughout the Cenozoic era, the land surface of Connecticut is adjusted to its presence; the major rivers flow south or southeast, and overall the surface of the landscape slopes in the same direction, though of course highly varied in detail.

新生代或现代至今已持续约6000万年，水流侵蚀、风化并搬运了大量的岩石；在此期间，康涅狄格州地表可能已被剥蚀数百米厚的岩层。这些侵蚀物质全部被输送到大西洋，并在大陆架和大陆边缘不断堆积。因此，我们今天看到的地貌都是这种持续侵蚀的结果；康涅狄格州没有像美国西部某些地区那样，由近期火山活动堆积或沿地震断层隆起的山脉或其他地貌。由于大西洋在整个新生代时期都存在，康涅狄格州的地表也适应了它的存在；主要河流向南或东南流淌，地表整体坡度也大致相同，当然，具体细节差异很大。

How easily Professor Rodgers carries us along with his narrative, sounding erudite but not professorial, luring us into his vast time frame so painlessly that we hardly blink at the words “so far” in the statement that Cenozoic time “has lasted about 60 million years so far,” or at the “recent” volcanic activity that has given the western United States some of its contours but has spared Connecticut. What makes his writing work, of course, is that it’s well written. The English is clean, the order logical, the various steps illustrated with processes that we can visualize: the running of water, the washing away of soil. True, we visualize in infinitely speeded-up motion what it took nature millions of years to accomplish, but the feat is that we have been enabled to visualize it at all. This is the gift that good science writing can bestow in all those disciplines where the scale is so unfathomably large, like astronomy, or so unfathomably small, like cell biology and sub-atomic physics, that we can only imagine what is being described. Language is our rope ladder across the abyss.

罗杰斯教授的叙述引人入胜，他博学而不失轻松，将我们带入他那浩瀚的时间框架之中，如此自然流畅，以至于我们几乎不会注意到“迄今为止”这几个字，比如新生代“至今已持续约6000万年”，或是“近期”的火山活动塑造了美国西部的部分地貌，却使康涅狄格州幸免于难。当然，他写作成功的关键在于其精湛的文笔。英语简洁流畅，结构逻辑清晰，各个步骤都用我们能够想象的过程加以阐释：水的流动，土壤的冲刷。诚然，我们以无限加速的方式想象着自然界历经数百万年才完成的过程，但真正的奇迹在于，我们能够将其可视化。这就是优秀的科学写作所能带来的馈赠，它适用于所有那些尺度大到难以想象的学科，例如天文学，或者尺度小到难以想象的学科，在这些学科中，我们只能靠想象来描述事物。语言是我们跨越深渊的绳索梯。

One scientist who manages to simplify these immensities for me is James Trefil, a professor of physics and author (speaking of invisible phenomena) of the popular From Atoms to Quarks . To a physicist, Trefil says, “the entire world is a physics laboratory; everything we see around us operates according to a very small number of basic principles. There are Newton’s three laws that describe the motion of material objects, the three laws of thermodynamics that describe things related to heat, four of Maxwell’s equations that describe electricity and magnetism, the single principle of general relativity that describes gravity, and a few more laws (depending on which philosopher of science you talk to) for quantum mechanics, the physics of the sub-atomic world.”

詹姆斯·特雷菲尔是一位科学家，他能用浅显易懂的方式向我解释这些浩瀚的宇宙奥秘。他是物理学教授，也是畅销书《从原子到夸克》（From Atoms to Quarks）的作者（该书探讨的是那些不可见的现象）。特雷菲尔说，对物理学家而言，“整个世界就是一个物理实验室；我们周围的一切都遵循着极少数的基本原理。牛顿三大定律描述了物体的运动，热力学三大定律描述了与热相关的现象，麦克斯韦四大方程描述了电磁现象，广义相对论的基本原理描述了引力，还有一些定律（取决于你咨询的是哪位科学哲学家）描述了量子力学，也就是亚原子世界的物理学。”

Armed with these dozen-odd laws and what appears to be a magnetic attraction to the Beartooth range of the Montana Rockies, Trefil has written a book called Meditations at 10,000 Feet: A Scientist in the Mountains , in which he muses on such down-to-earth questions as the age of the ground he is hiking on, noting that “the appearance of a rock, like the appearance of a person, tells you something about the sort of life it has had.”

凭借这十几条定律，以及对蒙大拿州落基山脉熊牙山脉的某种莫名吸引力，特雷菲尔写了一本书，名为《万米高空的冥想：一位山中科学家》，书中他思考了一些实际的问题，例如他正在徒步旅行的地面的年龄，并指出“一块岩石的外观，就像一个人的外观一样，可以告诉你它经历过什么样的生命”。

Estimating the age of the earth has long been a major intellectual pastime of the learned. In the seventeenth century the Anglo-Irish bishop James Ussher, by counting up the lives in biblical genealogy, concluded that the earth had been created on Tuesday, October 26, 4004 B.C ., at nine o’clock in the morning. Later scientists used the saltiness of the ocean, the heat flow through the earth’s crust, and the rate of formation of sediments in rivers to estimate the same number. Insofar as one can identify historical themes in such widely diverse fields of study, the trend throughout the nineteenth and early twentieth century was to assign longer and longer lifespans to our planet.

估算地球年龄一直是学者们的一项重要学术研究。17世纪，英裔爱尔兰主教詹姆斯·乌舍尔（James Ussher）通过统计圣经家谱中的人物，得出结论：地球诞生于公元前4004年10月26日星期二上午9点。后来的科学家则利用海洋的盐度、地壳的热流以及河流中沉积物的形成速度来估算地球的年龄。尽管研究领域如此广泛，但历史趋势却呈现出不同的面貌：19世纪和20世纪初，人们普遍认为地球的寿命越来越长。

With the advent of radiometric dating, an important new tool was added to the equipment of those seeking to date the earth. The new technique depends on a simple premise: the earth must be at least as old as the oldest rock on its surface. If we can find a rock that is of any datable age, we can be sure that the earth must be older than that age.

随着放射性测年法的出现，为那些致力于测定地球年龄的人们增添了一项重要的工具。这项新技术基于一个简单的前提：地球的年龄至少要与地表最古老的岩石的年龄一样大。如果我们能找到一块可以测定年龄的岩石，我们就可以确定地球的年龄必定比这块岩石的年龄更大。

By 1931, at a meeting of the National Research Council in Washington, D.C., the American geologist Arthur Holmes was able to state the earth was at least 1.46 billion years old. The assertion was based on the uranium-lead dating of minerals taken from the Black Hills of South Dakota. From that time on, the location of the world’s oldest rock jumped from continent to continent, residing for short periods in the U.S.S.R., South Africa and the Congo. I was delighted to discover that for a short period in the 1960s the world’s oldest stone was a 3.1-billion-year-old zircon found in the Beartooth Mountains of Montana. It was coming to know these mountains that eventually led me to write this book.

1931年，在华盛顿特区举行的国家研究委员会会议上，美国地质学家亚瑟·霍姆斯宣布地球至少有14.6亿年的历史。这一论断是基于对南达科他州黑山地区矿物的铀铅测年法得出的。从那时起，世界上最古老岩石的所在地便在各大洲之间辗转，曾短暂地位于苏联、南非和刚果。我欣喜地发现，在20世纪60年代的一段时间里，世界上最古老的石头是一块在蒙大拿州熊牙山脉发现的、拥有31亿年历史的锆石。正是对这些山脉的了解最终促使我写下了这本书。

Notice how helpful it is to sight an occasional person amid these primordial forces: the writer himself, the geologist Arthur Holmes revealing to his presumably stunned colleagues in 1931 that the earth was at least 1.46 billion years old, and the un-named geologist who only thirty years later jumped that figure to 3.1 billion. We’re being allowed to kibitz at the scientists’ game of earth-dating—one that’s still not over:

在这些原始力量的冲击下，偶尔出现一个人是多么有益：比如作者本人，还有地质学家亚瑟·霍姆斯，他在1931年向他那些想必震惊的同事们揭示了地球至少有14.6亿年的历史，以及仅仅30年后，那位不知名的地质学家将这个数字提高到了31亿年。我们得以旁观科学家们进行的地球年代测定游戏——这场游戏至今仍未结束：

Today the world’s oldest known rocks are in a formation of twisted gray metamorphic structure on the western coast of Greenland. Dated by the rubidium-strontium method, these rocks are almost 3.8 billion years old. Since some of the rocks are clearly sedimentary in origin, this finding also indicates that the earth had oceans (or at least large bodies of water) on its surface 3.8 billion years ago.

如今，世界上已知最古老的岩石位于格陵兰岛西海岸一处扭曲的灰色变质构造中。经铷锶法测定，这些岩石的年龄已接近38亿年。由于其中一些岩石明显是沉积岩，这一发现也表明，38亿年前地球表面曾存在海洋（或至少是大片水体）。

But that still doesn’t answer the main question, Trefil says. The question is: How can we go beyond the age of the oldest known rocks to the age of the earth itself?

但特雷菲尔说，这仍然没有回答主要问题。问题是：我们如何才能超越已知最古老岩石的年龄，推算出地球本身的年龄？

Radiometric dating cannot be used to determine the age of anything that happened before the melting and differentiation of the earth. In effect, the melting reset all the geological clocks on earth. If we want to go beyond that event to the formation of the earth itself, we will have to use an indirect method of arriving at an estimate.

放射性测年法无法用于确定地球熔化和分异之前发生的任何事件的年龄。实际上，地球熔化重置了地球上所有的地质时钟。如果我们想要追溯到地球形成之前的时期，就必须采用间接方法来估算年龄。

One such estimate is based on the radiometric dating of meteorites. Both uranium-lead and rubidium-strontium measurements indicate that meteorites striking the earth were formed 4.6 billion years ago. If we believe that these meteorites represent material left over from the construction of the planets, then we say that the earth must have formed at the same time they did—4.6 billion years ago.

其中一种估算方法是基于陨石的放射性测年。铀铅法和铷锶法的测量结果均表明，撞击地球的陨石形成于46亿年前。如果我们认为这些陨石代表了行星形成过程中遗留下来的物质，那么我们就可以说地球必定是与这些陨石同时形成的——46亿年前。

A second line of inference is to look at the dating of rocks taken from the moon. Again, we find that standard techniques (primarily potassium-argon) give an age for moon rocks of about 4.6 billion years. The moon, as we know, underwent differentiation only at the surface, and solidified quickly. Consequently, geological clocks on its surface were reset much earlier than those on the earth, and their age is a much better indication of the time of the moon’s formation than are the corresponding ages for earth rocks. If you think the earth and the moon formed at the same time, you would conclude that the earth is 4.6 billion years old.

第二种推论方法是对从月球采集的岩石进行年代测定。我们发现，使用标准方法（主要是钾氩法）测得的月球岩石年龄约为46亿年。我们知道，月球的岩浆分异作用仅发生在表面，并且凝固得很快。因此，月球表面的地质钟重置的时间远早于地球，其年龄比地球岩石的相应年龄更能准确地指示月球的形成时间。如果你认为地球和月球是同时形成的，那么你就会得出地球年龄为46亿年的结论。

Enough! I have a hard enough time handling three score years and ten. Still, Professor Trefil has warmed up his narrative more than I would have thought possible. He hasn’t simply told me the story of the age of the earth; he has told me the even more amazing story of the leap in man’s ability to calculate that age—an intellectual feat that takes us from Bishop Ussher’s seventeenth-century Biblical surmise (not quite 6,000 years) to the potassium-argon dating of rocks that man has actually gone to the moon to get (4.6 billion years).

够了！光是“七十岁”这个数字就够我受的了。不过，特雷菲尔教授的叙述比我想象的还要精彩。他不仅讲述了地球的年龄，还讲述了人类计算地球年龄能力飞跃发展的惊人故事——这一智力壮举将我们从乌舍尔主教十七世纪基于圣经的推测（不足六千年）带到了人类登上月球采集岩石并进行钾氩测年的结果（四十六亿年）。

This is the human need that writing-across-the-curriculum programs will have to bear in mind in disciplines that take students far beyond the human frame of reference. We want the study of the earth, for instance, to make some connection with the time we spend inhabiting it: How should we think about it? How should we take care of it? Writers and learners will write better and learn more if they understand the “why” of what they are studying.

这就是跨学科写作项目必须牢记的人类需求，尤其是在那些将学生带入远超人类参照框架的学科领域时。例如，我们希望对地球的研究能够与我们居住于此的时间建立某种联系：我们应该如何看待地球？我们应该如何保护地球？如果写作者和学习者理解了他们所学内容的“意义”，他们就能写得更好，学得更多。

I put this problem to a group of professors at Boise State University several years ago; we were discussing how to bring writing into the science curriculum. One of them, Monte D. Wilson, professor of geology, said that he tries to expose his students to writing that is excellent both as science and as prose. I asked him if I could see some examples, and he gave me four that amply proved his point. They represented the best of both writing worlds.

几年前，我曾向博伊西州立大学的一群教授提出过这个问题；当时我们正在讨论如何将写作融入科学课程。其中一位教授，地质学教授蒙特·D·威尔逊说，他努力让学生接触既是优秀的科学文章又是优秀的散文作品。我问他能否举几个例子，他给了我四个，充分证明了他的观点。这些例子完美地融合了科学和散文两种写作风格。

The first was every inch a scientific document, complete with tables and topographic maps and published by the United States Government (Geological Survey Professional Paper 596). Entitled “The Catastrophic Late Pleistocene Bonneville Flood in the Snake River Plain, Idaho,” it was an exhaustive account by Harold E. Malde of the fieldwork that enabled him to retrace what happened when “Lake Bonneville, at one time in its early history, spilled northward at Red Rock Pass near Preston, Idaho, and suddenly released an enormous volume of water onto the Snake River Plain, leaving a vivid record of its cataclysmic passage.”

第一份报告完全是一份科学文献，包含表格和地形图，由美国政府出版（地质调查局专业论文596）。该报告题为《爱达荷州蛇河平原晚更新世灾难性的博纳维尔洪水》，是哈罗德·E·马尔德详尽记录的野外考察工作，使他得以重现“博纳维尔湖在其早期历史中，曾在爱达荷州普雷斯顿附近的红岩山口向北溢出，突然向蛇河平原倾泻了大量的水，留下了这场灾难性洪水的生动记录”。

“Hal Malde’s paper is an example of excellent professional writing,” Professor Wilson told me. “Although it was intended for professional geologists, it’s easily understood by non-scientists. Its scientific content is first-rate; in fact, it won the Geological Society of America’s award in 1970 for its contribution to the study of landforms—what we call geomorphology. His style gives you that feeling of interest that’s associated with a good story rather than the leaden feeling that’s all too often associated with a scientific treatise.” Reading it, I could only agree; although the Pleistocene Age was hardly yesterday, in Malde’s writing it almost seemed that way:

“哈尔·马尔德的论文堪称专业写作的典范，”威尔逊教授告诉我。“虽然它是为专业地质学家撰写的，但非专业人士也能轻松理解。它的科学内容一流；事实上，它因其对地貌学（我们称之为地貌学）研究的贡献，荣获了1970年美国地质学会的奖项。他的文风引人入胜，如同阅读一个精彩的故事，而非科学论文常见的枯燥乏味。”读完之后，我深表赞同；尽管更新世并非发生在昨天，但在马尔德的笔下，却仿佛就在昨天。

Boulders of sedimentary material are especially evident in the railroad pit at Mile 109 and at the upper end of the Grandview Basin, where floodwater was impounded in deep temporary lakes. The basalt boulders are typically very well rounded and obviously have been thoroughly rolled, tumbled and abraded during their passage downstream….

在109英里处的铁路坑和格兰德维尤盆地的上游，尤其可以明显看到沉积物巨石，那里洪水曾被蓄积成深邃的临时湖泊。这些玄武岩巨石通常都非常圆润，显然在向下游移动的过程中经历了彻底的滚动、翻滚和磨损……

The three other pieces were of a different order. “They’re not examples of scientific writing intended for scientists; they’re prose writings on scientific topics,” Professor Wilson explained. “The earthquake piece by John Muir, for instance, conveys his characteristic reverence for nature, but it also does a nice job of relating earthquakes to landscapes.” In fact, I can’t imagine a nicer job. This is how the great naturalist recalled the Inyo Earthquake, which struck Yosemite Valley on the night of March 26, 1872. Muir at the time was caretaker of Black’s Hotel, under Sentinel Rock.

另外三篇文章则截然不同。“它们并非面向科学家的科学论文，而是以散文形式探讨科学主题的作品，”威尔逊教授解释道。“例如，约翰·缪尔关于地震的文章，既展现了他对自然一贯的敬畏之情，又巧妙地将地震与地貌景观联系起来。” 事实上，我想不出还有比这更精彩的了。这位伟大的博物学家是这样回忆1872年3月26日晚袭击优胜美地山谷的因约地震的。当时，缪尔是哨兵岩下布莱克酒店的管理员。

In Yosemite Valley, one morning about two o’clock, I was aroused by an earthquake; and though I had never before enjoyed a storm of this sort, the strange, wild thrilling motion and rumbling could not be mistaken, and I ran out of my cabin, both glad and frightened, shouting, “A noble earthquake!” feeling sure I was going to learn something. The shocks were so violent and varied, and succeeded one another so closely, one had to balance in walking as if on the deck of a ship among the waves, and it seemed impossible the high cliffs should escape being shattered. In particular, I feared that the sheer-fronted Sentinel Rock, which rises to a height of three thousand feet, would be shaken down, and I took shelter back of a big pine, hoping I might be protected from out-bounding boulders, should any come so far. I was now convinced that an earthquake had been the maker of the taluses [in the park], and proof positive came soon enough.

在优胜美地山谷，一天清晨两点左右，我被一场地震惊醒。虽然我从未经历过如此猛烈的风暴，但那奇异、狂野、令人胆寒的震动和隆隆声却绝非错觉。我既兴奋又害怕地跑出小屋，大喊着：“一场伟大的地震！”我确信自己即将有所发现。震动如此剧烈、变化多端，而且接连不断，以至于行走时必须像在波涛汹涌的船甲板上一样保持平衡，高耸的悬崖似乎随时都会崩塌。我尤其担心高达三千英尺、正面陡峭的哨兵岩会被震落，于是我躲到一棵大松树后，希望能够抵挡住可能滚落的巨石。此时我确信，公园里的碎石坡就是地震造成的，而确凿的证据很快就出现了。

A talus is a pile of rock debris at the foot of a cliff. It’s the only geological term Muir had to use; otherwise his language has the dramatic flair of a Victorian novel. Read on:

碎石坡是指悬崖底部堆积的岩石碎屑。这是缪尔唯一需要使用的地质学术语；否则，他的语言就如同维多利亚时代的小说一般充满戏剧张力。继续阅读：

It was a calm moonlight night, and no sound was heard for the first minute or two save a low muffled underground rumbling and a slight rustling of the agitated trees, as if, in wrestling with the mountains, Nature were holding her breath. Then, suddenly, out of the strange silence and strange motion there came a tremendous roar. The Eagle Rock, a short distance up the valley, had given way, and I saw it falling in thousands of the great boulders I had been studying for so long, pouring to the valley floor in a free curve luminous from friction, making a terribly sublime and beautiful spectacle—an arc of fire fifteen hundred feet across, as true in form and as steady as a rainbow, in the midst of the stupendous roaring rock-storm. The sound was inconceivably deep and broad and earnest, as if the whole earth, like a living creature, had at last found a voice and were calling to her sister planets. It seemed to me that if all the thunder I ever heard were condensed into one roar it would not equal this rock roar at the birth of a mountain talus. Think, then, of the roar that arose to heaven when all the thousands of ancient canyon taluses throughout the length and breadth of the range were simultaneously given birth.

那是一个宁静的月夜，最初的一两分钟里，除了低沉的地下隆隆声和树木轻微的沙沙声外，一片寂静，仿佛大自然在与群山搏斗时屏住了呼吸。突然，在这奇异的寂静和奇异的动静中，传来一声震耳欲聋的轰鸣。山谷上游不远处的鹰岩崩塌了，我看到它化作数千块我研究已久的巨石，倾泻而下，在摩擦的光芒中划出一道自由的弧线，落到谷底，形成了一幅壮丽无比的景象——一道宽达一千五百英尺的火焰弧线，形状优美，稳定如彩虹，矗立在这惊天动地的岩石风暴之中。那声音深沉、宽广、真挚，难以想象，仿佛整个地球，如同一个活生生的生物，终于发出了声音，向它的姐妹星球呼唤。我觉得，即便我听过的所有雷声都汇聚成一声轰鸣，也比不上这座山体碎石坡诞生时岩石发出的咆哮。试想一下，当山脉纵横交错的数千座古老峡谷碎石坡同时诞生时，那响彻云霄的轰鸣声该是何等震撼！

Paragraphs don’t come much richer than that. The grandeur of the moment is vividly caught, yet the words are precise and relatively simple.

这段文字的精彩程度难以超越。它生动地捕捉到了那一刻的宏伟气势，同时用词精准简洁。

The main storm was soon over, and, eager to see the newborn talus, I ran up the valley in the moonlight and climbed it before the huge blocks, after their wild fiery flight, had come to complete rest. They were slowly settling into their places, chafing, grating against one another, groaning, and whispering; but no motion was visible except in a stream of small fragments pattering down the face of the cliff at the head of the talus. A cloud of dust particles, the smallest of the boulders, floated out across the whole breadth of the valley and formed a ceiling that lasted until after sunrise; and the air was loaded with the odor of crushed Douglas Spruces, from a grove that had been mowed down and mashed like weeds.

暴风雨很快就过去了，我急切地想看看新生的碎石坡，便在月光下沿着山谷奔跑，趁着那些巨大的石块在狂野的燃烧飞舞之后尚未完全静止，便爬上了碎石坡。它们正缓缓落回原位，彼此摩擦、碰撞、呻吟、低语；但除了碎石坡顶端悬崖上不断飘落的小碎片之外，看不到任何动静。一团由最小的巨石碎片组成的尘埃云飘散在整个山谷，形成了一片穹顶，一直持续到日出之后；空气中弥漫着被碾碎的花旗松的气味，那是来自一片被像杂草一样割除的树林。

Sauntering about to see what other changes had been made, I found the Indians in the middle of the valley, terribly frightened, of course, fearing that the angry spirits of the rocks were trying to kill them. The few whites wintering in the valley were assembled in front of the old Hutchings Hotel, comparing notes and meditating flight to steadier ground, seemingly as sorely frightened as the Indians. It is always interesting to see people in dead earnest, from whatever cause, and earthquakes make everybody earnest….

我四处闲逛，想看看还有哪些变化，结果发现印第安人聚集在山谷中央，他们当然吓坏了，担心岩石的愤怒精灵要杀了他们。几个在山谷里过冬的白人聚集在老哈钦斯酒店前，互相交流着情况，商量着如何逃往更安全的地方，看起来和印第安人一样惊恐万分。看到人们如此认真地对待这件事总是很有意思，不管是什么原因，而地震会让每个人都变得认真起来……

Jump forward three quarters of a century to Alan Paton’s Cry, the Beloved Country . I remember the impact that the novel made when it was published in 1948. It was the first voice to tell us of the pain of South Africa, and as a voice it was not quite like any other in its cadences and its plain strength. I knew all along that it was literature; that’s what gave it its grip on the emotions of readers all over the world. But I didn’t know that it was also good geology. “Although Cry, the Beloved Country was written almost forty years ago,” Professor Wilson told me, “it’s strikingly relevant today. The short first chapter is a beautifully written description of the importance of ecological principles to social systems.”

时光荏苒，转眼来到艾伦·佩顿的《哭泣吧，亲爱的祖国》。我至今仍记得这部小说在1948年出版时所引起的巨大反响。它是第一部向我们讲述南非苦难的作品，其独特的韵律和铿锵有力的笔触，使其与任何其他作品都截然不同。我一直都知道这是一部文学作品；正是文学的魅力，让它深深触动了世界各地读者的心弦。但我当时并不知道，它同时也是一部优秀的地理学著作。“尽管《哭泣吧，亲爱的祖国》写于近四十年前，”威尔逊教授告诉我，“但它在今天依然具有惊人的现实意义。短短的第一章就以优美的文笔，阐述了生态原则对社会系统的重要性。”

Here’s the first chapter in its entirety:

以下是第一章全文：

There is a lovely road that runs from Ixopo into the hills. These hills are grass-covered and rolling, and they are lovely beyond any singing of it. The road climbs seven miles into them, to Carisbrooke; and from there, if there is no mist, you look down on one of the fairest valleys of Africa. About you there is grass and bracken and you may hear the forlorn crying of the titihoya, one of the birds of the veld. Below you is the valley of the Umzimkulu, on its journey from the Drakensberg to the sea; and beyond and behind the river, great hill after great hill; and beyond and behind them, the mountains of Ingeli and East Griqualand.

从伊克索波 (Ixopo) 有一条美丽的公路通往山丘。这些山丘绿草茵茵，绵延起伏，美得令人窒息。公路蜿蜒向上七英里，到达卡里斯布鲁克 (Carisbrooke)；从那里，如果没有雾气，你可以俯瞰非洲最美丽的山谷之一。周围是青草和蕨类植物，你或许还能听到草原鸟儿——蒂蒂霍亚鸟 (titihoya) 凄婉的鸣叫。你的下方是乌姆齐姆库鲁河谷 (Umzimkulu Valley)，它从德拉肯斯山脉 (Drakensberg) 奔流向大海；河的彼岸，连绵起伏的群山；再往后，便是英格利 (Ingeli) 和东格里夸兰 (East Griqualand) 的山脉。

The grass is rich and matted, you cannot see the soil. It holds the rain and the mist, and they seep into the ground, feeding the streams in every kloof. It is well-tended, and not too many cattle feed upon it; not too many fires burn it, laying bare the soil. Stand unshod upon it, for the ground is holy, being even as it came from the Creator. Keep it, guard it, care for it, for it keeps men, guards men, cares for men. Destroy it and man is destroyed.

草木茂盛，密不透风，不见泥土。它蓄积雨水和雾气，渗入地下，滋养着峡谷间潺潺的溪流。这片土地有人精心照料，牲畜不多，火也少，不会轻易烧毁裸露的土壤。赤脚踏上这片土地，因为它神圣，如同造物主赐予的原貌。守护它，保护它，照料它，因为它养育人类，守护人类，关爱人类。毁掉它，人类也将随之毁灭。

Where you stand the grass is rich and matted, you cannot see the soil. But the rich green hills break down. They fall to the valley below, and falling, change their nature. For they grow red and bare; they cannot hold the rain and mist, and the streams are dry in the kloofs. Too many cattle feed upon the grass, and too many fires have burned it. Stand shod upon it, for it is coarse and sharp, and the stones cut under the feet. It is not kept, or guarded, or cared for, it no longer keeps men, guards men, cares for men. The titihoya does not cry here any more.

你脚下，青草茂盛，密不透风，不见泥土。然而，翠绿的山丘崩塌，倾泻而下，落入山谷，改变了自身的本质。它们变得赤红光秃，无法蓄留雨水和雾气，峡谷中的溪流也干涸了。太多的牲畜啃食着青草，太多的火灾焚烧了它。赤脚踩在上面，你会发现它粗糙锋利，脚下的石头会硌得脚生疼。它无人照管，无人守护，无人照料，它不再庇护人类，不再守护人类，不再关爱人类。这里再也听不到蒂蒂霍亚的啼鸣了。

The great red hills stand desolate, and the earth has torn away like flesh. The lightning flashes over them, the clouds pour down upon them, the dead streams come to life, full of the red blood of the earth. Down in the valleys women scratch the soil that is left, and the maize hardly reaches the height of a man. They are valleys of old men and old women, of mothers and children. The men are away, the young men and the girls are away. The soil cannot keep them any more.

巨大的红色山丘荒凉耸立，大地如同血肉般被撕裂。闪电划破天际，乌云倾盆而下，死寂的溪流重获新生，涌动着大地鲜红的血液。山谷里，妇女们刨挖着残存的土地，玉米长得矮小，几乎只到成年人的身高。这里是老人和老妇人、母亲和孩子的家园。男人们都已离家，年轻人和女孩们也都离开了。土地再也留不住他们了。

The fourth example was a passage from A Sand County Almanac , by the conservationist Aldo Leopold, a book that has many fans, judging by how many people have commended it to me. (For my taste it’s a little florid.) Professor Wilson told me that he often finds in Leopold’s book a helpful explanation of some phenomenon that his geology class is wrestling with. About the following passage, called “Cheat Takes Over,” he said, “My students who are out on field projects often complain about the prickly cheat grass. I ask them to read Leopold’s essay in the hope that they’ll contemplate the ecological relationships and principles that are so well expressed in it.”

第四个例子摘自自然保护主义者奥尔多·利奥波德的《沙乡年鉴》，这本书很受欢迎，从很多人向我推荐它就能看出。（就我个人而言，我觉得它有点过于华丽。）威尔逊教授告诉我，他经常在利奥波德的书中找到一些有用的解释，来解释他地质课上学生们正在研究的一些现象。关于下面这段题为“杂草入侵”的文字，他说：“我的学生们在野外考察时经常抱怨带刺的杂草。我让他们读利奥波德的这篇文章，希望他们能思考一下文中精彩阐述的生态关系和原理。”

As a fourth-generation Manhattanite, my roots deep in the cement, I had never felt the rough hand of cheat grass or even heard of it. Aldo Leopold made me realize that city dwellers are lucky not to have been visited by some of these “uninvited ecological guests.”

作为土生土长的曼哈顿人，我的根深深扎在钢筋水泥之中，我从未感受过野燕麦的刺痛，甚至从未听说过它。奥尔多·利奥波德让我意识到，城市居民很幸运，没有受到这些“不速之客”的侵扰。

Ecological stowaways began to arrive with the earliest settlements. The Swedish botanist, Peter Kalm, found most of the European weeds established in New Jersey and New York as early as 1750. They spread as rapidly as the settler’s plow could prepare a suitable seedbed.

随着最早一批定居者的到来，一些生态“偷渡者”也随之而来。瑞典植物学家彼得·卡尔姆发现，早在1750年，新泽西州和纽约州就已经出现了大部分欧洲杂草。它们蔓延的速度与定居者犁地开垦出适宜苗床的速度一样快。

Others arrived later, from the West, and found thousands of square miles of ready-made seedbed prepared by the trampling hoofs of range livestock. In such cases the spread was often so rapid as to escape recording; one simply woke up one fine spring to find the range dominated by a new weed. A notable instance was the invasion of the intermountain and northwestern foothills by downy chess or cheat grass (Bromus tectorum) .

后来，来自西部的人们也来到了这里，发现数千平方英里的土地上已经铺满了牲畜践踏而成的种子床。在这种情况下，杂草的蔓延速度往往快到难以记录；人们可能只是在一个美好的春天醒来，就发现牧场上已经长满了新的杂草。一个显著的例子是，绒毛状雀麦（Bromus tectorum）入侵了山间和西北山麓地带。

Lest you gain too optimistic an impression of this new ingredient of the melting pot, let me say that cheat is not a grass in the sense of forming a live sod. It is an annual weed of the grass family, like foxtail or crabgrass, dying each fall and reseeding that fall or the next spring. In Europe its habitat is the decaying straw of thatched roofs. The Latin word for roof is tectum , hence the label “Brome of the roofs.” A plant that can make a living on the roof of a house can also thrive on this rich but arid roof of the continent.

为了避免你对这种新加入“大熔炉”的植物抱有过高的期望，我必须说明，这种名为“羊茅”（Cheat）的植物并非传统意义上的草，它不会形成活草皮。它是一种禾本科一年生杂草，与狗尾草或马唐类似，每年秋季枯萎，并在同年秋季或来年春季重新播种。在欧洲，它的栖息地是茅草屋顶腐烂的稻草。拉丁语中“屋顶”一词为“tectum”，因此它也被称为“屋顶上的羊茅”。这种能够在屋顶上生存的植物，同样也能在这片富饶却干旱的大陆“屋顶”上茁壮成长。

Today the honey-colored hills that flank the northwestern mountains derive their hue not from the rich and useful bunchgrass and wheatgrass which once covered them, but from the inferior cheat which has replaced these native grasses. The motorist who exclaims about the flowing contours that lead his eye upward to far summits is unaware of this substitution. It does not occur to him that hills, too, cover ruined complexions with ecological face powder.

如今，环绕西北山脉的蜜色山丘，其色泽并非源自曾经覆盖其上的肥沃而有益的丛生草和麦草，而是来自取代这些本土草种的劣质野燕麦。驾车者惊叹于蜿蜒的山峦轮廓引领视线向上延伸至远方山峰，却对此浑然不知。他丝毫没有意识到，山丘也如同用生态粉底掩盖了斑驳的肤色。

The cause of the substitution is overgrazing. When the too-great herds and flocks chewed and trampled the hide off the foothills, something had to cover the raw eroding earth. Cheat did….

造成这种替代现象的原因是过度放牧。当数量过多的牲畜啃食践踏山麓的植被时，裸露的、被侵蚀的土地就必须被某种东西覆盖。而奇特就做到了……

John Muir and Aldo Leopold were among the earliest writers to alert their fellow citizens to the fact that the earth was being mistreated, thereby helping to launch the environmental movement that made “ecology” a household word in the 1960s. In fact, Muir was one of the founders of the Sierra Club. Today, such is the public awareness of the chemical agents polluting our earth, air and water that most of us routinely read geological writing that we would have shied away from a generation ago. There’s a newspaper in Colorado that I admire, for instance, called High Country News —“A Paper for People Who Care About the West”—which is devoted solely to environmental matters. Many of its articles deal with the legal and political conflicts between private and public interests that are the daily battleground of conservation. But just as many deal accessibly with subjects that fall within such formal disciplines as geology (mud slides), engineering (flood control) and meteorology (acid rain). The following article, by Ed Marston and Mary Moran, is a typically clear explanation of a geological calamity that befell the area near Redstone in the spring of 1986:

约翰·缪尔和奥尔多·利奥波德是最早一批提醒公众地球正遭受破坏的作家，他们的行动推动了环境运动的兴起，使得“生态学”在20世纪60年代成为家喻户晓的词汇。事实上，缪尔还是塞拉俱乐部的创始人之一。如今，公众对污染地球、空气和水的化学物质的认知如此之高，以至于我们大多数人都会定期阅读地质学方面的文章，而这些内容在上一代人看来或许是难以接受的。例如，我非常欣赏科罗拉多州的一份报纸——《高地新闻》（High Country News），其宗旨是“为关心西部的人们而作”，这份报纸专门关注环境问题。它的许多文章都探讨了私人利益和公共利益之间在保护工作中每天都在发生的法律和政治冲突。但同样多的文章也以通俗易懂的方式探讨了地质学（泥石流）、工程学（防洪）和气象学（酸雨）等学科领域的相关主题。以下这篇文章由埃德·马斯顿和玛丽·莫兰撰写，对1986年春季发生在雷德斯通附近地区的地质灾难进行了清晰易懂的解释：

Over the past month, western Colorado’s Muddy Creek earthslide has moved an estimated 140 million cubic yards of rock, sand and soil more than 200 feet downslope. This world-class slide, many times greater than Utah’s Thistle Slide, which drowned a town, railroad and highway in 1984, has wreaked havoc on a sparsely settled mountain hillside.

过去一个月，科罗拉多州西部穆迪溪的山体滑坡估计已将1.4亿立方码的岩石、沙子和土壤向下移动了200多英尺。这场世界级的滑坡规模是1984年犹他州蓟山体滑坡的数倍，后者曾淹没了一个城镇、铁路和公路，此次滑坡给人口稀少的山坡造成了严重破坏。

Its major effect on man’s work has been to close State Highway 133 between the Crystal River Valley and the North Fork Valley. Luckily, very few people live near the slide. But the few residents of this remote high country have suffered….

这次滑坡对人类活动的主要影响是导致连接水晶河谷和北叉谷的133号州际公路封闭。幸运的是，滑坡附近居民稀少。但居住在这片偏远高地的少数居民也遭受了损失……

Although the slide consists of three lobes, one almost a mile wide and extending two miles up the mountain, the lobes aren’t moving as solid units. On the average, the 140 million cubic yards of rock, sand and soil are moving together. But each of the lobes has its own internal stresses and strains. Fissures open here, swallowing a stream perhaps or splitting a tree in half. Elsewhere, the ground heaves and humps.

尽管滑坡体由三个滑坡体组成，其中一个滑坡体宽近一英里，向上延伸两英里，但这些滑坡体并非作为一个整体移动。平均而言，这1.4亿立方码的岩石、沙子和土壤是同时移动的。但每个滑坡体都有其自身的内部应力和应变。裂缝在这里出现，可能吞噬溪流，或者将树木劈成两半。在其他地方，地面隆起隆起。

An older state highway, which crosses the slide, presents the most graphic illustration of its effects. As you drive toward the slide from Carbondale the road abruptly ends in a crack, with pasture beyond. It is not until you get out of the car that you can see the rest of the road—a fair distance down the hill….

一条横穿滑坡地带的老旧州际公路，最直观地展现了滑坡的影响。从卡本代尔方向驱车前往滑坡地带，道路突然在一道裂缝中戛然而止，裂缝尽头是一片牧场。只有下车后才能看到道路的其余部分——它位于山下相当远的地方……

What has caused this havoc? According to Colorado’s state geologist, John Rold, the slide probably first moved 5,000 to 8,000 years ago. At that time the earth was coming out of its last ice age, and there was abundant water in the soils and flowing above ground. Many Colorado landslides date from this unstable period.

这场灾难的根源是什么？据科罗拉多州地质学家约翰·罗尔德（John Rold）称，滑坡可能最初发生在5000至8000年前。当时地球正从上一个冰河时代结束，土壤中水分充足，地表径流也很多。科罗拉多州的许多滑坡都发生在这个不稳定的时期。

The slide’s reactivation this year wasn’t a surprise, Rold says. Precipitation has been above average for five years now in western Colorado, building up moisture content in the soils….

罗尔德表示，今年滑坡再次发生并不令人意外。科罗拉多州西部地区的降水量已经连续五年高于平均水平，导致土壤水分含量增加……

Obviously—from these various passages—the earth is not as solid a place as I thought it was. But at least it’s visible; if it quakes or slides we can see it shift and try to get out of the way. Not so the sea. That’s a world so impenetrable that we can only go there through the mind of a photographer or a filmmaker, who gives us brief glimpses through the gloom, or through a writer, who uses language and scholarship to surmise what life is like on the ocean floor.

显然——从这些不同的段落来看——地球并不像我想象的那样坚实。但至少它是可见的；如果它发生地震或滑坡，我们可以看到它的移动并试图躲避。海洋则不然。那是一个如此难以接近的世界，我们只能通过摄影师或电影制作人的视角去了解它，他们透过幽暗的海洋让我们得以窥见一斑；或者通过作家，他们运用语言和学术知识来推测海底生物的样貌。

No book that I know is more eloquent about these sunken mysteries than Rachel Carson’s The Sea Around Us . Miss Carson is better known for her later classic, Silent Spring , which, by calling attention to the insidious damage that well-meant chemicals like DDT were foisting on the planet, gave the young environmental movement its biggest push in the 1960s. But in The Sea Around Us a stylist of vigor and beauty was already at work. Miss Carson was not a writer who chose the sea as her subject; she was an aquatic biologist who could write. In the following passage she brings off two feats—one scientific, the other historical. First she imagines for us a world of creatures in “the sunless sea” that is beyond our own imagining. Then she tells us the story of how scientists began to look for—and finally to receive—scraps of extraordinary information from the deep. Her story has the appeal of every story about scientists stepping into unknown territory and building on the knowledge of their predecessors. But this time the frontier is straight down:

在我所知的书中，没有哪一本比蕾切尔·卡森的《我们周围的海洋》更能雄辩地阐述这些沉没的谜团。卡森女士更为人熟知的作品是她后来的经典之作《寂静的春天》，该书揭露了诸如滴滴涕等出于好意的化学物质对地球造成的隐性破坏，为20世纪60年代新兴的环保运动注入了强劲动力。但在《我们周围的海洋》中，她已展现出一种充满活力和美感的文风。卡森女士并非一位选择海洋作为写作主题的作家；她是一位文笔出众的水生生物学家。在接下来的段落中，她完成了两项壮举——一项是科学上的，另一项是历史上的。首先，她为我们描绘了一个“不见天日的海洋”中生物的世界，一个超越我们想象的世界。然后，她讲述了科学家们如何开始寻找——并最终获得——来自深海的非凡信息的片段。她的故事具有所有科学家踏入未知领域并在前人知识基础上不断探索的故事的魅力。但这一次，边界线是垂直向下的：

Between the sunlit surface waters of the open sea and the hidden hills and valleys of the ocean floor lies the least known region of the sea. These deep, dark waters, with all their mysteries and their unsolved problems, cover a very considerable part of the earth. The whole world ocean extends over about three fourths of the surface of the globe. If we subtract the shallow areas of the continental shelves and the scattered banks and shoals, where at least the pale ghost of sunlight moves over the underlying bottom, there still remains about half the earth that is covered by miles-deep, lightless water, that has been dark since the world began.

在阳光普照的开阔海面和幽深的海底山丘之间，隐藏着海洋中最不为人知的区域。这片深邃黑暗的水域，充满了神秘和未解之谜，覆盖了地球相当大的面积。整个世界海洋覆盖了地球表面约四分之三的面积。即使我们减去大陆架的浅水区和零星分布的浅滩，那里至少还能看到一丝微弱的阳光掠过海底，地球表面仍然有大约一半的面积被深达数英里、漆黑一片的海水覆盖，自世界诞生以来，这片海水就一直处于黑暗之中。

This region has held its secrets more obstinately than any other. Man, with all his ingenuity, has been able to venture only to its threshold. Wearing a diving helmet, he can walk on the ocean floor about 10 fathoms down. He can descend to an extreme limit of about 500 feet in a complete diving suit, so heavily armored that movement is almost impossible, carrying with him a constant supply of oxygen. Only two men in all the history of the world have had the experience of descending, alive, beyond the range of visible light. These men were William Beebe and Otis Barton. In the bathysphere, they reached a depth of 3028 feet in the open ocean off Bermuda, in the year 1934. Barton alone, in a steel sphere known as the benthoscope, descended to the great depth of 4500 feet off California, in the summer of 1949.

这片区域比其他任何地方都更顽固地保守着它的秘密。人类凭借其全部的智慧，也只能冒险涉足其边缘。戴上潜水头盔，他可以在大约10英寻（约16米）深的海底行走。穿着全套潜水服，这些潜水服的防护极其严密，几乎无法行动，并且需要持续供氧，他可以下潜到大约500英尺（约150米）的极限深度。纵观世界历史，只有两个人曾活着下潜到可见光范围之外。他们是威廉·比比和奥蒂斯·巴顿。1934年，他们乘坐深海潜水器在百慕大附近的开阔海域下潜到3028英尺（约910米）的深度。1949年夏天，巴顿独自一人乘坐被称为“深海听器”的钢球，在加利福尼亚附近下潜到4500英尺（约1370米）的深海。

Although only a fortunate few can ever visit the deep sea, the precise instruments of the oceanographer, recording light penetration, pressure, salinity and temperature, have given us the materials with which to reconstruct in imagination these eerie, forbidding regions. Unlike the surface waters, which are sensitive to every gust of wind, which know day and night, respond to the pull of sun and moon, and change as the seasons change, the deep waters are a place where change comes slowly, if at all. Down beyond the reach of the sun’s rays there is no alternation of light and darkness. There is rather an unending night, as old as the sea itself. For most of its creatures, groping their way endlessly through its black waters, it must be a place of hunger, where food is scarce and hard to find, a shelterless place where there is no sanctuary from ever-present enemies, where one can only move on and on, from birth to death, through an endless night, confined as in a prison to his own particular layer of the sea.

尽管只有极少数幸运儿才能踏足深海，但海洋学家们精密的仪器，记录着光线穿透、压力、盐度和温度等数据，为我们提供了丰富的素材，让我们得以在想象中重构这些神秘而险恶的区域。与对每一阵风都敏感、分明昼夜、受日月引力影响、随季节更迭而变化的表层水域不同，深海是一个变化缓慢甚至停滞的地方。在阳光无法触及的深处，没有光与暗的交替。那里只有永无止境的黑夜，与海洋本身一样古老。对于大多数在漆黑的海水中摸索前行的生物来说，那里一定是饥饿之地，食物稀少且难以寻觅；那里没有庇护所，没有可以躲避无处不在的敌人的庇护，只能在无尽的黑夜中不停地游荡，从出生到死亡，如同被囚禁在自己所处的海洋深处一般。

They used to say that nothing could live in the deep sea. It was a belief that must have been easy to accept, for without proof to the contrary, how could anyone conceive of life in such a place?

人们过去常说深海里不可能有生物生存。这种说法很容易被接受，因为在没有相反证据的情况下，谁又能想象生命会在那样的地方存在呢？

A century ago the British biologist Edward Forbes wrote: “As we descend deeper and deeper into this region, the inhabitants become more and more modified, and fewer and fewer, indicating our approach to an abyss where life is either extinguished, or exhibits but a few sparks of its lingering presence.” Yet Forbes urged further exploration of “this vast deep-sea region” to settle forever the question of the existence of life at great depths.

一个世纪前，英国生物学家爱德华·福布斯写道：“随着我们不断下潜到这个区域深处，这里的生物变得越来越怪异，数量也越来越少，这表明我们正接近一个深渊，在那里，生命要么已经灭绝，要么只剩下些许残存的火花。”然而，福布斯仍然敦促人们进一步探索“这片广袤的深海区域”，以彻底解决深海是否存在生命的问题。

Even then the evidence was accumulating. Sir John Ross, during his exploration of the arctic seas in 1818, had brought up from a depth of 1000 fathoms mud in which there were worms, “thus proving there was animal life in the bed of the ocean notwithstanding the darkness, stillness, silence and immense pressure produced by more than a mile of superincumbent water.”

即使在那时，证据也在不断积累。约翰·罗斯爵士在 1818 年探索北极海域时，从 1000 英寻深处打捞出含有蠕虫的泥浆，“从而证明，尽管海底黑暗、静谧、寂静，且被超过一英里厚的海水压得喘不过气来，但海底仍然存在动物生命。”

Then from the surveying ship Bulldog , examining a proposed northern route for a cable from Faroe to Labrador in 1860, came another report. The Bulldog’s sounding line, which at one place had been allowed to lie for some time on the bottom at a depth of 1260 fathoms, came up with thirteen starfish clinging to it. Through these starfish, the ship’s naturalist wrote, “the deep has sent forth the long coveted message.” But not all the zoologists of the day were prepared to accept the message. Some doubters asserted that the starfish had “convulsively embraced” the line somewhere on the way back to the surface.

1860年，勘测船“斗牛犬号”（Bulldog）正在勘测一条拟建的从法罗群岛到拉布拉多的北部海底电缆线路，随后传来另一份报告。“斗牛犬号”的测深绳在1260英寻（约2000米）的深处沉睡了一段时间后，浮出水面时，上面附着着13只海星。船上的博物学家写道，通过这些海星，“深海传递了人们期盼已久的信息”。但并非所有当时的动物学家都愿意接受这一信息。一些怀疑者断言，这些海星是在绳子返回水面的过程中“猛烈地缠绕”住它的。

By quoting the ship’s naturalist and his wonderful phrase about the long coveted message, Miss Carson keeps herself in the story, notifying us that her interest is more than scientific. As a historian she has obviously buried herself in the logs and journals of the men who sailed on the Bulldog , looking for the human element that every writer needs to bring a scientific achievement to life. She also gives us a strong sense of elapsing time, reminding us of the sequential nature of scientific progress. The next two paragraphs have the cumulative thrill of discovery:

卡森小姐引用船上博物学家关于那条人们期盼已久的信息的精彩描述，使她始终置身于故事之中，并暗示我们她的兴趣远不止于科学层面。作为一名历史学家，她显然深入研究了“斗牛犬号”船员的航海日志和日记，寻找每位作家都需要的、能够赋予科学成就以生命力的人性元素。她也让我们强烈感受到时间的流逝，提醒我们科学进步是一个循序渐进的过程。接下来的两段文字充满了发现的激动人心：

In the same year, 1860, a cable in the Mediterranean was raised for repairs from a depth of 1200 fathoms. It was found to be heavily encrusted with corals and other sessile animals that had attached themselves at an early stage of development and grown to maturity over a period of months or years.
