There was not the slightest chance that they had become entangled in the cable as it was being raised to the surface.

同年，即1860年，地中海一条海底电缆从1200英寻深处被打捞上来维修。人们发现电缆上密布着珊瑚和其他固着生物，这些生物在发育早期就附着在电缆上，经过数月甚至数年的生长才最终成熟。因此，它们绝不可能在电缆被打捞上来的过程中缠绕住电缆。

Then the Challenger set out from Portsmouth in the year 1872 and traced a course around the globe. From bottoms lying under miles of water, from silent deeps carpeted with red clay ooze, and from all the lightless intermediate depths, net-haul after net-haul of strange and fantastic creatures came up and were spilled out on the decks. Poring over the weird beings thus brought up for the first time into the light of day, beings no man had ever seen before, the Challenger scientists realized that life existed even on the deepest floor of the abyss.

1872年，挑战者号从朴茨茅斯启航，开始了环球航行。从深不见底的海底，从覆盖着红色黏土的寂静深渊，到所有黑暗的中间深度，一网又一网地捕获着奇异的生物，倾泻在甲板上。挑战者号的科学家们仔细观察着这些首次被带到阳光下的怪异生物，这些生物此前从未被人类见过。他们意识到，即使在深渊的最深处，生命依然存在。

The ultimate frontier, of course, is what I’ll call the sky, using that simple word to hold at bay the terrors of infinite space. It’s no fun to think about infinity and no cinch to write about it. Again, it helps to look for some human link, and, again, I’ll take an example from Meditations at 10,000 Feet , by James Trefil, who, when last heard from in this chapter, had given us the hardly comforting news that the earth is 4.6 billion years old. Here he describes how an American astronomer earlier in this century discovered that the Milky Way was only a fragment of a much larger story.

当然，最终的疆界，我姑且称之为天空，用这个简单的词来抵挡无限空间带来的恐惧。思考无限并非易事，而要描述它更是难上加难。再次强调，寻找一些与人类相关的联系会有所帮助。我将再次引用詹姆斯·特雷菲尔的《万尺沉思录》中的一个例子。在本章中，他上次出现时，给我们带来了一个令人不安的消息：地球已有46亿年的历史。而在这本书中，他描述了本世纪初一位美国天文学家如何发现银河系只是一个更大故事的碎片。

The best place to start is to recall why it is that telescopes are located on mountaintops. The purpose of a telescope is to gather light that has been emitted by distant sources. By analyzing this light we learn about the emitting object, whether that object is a nearby ship, a neighboring planet or a galaxy at the edge of the observable universe. Sometimes this knowledge is rather straightforward—we learn the size and shape of the thing being studied, more or less as we would by looking at it with our naked eye. In other cases we subject the incoming light to a more sophisticated analysis and determine facts about the objects such as temperature and chemical composition. But no matter what type of analysis we do, we are limited by the amount of light available to our instrument.

最好的切入点是回顾一下为什么望远镜要建在山顶上。望远镜的作用是收集来自遥远光源的光。通过分析这些光，我们可以了解发出光的物体，无论是附近的飞船、邻近的行星，还是位于可观测宇宙边缘的星系。有时，这种了解相当直接——我们能知道被研究物体的大小和形状，这和我们用肉眼观察差不多。而在其他情况下，我们需要对入射光进行更复杂的分析，从而确定物体的温度和化学成分等信息。但无论我们进行何种分析，都受限于仪器接收到的光量。

We normally think of the earth’s atmosphere as being completely transparent, for we can often see things a surprising distance away…. From such everyday experiences we conclude that light can easily be transmitted through a thickness of atmosphere ranging up to 100 miles. We also know that the earth’s atmosphere forms a fairly thin layer around our planet. “Outer space” is generally reckoned to start at an altitude around 50,000 feet—roughly ten miles. This means that light entering the atmosphere has to travel at most ten miles to get to the surface. Why, then, do we go to the trouble of building roads to the tops of mountains to put our telescopes a few miles closer to the source of light? Wouldn’t a telescope function just as well at sea level?

我们通常认为地球大气层是完全透明的，因为我们经常能看到很远的物体……从这些日常经验中，我们得出结论：光线可以轻易穿过厚度达100英里的大气层。我们也知道，地球大气层在地球周围形成了一个相当薄的层。“外太空”通常被认为从大约50,000英尺（约15,000米）的高度开始——大约10英里（约16公里）。这意味着进入大气层的光线最多只需传播10英里（约16公里）就能到达地表。那么，我们为什么还要费尽心思修建道路通往山顶，只为了让望远镜离光源更近几英里呢？望远镜在海平面上难道不能同样有效地工作吗？

The answer depends on what we want to study. If we want to look at a relatively bright, nearby object, sea-level telescopes will work perfectly well. Galileo saw spots on the sun and mountains on the moon from his balcony in Florence, and the planets Neptune and Uranus were discovered by telescopes located on the ground near major European cities (Berlin and London). Even today the study of the positions of nearby stars (a field known as astrometry) is carried out with such telescopes, one of which is in downtown Pittsburgh. The accurate determination of the position of nearby stars has great practical importance, since it is by sightings of such stars that satellites are navigated. Nevertheless such studies do not occupy the main attention of professional astronomers.

答案取决于我们想要研究什么。如果我们想观测一个相对明亮且距离较近的天体，海平面望远镜就完全足够了。伽利略在佛罗伦萨的阳台上观测到了太阳上的黑子和月球上的山脉，而海王星和天王星则是通过架设在欧洲主要城市（柏林和伦敦）附近的地面望远镜发现的。即使在今天，人们仍然使用这类望远镜来研究附近恒星的位置（这一领域被称为天体测量学），其中一台就位于匹兹堡市中心。精确测定附近恒星的位置具有重要的实际意义，因为卫星的导航正是依靠对这些恒星的观测。然而，这类研究并非专业天文学家关注的重点。

A much more likely target for a telescope being used in frontier research is a distant faint object, be it star, galaxy or interstellar cloud. Since the mid-nineteenth century, astronomers have not been content with finding out where objects are in the sky; they have moved on to asking what the objects are. Answering this sort of question requires a sophisticated analysis of incoming light….

对于用于前沿研究的望远镜而言，更可能的目标是遥远而暗淡的天体，无论是恒星、星系还是星际云。自19世纪中叶以来，天文学家不再满足于确定天体在天空中的位置；他们开始探究这些天体究竟是什么。回答这类问题需要对入射光进行复杂的分析……

Such sophistication can’t be achieved at ground level, Trefil points out, because of “light pollution” from cities, because of the greater density and distortion of the atmosphere at lower altitudes, and because “if an object is very distant from the earth it is likely to appear quite small, regardless of its true size,” its light almost too faint to be analyzed. Hence the flight to the mountaintops.

特雷菲尔指出，这种精细的观测在地面上是无法实现的，原因在于城市的“光污染”、低空大气密度更大、扭曲现象更严重，以及“如果一个物体距离地球非常远，无论其真实大小如何，它看起来都很小”，其光线几乎微弱到无法分析。因此，人们选择飞到山顶进行观测。

The beginning of twentieth-century astronomy can be traced to the installation of a 100-inch telescope on top of Mount Wilson near Los Angeles in the early 1920s. Edwin Hubble, using the unprecedented resolving power of his new instrument, was able to establish that our Milky Way was only one of a large number of galaxies in the universe. The technique he used was simple, at least in principle.

二十世纪天文学的开端可以追溯到20世纪20年代初，当时在洛杉矶附近的威尔逊山上安装了一台100英寸的望远镜。埃德温·哈勃利用这台新仪器前所未有的分辨率，证实了我们的银河系只是宇宙中众多星系之一。他使用的技术，至少在原理上来说，非常简单。

A certain class of stars known as Cepheid variables grow alternately bright and dim over periods of weeks or months. By examining such stars in the neighborhood of the earth, it had been established that the time it took each star to go through one of its cycles depended on how much total light it emitted. This means that if you measure the amount from the variable star light that falls on a telescope you can tell how far away it is. If the star appears faint while its period indicates that it is actually very bright, you conclude that it must be far away. Similarly, if it appears bright but its period indicates that it must be faint, it must be close by.

有一类被称为造父变星的恒星，其亮度会在数周或数月内交替变化。通过观测地球附近的这类恒星，人们发现每颗恒星完成一个周期所需的时间取决于其发出的总光量。这意味着，如果你测量射向变星的望远镜所接收到的光量，就可以判断它的距离。如果一颗恒星看起来很暗，但根据其周期判断，它实际上非常明亮，那么它一定距离很远。同样地，如果它看起来很亮，但根据其周期判断，它实际上很暗，那么它一定距离很近。

Because Hubble could actually pick out individual stars in the Andromeda Nebula he was able to establish that its distance from the earth was over 200 million light-years. Contrasting this 200 million to the greatest distance between stars in the Milky Way—a “mere” 100,000 light-years—Hubble argued that the collection of stars in the Andromeda Nebula constituted an “island universe” like our own. Overnight, the horizons of astronomy expanded from the study of a single galaxy to the study of the collection of billions of galaxies that make up our universe.

由于哈勃能够清晰地分辨出仙女座星云中的单个恒星，他得以确定仙女座星云距离地球超过2亿光年。将这2亿光年与银河系中恒星间最大距离——“仅仅”10万光年——进行对比，哈勃认为仙女座星云中的恒星群构成了一个类似我们宇宙的“孤岛宇宙”。一夜之间，天文学的视野从研究单个星系扩展到研究构成我们宇宙的数十亿个星系。

Hubble’s discovery, with its immense implications for the place of mankind in the universe, depended on his ability to make out a single star in a galaxy hundreds of millions of light-years away. This is a familiar pattern in the history of science; the greatest intellectual advances often depend on our ability to deal with the grubby details of instrumentation.

哈勃的发现意义深远，它关乎人类在宇宙中的地位，而这一切都取决于他能否分辨出数亿光年之外星系中的一颗恒星。这在科学史上是一个常见的模式：最伟大的智力进步往往取决于我们处理仪器操作中繁琐细节的能力。

# ↩

7. Art and Artists

7. 艺术与艺术家

I’m often surprised by the art I see in the homes of highly literate people. The books so carefully arrayed on their book-shelves reveal them to be men and women of knowledge and taste. But the painters hanging on their walls are the equivalent of writers they wouldn’t be caught dead reading—Danielle Steel, say, or Kahlil Gibran. Obviously visual literacy isn’t as important to them as verbal literacy. Or maybe they think that because art is all around them they don’t need to make an effort to learn about it—the kind of effort they made with all those books. But art is a language that has to be studied like any other language.

我常常对那些文化程度很高的人家中的艺术收藏感到惊讶。他们书架上精心摆放的书籍表明他们学识渊博、品味高雅。但挂在墙上的画作，却像是他们宁愿死也不会去读的作家——比如丹妮尔·斯蒂尔或纪伯伦。显然，对他们来说，视觉素养远不如语言素养重要。或许他们认为，既然艺术无处不在，就无需像学习那些书籍那样，费心去了解它。但艺术也是一种语言，需要像学习其他语言一样去学习。

I don’t mean to suggest that a visitor entering my apartment will think he has stumbled into the National Gallery by mistake. If the art on its walls and its shelves is more than ordinarily interesting it’s because my wife has done her best to educate me and because we have looked at art for many years in many parts of the world. Still, I feel that I’m only slightly more visually literate than the next man. Whenever I listen to an artist or an art historian I’m struck by how much they see and how much they know —and how much I don’t.

我并非暗示来访者会误以为自己走进了国家美术馆。如果说我家墙上和架子上的艺术品比一般人更有意思，那是因为我妻子尽力教我艺术，也因为我们多年来在世界各地欣赏过许多艺术作品。即便如此，我仍然觉得自己的视觉素养只比别人略高一些。每当我聆听艺术家或艺术史学家的讲解时，我都会惊叹于他们眼光之广、知识之渊博——以及我自身的无知。

Good art writing should therefore do at least two things. It should teach us how to look: at art, architecture, sculpture, photography and all the other visual components of our daily landscape. And it should give us the information we need to understand what we’re looking at.

因此，好的艺术评论至少应该做到两点。它应该教会我们如何观察：艺术、建筑、雕塑、摄影以及我们日常生活中所有其他视觉元素。它还应该提供我们理解所见之物所需的信息。

One teacher who had this capacity was George Nelson, the American designer whose many gifts to urban man include the pedestrian mall—the city street that’s closed to cars. Nelson spent much of his fifty-year career with the Herman Miller company, designing the innovative office products that gave the firm much of its renown. I met him once, briefly, in the mid-1960s, when I was assigned to write a magazine article about a bold new system of office furniture he had created. I had never heard of him and knew nothing of the reverence in which he was held by the design world, but I have never forgotten the playfulness of his mind. I also remember how important he felt good writing was. After that, right up to his death in 1986, whenever I saw one of his articles I realized that part of his enormous influence came from his ability to present visual ideas with clarity, humanity and humor.

乔治·尼尔森就是这样一位拥有这种能力的老师。这位美国设计师为都市人做出了诸多贡献，其中包括步行街——禁止车辆通行的城市街道。尼尔森在赫曼·米勒公司工作了五十年，期间设计了许多创新办公产品，为公司赢得了极高的声誉。我曾在20世纪60年代中期与他有过一次短暂的会面。当时我受命撰写一篇关于他设计的一套大胆创新的办公家具系统的杂志文章。在此之前，我从未听说过他，也完全不了解他在设计界所受到的崇敬，但我始终铭记着他那充满趣味的思维。我还记得他非常重视优秀的写作。此后，直到1986年他去世，每当我看到他的文章，我都会意识到，他之所以拥有如此巨大的影响力，部分原因在于他能够以清晰、人性化和幽默的方式呈现视觉理念。

Here’s a passage from his lively book How to See:

以下摘自他生动有趣的著作《如何去看》：

Visual decoding takes place at a great variety of levels, and in this sense it is not basically different from the use of any language. When the Lone Ranger and his faithful Tonto stop at some scuff marks in the desert and conclude that a band of outlaws has passed that way, carrying a ravishing blond captive on a strawberry roan, and that the leader’s horse had recently thrown a shoe, we marvel at their skill in getting so much information out of some disturbed earth. What these two would do if confronted by Picasso’s Guernica is another question. Reading a painting takes another set of skills….

视觉解码发生在各种不同的层面，从这个意义上讲，它与任何语言的使用并无本质区别。当独行侠和他的忠犬汤托在沙漠中看到一些擦痕，并推断出曾有一伙不法之徒骑着一匹草莓色的马，带着一位美艳的金发俘虏经过此地，而且头目的马蹄铁刚刚脱落时，我们不禁惊叹于他们竟能从一片被扰动的泥土中获取如此丰富的信息。如果他们面对的是毕加索的《格尔尼卡》，又会作何反应呢？这又是另一个问题了。解读一幅画作需要另一套截然不同的技能……

In visual reading, like verbal reading, the completeness of the reading relates directly to the quality of the reader’s stored information. A cat may look at a king, as the old saying goes, but the visual message is more interesting if the onlooker also knows what a king is. Visual communication, therefore, is not unlike other kinds of communication in that it is broadcast and received and in that it uses a code of language which has to be intelligible to the receiver.

视觉阅读与语言阅读一样，阅读的完整性直接取决于读者已存储信息的质量。正如古语所说，“猫看国王，如果知道国王是什么，那视觉信息就会更有趣”。因此，视觉交流与其他交流方式并无二致，它同样需要传播和接收，并且都使用一种必须能够被接收者理解的语言代码。

This becomes instantly apparent when we turn to modern painting. In the art of the nineteenth century and earlier, a painting was invariably a picture of something. You could look at it and see that the subject was a dog or a family group, a still life, a landscape. At the popular level of viewing, identifying the subject and perhaps the sentiment was sufficient. In this sense traditional painting is not unlike what we get on a TV screen: a story illustrated by photographic images. If the police are chasing the villain, we see cars screaming around curves, going off cliffs; gunplay; and the inevitable finale….

当我们转向现代绘画时，这一点便显而易见。在十九世纪及更早的艺术中，绘画总是描绘某个事物。你可以一眼看出画中描绘的是狗、一家人、静物或风景。在大众层面，识别出主题，或许还能感受到某种情感，就足以理解了。从这个意义上讲，传统绘画与我们在电视屏幕上看到的并无二致：用图像来讲述故事。如果警察在追捕罪犯，我们就会看到汽车在弯道上呼啸而过，冲下悬崖；枪战；以及不可避免的结局……

It is when subject matter, perspective and other familiar elements in painting disappear, as in modern painting, that the absence of nonverbal comprehension comes out into the open. Why does a museum show a cluster of four aluminum boxes as art? What gives value of any kind to a painting which is nothing more than a white or black surface? Léger’s people look like boilers: where has he seen such people? Why do the Cubists chop up guitars, tables, newspapers and bottles and put them back together all wrong? The usual responses, going back at least sixty years to the New York Armory Show, are that the artists are crazy; it is fairly standard for people to react to newness with nervous hostility. It is also possible, however, that the artists are sane and that the world they are painting is crazy.

当绘画中的主题、视角和其他熟悉的元素消失时，例如在现代绘画中，非语言理解的缺失便暴露无遗。为什么博物馆会把四个铝盒堆砌在一起当作艺术品展出？一幅画作，如果仅仅是黑白两色的表面，又有什么价值可言？莱热笔下的人物看起来像锅炉：他究竟在哪里见过这样的人？为什么立体主义者要把吉他、桌子、报纸和瓶子切割成碎片，然后再胡乱地拼凑起来？通常的反应，至少可以追溯到六十年前的纽约军械库展览，是认为这些艺术家疯了；人们对新事物抱有紧张的敌意，这几乎是人之常情。然而，也可能是艺术家们是理智的，而他们所描绘的世界才是疯狂的。

This is enjoyable stuff, lighthearted in tone but serious in its ideas. I especially like the sentence about the cat looking at a king. Like a well-constructed joke, it makes its point at the end and thereby takes us by surprise—always a tonic in writing. It reminds me of a sentence in Walden , by that underestimated humorist Henry David Thoreau: “The cart before the horse is neither beautiful nor useful.” Thoreau was complaining about people who don’t present their facts in logical order. Nelson was saying that nobody can understand art unless he brings to it certain necessary information.

这篇文章读起来很轻松愉快，语气轻松诙谐，但思想却很深刻。我尤其喜欢那句关于猫注视国王的句子。它就像一个精心设计的笑话，在结尾处点明主题，出人意料——这在写作中总是一种妙招。这让我想起了被低估的幽默作家亨利·大卫·梭罗在《瓦尔登湖》中的一句话：“本末倒置既不美观也不实用。”梭罗是在抱怨人们不按逻辑顺序陈述事实。而纳尔逊则是在说，除非具备某些必要的知识，否则没有人能够真正理解艺术。

Also notice how Nelson anchors his writing in specific detail. He doesn’t talk about “Cubism”; he talks about “the Cubists”—real people—and how they broke various conventions to create the ism. He makes us see paintings by Picasso and Braque and Leger; if we don’t know the actual paintings, we still get the point of what the Cubists did. We have been given a picture.

还要注意纳尔逊是如何将他的写作锚定在具体细节上的。他不谈论“立体主义”，而是谈论“立体主义者”——真实的人物——以及他们如何打破各种常规，创造出这种主义。他让我们看到毕加索、布拉克和莱热的画作；即使我们不认识这些画作本身，我们仍然能够理解立体主义者的创作理念。他为我们呈现了一幅画面。

Today the most consistently graceful writer about art, at least for my money—the cost of buying the daily and Sunday New York Times —is that paper’s art critic John Russell. A broadly educated man, he wears his erudition lightly. I never think of him as a scholar assaulting me with how much he knows, but as a teacher eager to share a lifelong passion for his subject. The following passage is the introduction to his book Meanings of Modern Art . It starts with deceptive simplicity—in fact, with sixteen consecutive one-syllable words, perhaps the world record for an art historian. But before it’s over we have been taken on a trip of remarkable range and subtlety.

如今，在我看来，最文笔优美、文采斐然的艺术评论家当属《纽约时报》的艺术评论家约翰·罗素。他学识渊博，却从不炫耀自己的学识。我从不觉得他是一位故作高深的学者，而是一位乐于分享他对艺术毕生热爱的老师。以下这段文字摘自他的著作《现代艺术的意义》的引言。开头看似简洁，实则不然——事实上，它由十六个连续的单音节词组成，这或许是艺术史学家写作的“世界纪录”。然而，读完之后，我们却已踏上了一段视野开阔、意蕴深远的艺术之旅。

When art is made new, we are made new with it. We have a sense of solidarity with our own time, and of psychic energies shared and redoubled, which is just about the most satisfying thing that life has to offer. “If that is possible,” we say to ourselves, “then everything is possible”; a new phase in the history of human awareness has been opened up, just as it was opened up when people first read Dante, or first heard Bach’s 48 preludes and fugues, or first learned from Hamlet and King Lear that the complexities and contradictions of human nature could be spelled out on the stage.

当艺术焕然一新时，我们也随之焕然一新。我们与所处的时代产生一种共鸣，一种精神能量的共享与加倍，这几乎是人生所能提供的最令人满足的事物。“如果这都可能，”我们对自己说，“那么一切皆有可能”；人类意识史的一个新阶段已经开启，正如人们第一次阅读但丁，第一次聆听巴赫的48首前奏曲与赋格曲，或者第一次从《哈姆雷特》和《李尔王》中领悟到人性的复杂性和矛盾性可以在舞台上得到淋漓尽致地展现时一样。

This being so, it is a great exasperation to come face to face with new art and not make anything of it. Stared down by something that we don’t like, don’t understand and can’t believe in, we feel personally affronted, as if our identity as reasonably alert and responsive human beings had been called into question. We ought to be having a good time, and we aren’t. More than that, an important part of life is being with-held from us; for if any one thing is certain in this world it is that art is there to help us live, and for no other reason.

正因如此，面对新艺术作品却无动于衷，实在令人恼火。面对我们不喜欢、不理解、也无法相信的事物，我们感到受到了冒犯，仿佛我们作为理性敏锐、反应灵敏的人类的身份受到了质疑。我们本应从中获得乐趣，却并非如此。更重要的是，我们失去了生活中重要的一部分；因为如果说这世上有什么是确定无疑的，那就是艺术的存在是为了帮助我们更好地生活，除此之外别无其他。

Note how quickly Russell establishes rapport with his readers. He knows how stupid we feel in the presence of art we can’t fathom, how terrible we feel to be left out. Feeling left out is one of the oldest and worst ways of feeling terrible, as every child knows who remains unchosen after the rite of “choosing up sides” or who is sent to play right field, that Siberia of childhood baseball, where (with luck) no ball will be hit. Russell assures us that we’re not jerks. Trust me, he says, I’m one of you. Of course he’s not—he’s much brighter, and we want him to be. But we’re also glad he knows how it feels to be one of us.

注意罗素是如何迅速与读者建立起融洽关系的。他深知，面对我们无法理解的艺术作品，我们会感到多么愚蠢；被排除在外，我们会感到多么难受。被排除在外是最古老、最痛苦的感受之一，每个孩子都知道，在“选边站”的仪式之后，谁会被落下，谁会被派去打右外野——那是童年棒球的“西伯利亚”，在那里（如果幸运的话）一个球都打不到。罗素向我们保证，我们不是混蛋。他说，相信我，我和你们一样。当然，他不是——他比我们聪明得多，我们也希望他是。但我们也很高兴他能体会到作为我们中一员的感受。

Continuing, Russell writes that “for hundreds of years, and on many matters of supreme importance, art had the edge over all other sources.”

罗素继续写道：“数百年来，在许多至关重要的问题上，艺术都比所有其他来源更有优势。”

It gave out the truth about this world and the next one. It encapsulated history. It told us what people wiser than ourselves were thinking. It told the stories that everyone wanted to hear…answered the great riddles, filled in the gaps in our general knowledge, and laid Eternity on the line. Above all, it gave reassurance; it told us what we wanted to hear—that experience was not formless and illegible, that man could speak to man without the obstructions of language.

它揭示了今世来世的真相，浓缩了历史，告诉我们比我们更有智慧的人在想什么。它讲述了每个人都想听的故事……解答了伟大的谜题，填补了我们知识的空白，并将永恒置于一线。最重要的是，它给予我们安慰；它告诉我们想听的话——经验并非无形无迹，人与人之间可以超越语言的障碍进行交流。

Art restored to us the lost wholeness, the sensation of being at one with Nature, and at one with society, which we crave from the moment of birth…. So we are quite right to be dismayed when art seems to shift its ground in ways that we find difficult to follow. Still less do we like to think that art might one day peter out. We should prefer to think—and in my opinion we are quite right to think—that the masterpieces of our own day can perfectly well stand comparison with the great achievements of the past.

艺术为我们恢复了失去的完整性，恢复了我们自出生之日起就渴望的与自然、与社会融为一体的感觉……因此，当艺术似乎以我们难以理解的方式改变其发展方向时，我们感到沮丧是完全合理的。我们更不愿相信艺术终有一天会消亡。我们应该相信——而且我认为我们完全有理由相信——我们这个时代的杰作完全可以与过去的伟大成就相媲美。

But the anxiety remains, Russell writes, because art has gradually altered its purpose and recoded its messages.

但罗素写道，这种焦虑依然存在，因为艺术逐渐改变了其目的，并重新编码了其信息。

It was in the second half of the nineteenth century that art was relieved of certain of the duties which it had been carrying out on society’s behalf and became free to look into its own nature. The duties in question had been many and varied. Philip IV of Spain never doubted that when his troops won a famous victory his court painter Velásquez was the best man to commemorate it. When Marat was murdered in his bath in 1793, it was by popular demand, almost, that Jacques-Louis David made haste to paint Marat Assassinated . When the Houses of Parliament burned down in 1834, art gave us our most memorable account of what happened: J.M.W. Turner was on hand to tell how the great scarf of flame unwound itself high in the night sky. Art had no rival on such occasions. It gave us what we could get nowhere else. Nor was the artist simply a passive recorder: when the French frigate Meduse was lost in particularly ghastly circumstances in 1816, it was a painter, Theodore Gericault, who brought the matter out of the newspapers and onto a deeper level of concern.

十九世纪下半叶，艺术摆脱了某些它曾代表社会承担的职责，得以自由地审视自身的本质。这些职责繁多且各不相同。西班牙国王腓力四世从未怀疑过，每当他的军队取得一场著名的胜利时，宫廷画家委拉斯凯兹都是纪念这场胜利的最佳人选。1793年，马拉在浴缸中遇刺身亡，几乎是出于民众的强烈要求，雅克-路易·大卫迅速创作了《马拉遇刺》。1834年，议会大厦被大火焚毁，艺术为我们留下了最令人难忘的记录：J·M·W·特纳亲临现场，描绘了那条巨大的火焰围巾如何在夜空中缓缓蔓延。在这样的时刻，艺术无可匹敌。它给予了我们其他任何地方都无法获得的体验。这位艺术家也并非只是被动的记录者：1816 年，法国护卫舰“美杜莎”号在极其可怕的情况下沉没，正是画家西奥多·杰里科将此事从报纸上带到了更深层次的关注之中。

In paintings such as the ones I have named, people were told what they wanted to know, and told it in a way that allied power to concision and eloquence to understanding…. That is to say that we have a deeper understanding of old age and are the readier to meet it ourselves if we have studied Joseph Wright of Derby’s The Old Man and Death . We have a deeper understanding of what it means for one person to give himself to another if we have studied Rembrandt’s The Jewish Bride . We have a deeper understanding of what it means to love the world and lose it if we have studied the valedictory images of the dying Watteau. Marcel Proust was one of the most observant men who ever lived, but he spoke for all of us when he wrote, “Until I saw Chardin’s paintings I never realized how much beauty lay around me in my parents’ house, in the half-cleared table, in the corner of a tablecloth left awry, in the knife beside the empty oyster-shell.”

在我提到的这些画作中，人们被告知了他们想知道的一切，而且是以一种将力量与简洁、雄辩与理解融为一体的方式呈现的……也就是说，如果我们研读过约瑟夫·赖特·德比的《老人与死神》，我们对老年会有更深刻的理解，也更能坦然面对自己的衰老。如果我们研读过伦勃朗的《犹太新娘》，我们对一个人奉献自己的意义会有更深刻的理解。如果我们研读过华托临终前的画作，我们对热爱世界却最终失去世界的意义会有更深刻的理解。马塞尔·普鲁斯特是历史上最具观察力的人之一，但他写下的这句话却道出了我们所有人的心声：“直到我看到夏尔丹的画作，我才意识到父母家中竟蕴藏着如此多的美：在半收拾的餐桌上，在凌乱的桌布一角，在空牡蛎壳旁的刀子上。”

But as the nineteenth century came to an end, Russell writes, people began to have needs that the Old Masters couldn’t satisfy because those needs didn’t exist when the Old Masters were around. New masters were needed to speak to the unprecedented despairs and horrors that the twentieth century would bring:

但正如罗素所写，随着十九世纪的结束，人们开始有了旧大师们无法满足的需求，因为这些需求在旧大师们生活的年代并不存在。人们需要新的大师来表达二十世纪前所未有的绝望和恐怖：

Poussin in his Massacre of the Innocents gave us an unforgettable image of a human mouth wide open in a scream; but because he was a great classical artist that scream was incidental to his Olympian overview of the scene as a whole. It fell to Edvard Munch, in 1893, to give us an image of a shriek which (in Munch’s own words) “pierced the whole of nature” and stood for a sudden, vast and quite irresistible sensation of panic and dismay. Europe needed just that picture at just that time, and nothing from the past could have taken its place. In 1945, when the complete facts about the Nazi concentration camps were available for the first time, Europe needed Picasso’s The Charnel House , which was the more powerful for its sobriety of color, its condensed, pressed-down, claustrophobic imagery and its refusal to itemize what was so readily to hand in print. The best art of the past hundred years came into being on occasions when nothing from the past would fill the bill.

普桑在《屠杀无辜者》中为我们呈现了一幅令人难忘的画面：一张血淋淋的嘴巴张得老大，发出凄厉的尖叫；但由于他是一位伟大的古典艺术家，这声尖叫在他宏大的画面构图中只是次要的。直到1893年，爱德华·蒙克才为我们描绘出一幅尖叫的画面，这尖叫（用蒙克自己的话说）“刺穿了整个自然”，代表着一种突如其来、巨大而又无法抗拒的恐慌和惊骇。当时的欧洲正需要这样一幅画，过去的任何作品都无法取代它。1945年，当纳粹集中营的全部真相首次公之于众时，欧洲需要毕加索的《停尸房》，这幅画之所以更加震撼人心，在于它色彩的克制、画面的凝练、压抑和令人窒息的氛围，以及它拒绝罗列那些唾手可得的印刷资料。过去一百年来最优秀的艺术作品，都是在过去没有任何作品能够满足特定需求的时候诞生的。

As a journalist Russell is no less mindful that art and life are connected. Several years ago he went to Flagstaff, Arizona, to see what he called “the most ambitious work of art now under construction in the United States”—the reshaping of Roden Crater, the crater of an extinct volcano, by the artist James Turrell. This is how he began his report in the Times:

作为一名记者，罗素同样深知艺术与生活息息相关。几年前，他前往亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫，参观了他称之为“美国目前正在建造的最雄心勃勃的艺术作品”——艺术家詹姆斯·特瑞尔对罗登火山口（一座死火山的火山口）的改造。以下是他为《泰晤士报》撰写的报道的开头：

One of the undecided problems of our time is the final status of the earthwork as artwork—the huge construction that is set up in remote places, often at great expense, and is necessarily available to only a very few people. Is it a moral breakthrough, a parable of purity that could be acted out in no other way, and a lasting enrichment of human awareness? Or is it the very rich man’s last ridiculous toy and the natural descendant of the eighteenth-century folly that looked like a castle, a bridge or a tower and served no practical purpose at all?

我们这个时代悬而未决的问题之一是土方工程作为艺术品的最终地位——这种在偏远地区建造的大型建筑，往往耗资巨大，而且必然只有极少数人才能欣赏。它究竟是道德上的突破，是无法以其他方式演绎的纯洁寓言，是人类意识的持久丰富？还是富人最后的荒诞玩具，是十八世纪那些外形像城堡、桥梁或塔楼却毫无实际用途的愚蠢建筑的自然继承者？

The query, so refreshingly put, sends us in many directions, for, as Russell goes on to explain, Turrell’s purpose at Roden Crater is “to put the visitor into a direct relationship with our universe that can be obtained in no other way and in no other place. His calculations will take care of the visitor who will come to the crater thousands of years from now. They will take care of an alignment of the moon that will occur once every 18.6 years.”

这个问题问得如此耳目一新，引人深思。正如罗素进一步解释的那样，特雷尔在罗登陨石坑的目的是“让访客与我们的宇宙建立一种其他任何方式、任何地点都无法获得的直接联系。他的计算将为数千年后来到陨石坑的访客做好准备。它们将确保每18.6年发生一次的月球轨道运行。”

Not waiting for the artist’s work to be finished—some time in the 1990s—Russell lay down in the bottom of the crater and opened his eyes wide. “What happens then,” he writes, “is that we experience the universe as a perfect sphere, with the rim of the crater—more than 5,000 feet in diameter—as its terrestrial frontier. All that is contingent or superfluous is abolished. As far as is possible on earth, movements and noise do not exist.”

不等艺术家完成作品——那是在20世纪90年代的某个时候——罗素就躺在了陨石坑底部，睁大了眼睛。“接下来发生的事，”他写道，“就是我们体验到宇宙是一个完美的球体，而陨石坑的边缘——直径超过5000英尺——就是它在地球上的边界。所有偶然的或多余的事物都被消除了。在地球上可能存在的范围内，运动和噪音都不存在了。”

Think how many disciplines that one article starts us musing about: astronomy and geology, ecology and aesthetics, physics and psychology, philosophy and religion. It originated, however, as an article about art; someone had to write about one artist’s vision before we could begin to muse. Writing is often our only avenue into a special world. Not everybody has a talent for painting, or for the piano, or for dance. But we can write our way into the artist’s head and into his problems and solutions. Or we can go there with another writer, as, in this case, we have been taken by John Russell into the mind of James Turrell. The literature is all around us, available as a model to every writer or student who is trying to make complex ideas clear.

想想看，这篇文章引发了多少学科的思考：天文学和地质学、生态学和美学、物理学和心理学、哲学和宗教。然而，它最初是一篇关于艺术的文章；在我们开始思考之前，必须有人先写出一位艺术家的愿景。写作往往是我们进入一个特殊世界的唯一途径。并非每个人都有绘画、钢琴或舞蹈的天赋。但我们可以通过写作进入艺术家的内心世界，了解他们的问题和解决方案。或者，我们可以跟随另一位作家的脚步，就像约翰·罗素带领我们进入詹姆斯·特瑞尔的内心世界一样。文学作品就在我们身边，为每一位试图阐明复杂概念的作家或学生提供范例。

Perspective, for instance, is a complex idea, surely not reducible to words. But consider this passage from Prints & People , by A. Hyatt Mayor, who was curator of prints at the Metropolitan Museum of Art for more than forty years. I first noticed his handiwork when I attended an exhibition of prints at the Met and found that the accompanying labels were a pleasure to read—something I hadn’t thought possible. I had always thought museum labels were meant as some kind of penance for the museumgoer. Why else were they written with such solemnity, printed in white type on a beige mat and hung at a height ideal for a child of nine?

例如，透视就是一个复杂的概念，当然无法用语言来概括。但请看A·海厄特·梅耶（A. Hyatt Mayor）所著《版画与人物》（Prints & People）中的这段话。梅耶曾在大都会艺术博物馆担任版画策展人四十余年。我第一次注意到他的工作是在参观大都会博物馆的版画展时，发现展品标签读起来令人愉悦——这在以前是我想都不敢想的。我一直认为博物馆的标签是对参观者的某种考验。否则，为什么它们要写得如此庄重，用白色字体印在米色卡纸上，而且挂在适合九岁孩子阅读的高度呢？

Hyatt Mayor’s labels not only told me what I needed to know; they were written with grace and humor and were unfailingly human, never forgetting that the artists who made the prints—and the people depicted in the prints—were as important as the technical process that produced them. Above all, the labels conveyed tremendous enjoyment. This was the writing of a man in love with prints.

凯悦酒店经理的标签不仅告诉我所需的信息，而且文笔优美幽默，始终充满人文关怀，从未忘记版画的创作者——以及版画中描绘的人物——与版画的制作工艺同样重要。最重要的是，这些标签传递出极大的乐趣。这出自一位热爱版画之人之手。

When Prints & People was published in 1972, near the end of Mayor’s career, it captured in a book all the qualities I had savored on the Met’s walls. I’ve chosen the following passage because it explains a technical subject—perspective—in chronological order, in personal detail and with clarity.

《版画与人物》一书出版于1972年，正值梅耶尔职业生涯的尾声，它将我在大都会艺术博物馆欣赏到的所有特质浓缩于一本书中。我之所以选择以下这段文字，是因为它以时间顺序、个人化的细节和清晰的语言，阐释了透视这一技术性主题。

After the antique world and the Middle Ages had seen objects singly and separately, the Renaissance began to embed things in a continuous matrix of space. Perhaps as early as 1424 some Tuscan painters and mathematicians correlated the artist’s sensuous impressions with the scientist’s intellectual analysis. Disciplines so distinct could parley in Renaissance Italy, where a man might still aspire to know something about everything. Scientists needed art to clarify the world’s complexity, and artists needed scientists to form principles for analyzing appearances. With mathematical perspective a painter could depict objects in their “real” size within an imaginary framework stretching to the horizon. The artifice enabled a Florentine to engrave the first convincing print of a city as only a hawk could then see it.

在古代和中世纪人们将事物孤立地看待之后，文艺复兴时期开始将事物置于一个连续的空间矩阵中。或许早在1424年，一些托斯卡纳的画家和数学家就将艺术家的感官印象与科学家的理性分析联系起来。在文艺复兴时期的意大利，如此截然不同的学科可以相互交流，因为那时人们仍然渴望了解万物。科学家需要艺术来阐明世界的复杂性，而艺术家则需要科学家来构建分析表象的原则。借助数学透视法，画家可以在延伸至地平线的想象框架内，以物体“真实”的大小来描绘它们。这种技法使得一位佛罗伦萨人得以雕刻出第一幅令人信服的城市版画，展现出当时只有鹰才能看到的景象。

From 1483 to 1499, perspective was elaborated as an end in itself in Milan by two Tuscans, Leonardo da Vinci and Fra Luca Pacioli, leading to Pacioli’s publication of the first series of perspective renderings. These puzzles stimulated Germans to contrive even more outlandish fantasies as perspective grew into a game for astonishment. While Pacioli was still working on his book, the Tuscan discovery somehow reached Jean Pelerin, a canon of the cathedral of Toul [in France], who used it for the first clear manual of perspective drawing. The French genius for discovering charm at home inspired the most personal and endearing of all perspective illustrations. These are the first prints that present rooms that we might settle into as we explore the canon’s wine cellar, his chapter house, his courtyard with an espaliered tree, and even his bedroom. The very coziness of these woodcuts may have kept them from circulating as widely as the formal instructions given to a more pedantic age by the great baroque architect Vignola. This Roman’s foreshortening of facades from a mole’s-eye point of view completed the lesson of Mantegna by showing baroque painters how to open ceilings upward through an illusion of soaring colonnades into clouds and the toes of lolling gods.

从1483年到1499年，透视法在米兰由两位托斯卡纳人——列奥纳多·达·芬奇和弗拉·卢卡·帕乔利——发展成为一项独立的艺术形式，最终促成了帕乔利出版第一套透视图集。这些作品激发了德国人构思出更加奇特的想象，透视法也逐渐演变成一种令人惊叹之物。在帕乔利仍在创作他的著作时，托斯卡纳人的这项发现不知何故传到了图勒大教堂的教士让·佩勒兰的耳中，他将其用于编写第一本清晰易懂的透视画法手册。这位法国天才善于发现居家之美，并由此创作出最具个人风格、最令人喜爱的透视插图。这些版画首次展现了我们可以置身其中的房间，仿佛带领我们探索这位教士的酒窖、会议厅、带有棚架树的庭院，甚至是他的卧室。这些木刻版画的温馨舒适或许正是它们未能像伟大的巴洛克建筑师维尼奥拉为那个更为严谨的时代所制定的正式规范那样广泛流传的原因。这位罗马建筑师以鼹鼠的视角来缩短立面的透视效果，完善了曼特尼亚的理论，向巴洛克画家们展示了如何通过高耸的柱廊、云朵和慵懒神祇的脚趾的错觉，将天花板向上打开。

In Mayor’s book each of these examples is keyed to an adjacent picture of the woodcut or etching or engraving he has just described. We see the hawk’s view of Florence, the octahedron of Pacioli, the three-dimensional whimsies of Hans Lencker, the French canon’s cozy bedroom, and Vignola’s intricate arrangement of balconies, columns and vaulted ceilings as they might look to a slightly drunken mole. The pictures complement the words, fixing the printmaker’s achievement in the reader’s eye. But the marvel is how well the words do the job on their own.

在梅耶的书中，每个例子都与他刚刚描述的木刻、蚀刻或雕版画的旁边图片相对应。我们看到了鹰眼俯瞰佛罗伦萨的景象、帕乔利的八面体构图、汉斯·伦克尔的三维立体奇观、法国教士舒适的卧室，以及维尼奥拉精心设计的阳台、柱子和拱形天花板，仿佛是醉醺醺的鼹鼠眼中的景象。图片与文字相得益彰，将版画家的成就呈现在读者眼前。但令人惊叹的是，文字本身也同样精彩绝伦。

Several hundred pages and three centuries later, Mayor is still going like a thoroughbred horse, stepping high and relishing the moment. Notice, below, not only how much information he imparts in one paragraph; also notice the wonder that he brings to the life and the work of the man he is writing about.

几百页的篇幅，三个世纪的时光，梅耶尔依然笔锋犀利，昂首阔步，兴致勃勃。请注意，在下文中，他不仅在一个段落中传递了如此丰富的信息，还展现了他对笔下人物生平及其事业的赞叹之情。

The great Chinese ink painters came from a bureaucratic aristocracy trained to semipictorial writing. Although European gentlefolk used to be taught to draw as they were taught to write, the aristocracy of Europe, so rich in remarkable authors, has produced only one remarkable artist: Count Henri-Marie-Raymond de Toulouse-Lautrec Monfa. Lautrec would probably have painted no better than his father if the breaking of both his legs in his teens had not saved him from wasting his life hunting with his cousins. Case-hardened with an aristocrat’s contempt for middle-class circumspection, he threw himself into the Paris of prostitutes and hoofers, who also had to put on a show and shrug off suffering with a jest. His fever for living burned out his life when he was thirty-six. He had drawn since he was a baby. After the sketchiest instruction in painting, he found in Degas and in Japanese prints the sifting of appearances that he needed for summing up a person or an animal in a few tingling lines. This pictorial shorthand looked like caricature—the distortion of a physical feature—but actually expressed an insight as innocent, and therefore as alarming, as a child’s. Looking upward from his child’s height, he caught people at startling angles in pictures to be hung high. He exercised his command of line and his joy in color through printers trained in color lithography by Cheret. Lautrec drew his first color lithograph for a poster when he was twenty-six. In the ten years that he yet had to live, his oils, vibrant though they often are, changed the course of art less than his lithographs, and especially his posters, which still startle by their strategy of attack. When their yellow and orange and black first flared in the gaslight of the boulevards, no one could miss the fact that art had taken a new turn.

中国伟大的水墨画家出身于受过半图画式写作训练的官僚贵族阶层。虽然欧洲的绅士淑女们过去也像学习写作一样学习绘画，但欧洲贵族阶层——这个人才济济的作家云集之地——却只诞生了一位杰出的艺术家：亨利·玛丽·雷蒙·德·图卢兹-洛特雷克·蒙法伯爵。如果不是十几岁时双腿骨折，洛特雷克或许也只能画出和他父亲一样的画作，否则他不会像他父亲那样虚度光阴，与表兄弟们一起打猎。他身上带着贵族特有的对中产阶级谨慎的蔑视，投身于巴黎的妓女和舞者的世界，这些人也必须装腔作势，用玩笑来掩饰痛苦。他对生活的热情最终在他三十六岁时耗尽了他的生命。他自幼便开始绘画。在接受过最粗浅的绘画指导后，他从德加和日本版画中找到了所需的技巧，能够用寥寥数笔勾勒出人物或动物的轮廓。这种绘画速记看似漫画——对身体特征的扭曲——但实际上却表达了一种如同孩童般纯真，因而也同样令人震惊的洞察力。他以孩童般的视角仰望，捕捉到人物在画作中令人惊艳的角度，并将这些画作高高悬挂。他通过谢雷特（Cheret）培训的彩色石版印刷师，磨练自己对线条的掌控力和对色彩的热爱。劳特雷克26岁时，为一张海报绘制了他的第一幅彩色石版画。在他余下的十年生命中，他的油画作品虽然色彩鲜艳，但对艺术发展的影响远不及他的石版画，尤其是他的海报，后者至今仍以其独特的冲击力令人震撼。当这些海报的黄色、橙色和黑色在林荫大道的煤气灯下闪耀时，没有人会忽视艺术已经迈入了一个新的阶段。

Take one last look at the style. Seemingly exuberant, it’s actually very spare, relying for its panache on individual words chosen to express a precise meaning: vivid nouns (hoofers, gaslight), working adjectives (tingling lines, startling angles, vibrant oils), strong verbs (burned out, flared). It has no flab; Mayor says what he wants to say in as many words as he needs to say it—and no more.

最后再仔细看看这种风格。它看似热情奔放，实则非常简洁，其精妙之处在于对每个词语的精挑细选，以表达精准的含义：生动的名词（舞者，煤气灯），贴切的形容词（令人心动的线条，惊艳的角度，鲜艳的油彩），有力的动词（燃烧殆尽，燃烧殆尽）。它没有丝毫赘述；市长用恰到好处的文字表达了他想说的话——不多不少。

Also notice what a pleasure it is to be in the company of a writer with enthusiasm for his subject. It doesn’t matter what the subject is; I want an ichthyologist to be as committed to fish as Mayor is to prints—to make me think there’s nothing more important to him. This is the personal connection that every reader wants to make with a writer; if we care about the writer we’ll follow him into subjects that we could have sworn we never wanted to know about. The blind attachment of a hobbyist to his hobby is as interesting a life force as the hobby itself.

还要留意与一位对自己的研究对象充满热情的作家相处是多么令人愉悦。研究对象是什么并不重要；我希望一位鱼类学家对鱼类的投入能像市长对版画的投入一样——让我觉得对他来说没有什么比鱼类更重要。这是每位读者都渴望与作家建立的个人联系；如果我们关心这位作家，我们就会跟随他探索那些我们原本发誓永远不会感兴趣的主题。业余爱好者对自己爱好的那种近乎盲目的投入，本身就如同爱好一样，是一种引人入胜的生命力。

Of all the visual arts, none is more compelling than photography. Its directness speaks so powerfully to our everyday experience that we take it for granted, seldom pausing to ask what made a great photograph great. As every tourist knows who has pointed a camera at the Grand Canyon, the difference between a good photograph and a great one is as wide as the Grand Canyon. What is that difference—what mysterious combination of art, technique, light, eye, personality, patience and luck? Can it be explained?

在所有视觉艺术中，摄影的魅力无人能及。它直击人心，与我们的日常生活息息相关，以至于我们习以为常，很少停下来思考一张伟大的照片究竟有何过人之处。正如每一位曾用相机记录大峡谷美景的游客所知，一张好照片与一张伟大照片之间的差距，如同大峡谷一般辽阔。这差距究竟是什么？是艺术、技巧、光线、眼光、个性、耐心和运气这些因素的神秘组合吗？它真的能够被解释吗？

A book that does this for me is Looking at Photographs , by John Szarkowski, curator of the department of photography at the Museum of Modern Art. There may be a better writer about the subject, but I can’t imagine who it would be. Selecting one hundred pictures from the museum’s collection, Szarkowski has written a brief essay about each one that distills just what we need to know about the photographer, his body of work and the picture being discussed. Here are two excerpts:

对我而言，约翰·萨科夫斯基（John Szarkowski）的《欣赏照片》（Looking at Photographs）一书就做到了这一点。萨科夫斯基是纽约现代艺术博物馆摄影部的策展人。或许有比他更优秀的作家，但我实在想不出会是谁。萨科夫斯基从博物馆的馆藏中精选了一百幅照片，并为每一幅照片撰写了一篇简短的评论文章，文章精炼地概括了我们需要了解的关于摄影师、他的作品以及照片本身的信息。以下是两段摘录：

Ansel Adams photographed the [Old Faithful] geyser on at least three separate occasions during the early forties, and produced pictures that are profoundly different from each other. The difference is due not to a willful act of artistic interpretation, but rather to the precision of Adams’s sensibility: He saw what was there not in vague and general terms, but with a rigorous exactitude. The problem (as Cézanne put it) was to realize his sensation.

安塞尔·亚当斯在四十年代初至少三次拍摄了老忠实喷泉，并创作出风格迥异的照片。这种差异并非源于刻意的艺术诠释，而是亚当斯敏锐的感知力：他并非以模糊笼统的方式看待事物，而是以严谨的精确性去捕捉。正如塞尚所说，问题在于如何将他的感知转化为现实。

Much of the best photography of the past generation has concerned itself with giving permanent form to the ephemeral. This concern has expressed itself not only in the analysis of that swarming flux of movement within which Cartier-Bresson found his decisive moment , but also in the approach to subjects that the casual observer might think static. A landscape does not move in the conventional sense, but it changes constantly in other ways, most notably through the agency of light. Ansel Adams attuned himself more precisely than any photographer before him to a visual understanding of the specific quality of the light that fell on a specific place at a specific moment. For Adams the natural landscape is not a fixed and solid sculpture but an insubstantial image, as transient as the light that continually redefines it. This sensibility to the specificity of light was the motive that forced Adams to develop his legendary photographic technique. This brilliant technique might be a millstone around the neck of a photographer who did not need it; for Adams nothing less would suffice to describe his subject.

过去一代最优秀的摄影作品大多致力于将转瞬即逝的事物永恒定格。这种关注不仅体现在对卡蒂埃-布列松捕捉到决定性瞬间的熙攘人群的分析中，也体现在对那些在普通观察者看来或许是静止不动的事物的拍摄手法上。风景并非以传统意义上的运动方式呈现，而是以其他方式不断变化，其中最显著的便是光线的作用。安塞尔·亚当斯比他之前的任何摄影师都更精准地把握了特定地点、特定时刻光线的独特质感。在亚当斯看来，自然景观并非固定不变的雕塑，而是一种虚幻的影像，如同不断重塑它的光线一般瞬息万变。正是这种对光线独特性的敏锐感知，促使亚当斯发展出他传奇般的摄影技法。对于不需要这种技法的摄影师而言，它或许会成为一种负担；但对亚当斯来说，唯有如此才能充分展现他的拍摄对象。

Shifting from the apparent stillness of nature to the perpetual motion of man, Szarkowski gives us a picture of Richard Avedon that is itself like a negative coming into focus as we see the photographer rejecting his earlier vision and deciding that what he wants is its exact opposite:

从看似静止的自然界转向人类永不停歇的运动，萨科夫斯基为我们呈现了一幅理查德·阿维顿的画像，这幅画像本身就像一张底片逐渐清晰，我们看到这位摄影师摒弃了他早期的构想，并决定他想要的恰恰是它的反面：

Even in the early years of his work as a fashion photographer, Richard Avedon was much interested in motion, or rather in the sense of motion, since his interest was not analytical but hortatory. As a young photographer in the early fifties Avedon seemed to think that motion was intrinsically a good thing. It is possible that Avedon was in fact one of the architects, unwitting or otherwise, of the Jet Set concept, which was based on the premise that people with style do not alight. Among his many memorable portraits, it is difficult to call one to mind that shows the subject sitting down.

即使在早期从事时尚摄影工作时，理查德·阿维顿就对动态，或者更确切地说是对动态的感知，抱有浓厚的兴趣，因为他的兴趣并非出于分析，而是出于感召。作为一名五十年代初的年轻摄影师，阿维顿似乎认为动态本身就是一件好事。或许阿维顿正是“喷气机时代”（Jet Set）概念的缔造者之一，无论他是否意识到这一点。“喷气机时代”的概念基于这样一个前提：有品位的人不会轻易下车。在他众多令人难忘的肖像作品中，很难想起有哪一张是人物坐着的。

In the beginning Avedon attempted to deal with the subject of motion in a rather literal way, by shooting moving subjects at slow shutter speeds, thus describing forms that tended to resemble feathery-edged projectiles. Some viewers felt that these pictures expressed movement. Whether they did or not, they did not describe a great deal about the object in motion. Perhaps for this reason Avedon later radically revised his approach to the problem. He decided (it would seem) that the most interesting thing that photography could do with movement was destroy it, and show its crystal-clear fossil, suspended in perpetuity, like the once-human figures disinterred at Vesuvius, seemingly overtaken in mid-stride; or, more nearly, like faces illuminated by a catastrophic explosion, the significance of which has not yet registered in their expressions. As the newspapers prove again each day, there is something fascinating and subtly disturbing about a photograph of a person open-mouthed in speech. The effect can be comic or ludicrous or tragic, but the root cause is the same. Life has been arrested.

起初，阿维顿尝试以一种相当直白的方式来处理运动这一主题，他使用慢速快门拍摄运动的物体，从而呈现出类似羽毛状抛射物的形态。一些观众认为这些照片表达了运动。无论是否如此，它们都没有充分展现运动物体的本质。或许正因如此，阿维顿后来彻底改变了他对这个问题的处理方式。他似乎认为，摄影处理运动最有趣的方式是将其摧毁，展现其晶莹剔透的化石，使其永恒凝固，就像维苏威火山挖掘出的人类遗骸，仿佛在半空中被火山灰吞噬；或者更确切地说，就像灾难性爆炸照亮的面孔，其意义尚未在他们的表情中显现。正如报纸每天所证明的那样，一张张着嘴说话的人的照片，总有一种既迷人又微妙的不安感。这种效果可以是滑稽的、荒诞的，也可以是悲剧性的，但其根源却是一样的。生命已然停滞。

Along with the vigor of the style and the photographic clarity of its images—the feathery-edged projectiles and the crystal-clear fossil—a quality that I like in Szarkowski’s writing is confidence. This is a man with hard-won knowledge of a subject that requires an understanding of both a creative process and a technical process, and he states his opinions boldly; there is nothing feathery-edged about them. A writer who undertakes to be a tour leader can’t afford to be bashful. We want a guide who is in command.

除了他作品中充满活力的文风和照片般的清晰度——从羽毛般纤细的弹丸到晶莹剔透的化石——萨科夫斯基文字中另一个令我欣赏的特质是自信。他是一位对创作过程和技术过程都了如指掌的领域有着深刻理解的作家，他的观点直言不讳，毫不含糊。一位自诩为导游的作家绝不能畏首畏尾。我们需要的是一位掌控全局的向导。

Good art writing should above all help us to see, just as good music writing should help us to hear, and its domain can be as wide as the world we live in. Often, in fact, we need to be shown what is right before our eyes. The graphic designer Paul Rand, in his book A Designer’s Art , notes that although the Oxford English Dictionary devotes two columns to “graphics” and four to “design,” most people don’t know what is meant by “graphic design.” The term “commercial art,” he says, is probably the one that comes closest to describing his métier, but “snobbery and the lack of clarity about its scope have contributed to its gradual disappearance.” Here’s his own definition: “A graphic designer is one who creates ideas that are expressed in words and/or pictures and generally solves problems of visual communication. Items that require the work of a graphic designer before they can be printed or produced include price tags, catalogues, newspapers, magazines, posters, brochures, advertisements, books, book jackets, stationery, logos, packaging, product nomenclature (nameplates), signs—in short, anything involving the visual manipulation of words and/or pictures.”

好的艺术评论首先应该帮助我们看清事物，正如好的音乐评论应该帮助我们听清事物一样，其范畴之广博，足以涵盖我们所生活的世界。事实上，很多时候，我们需要被直接呈现在眼前的事物。平面设计师保罗·兰德在他的著作《设计师的艺术》中指出，尽管《牛津英语词典》用两栏篇幅解释“图形”（graphics），用四栏篇幅解释“设计”（design），但大多数人并不了解“平面设计”的含义。他认为，“商业艺术”一词或许最能贴切地描述他的职业，但“势利眼以及对其范畴缺乏清晰的认识，导致了它逐渐消失”。以下是他自己的定义：“平面设计师是指创作以文字和/或图像表达的创意，并解决视觉传达问题的人。在印刷或制作之前需要平面设计师工作的物品包括：价格标签、产品目录、报纸、杂志、海报、宣传册、广告、书籍、书皮、文具、标志、包装、产品名称（铭牌）、标牌——简而言之，任何涉及文字和/或图像视觉处理的物品。”

Rand’s own ventures into most of these forms have so brilliantly solved the particular problem that our eye now accepts his designs as part of the American landscape. But there was nothing haphazard about their birth. The IBM logo, for instance, is one of his most famous creations. I’ve stared at it for five years on different word processors, never noticing that its three letters pose a severe design problem because of their increasing width—a problem Rand solved, as he explains in A Designer’s Art , by invoking one of the most historically helpful and pleasing of all visual aids:

兰德对这些设计形式的探索大多都巧妙地解决了特定问题，以至于我们现在已经将他的设计视为美国景观的一部分。但它们的诞生并非偶然。例如，IBM 的标志就是他最著名的作品之一。五年来，我一直在不同的文字处理软件上盯着它看，却从未注意到这三个字母由于宽度递增而构成了一个严重的设计问题——兰德在《设计师的艺术》一书中解释道，他通过运用历史上最实用、最令人愉悦的视觉辅助手段之一解决了这个问题：

Nature has striped the zebra. Man has striped his flags and awnings, ties and shirts. For the typographer, stripes are rules; for the architect they are a means of creating optical illusions. Stripes are dazzling, sometimes hypnotic, usually happy. They are universal. They have adorned the walls of houses, churches and mosques. Stripes attract attention.

大自然赋予斑马条纹，人类也赋予旗帜、遮阳篷、领带和衬衫条纹。对于排版师来说，条纹是规则；对于建筑师来说，条纹是创造视觉错觉的手段。条纹令人眼花缭乱，有时甚至令人着迷，通常给人以愉悦之感。它们是普世的，装饰着房屋、教堂和清真寺的墙壁。条纹引人注目。

The stripes of the IBM logo serve primarily as an attention-getting device. They take commonplace letters out of the realm of the ordinary. They are memorable. They suggest efficiency and speed. The recent spate of striped logos in the marketplace attests to their effectiveness.

IBM标志中的条纹主要起到吸引眼球的作用。它们使普通的字母脱颖而出，令人过目难忘，并暗示着高效和速度。近期市场上大量涌现的条纹标志也证明了这种设计的有效性。

Visually, stripes superimposed on a cluster of letters tend to tie them together. This is especially useful for complex groupings such as the letters IBM, in which each character gets progressively wider, thereby creating a somewhat uncomfortable, open-ended sequence.

从视觉上看，在字母簇上叠加条纹往往能将它们联系起来。这对于像 IBM 这样复杂的字母组合尤其有用，因为每个字母的宽度逐渐增加，从而形成一种略显突兀、开放式的序列。

Note the astonishing tightness of that passage. In 140 words Rand tells us everything a layman needs to know about the history of stripes in visual design and the application of that history to one of the memorable symbols of our times. Also notice what the style tells us about the man. He’s more than a great designer; he’s a humanist and a teacher—someone we’d like to have designing for us. The style is the man—as it always should be.

请注意这段文字惊人的精炼。兰德仅用140个字，就向外行人讲述了视觉设计中条纹的历史，以及这段历史如何应用于我们这个时代一个令人难忘的符号。还要注意这种风格如何展现了兰德其人。他不仅是一位伟大的设计师，更是一位人道主义者和导师——我们都希望有他这样的人为我们设计。风格即是兰德本人——理应如此。

One of the most potent elements in our daily landscape, affecting everything we read, is the typeface. Typefaces have always made a big difference to me. The bedroom of my boyhood years was so crammed with the artifacts of two hobbies—printing and baseball—that to reach my bed I had to thread a path between, on one side, a Chandler & Price printing press, a rack of drawers of assorted typefaces and a shelf of books by type designers and, on the other side, an immense hoard of Big League Gum cards, a mountain of back issues of Baseball magazine and a stack of books by authors like Babe Ruth. The room smelled faintly of grape, that being the purported flavor of the gum. I studied the typography books as intently as I studied the batting averages on the gum cards, endlessly reading in typefaces of different sizes and fonts the same expedient sentence containing every letter of the alphabet, “The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy sleeping dog,” or its far more interesting little brother, “Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs.” From all that looking I developed strong feelings about the subtle gradations that typecutters and printers have achieved in Roman letter forms over the centuries and how those forms can work for or against the emotional intentions of an author.

字体是我们日常生活中最具影响力的元素之一，它影响着我们阅读的一切。字体对我来说一直意义非凡。我童年时的卧室里堆满了印刷和棒球这两大爱好的物件，以至于我每次想走到床边，都得小心翼翼地穿过两边：一边是钱德勒-普莱斯印刷机、一排抽屉里装着各种各样的字体以及一架书架上的字体设计师著作；另一边则是堆积如山的美国职业棒球大联盟口香糖卡片、成堆的过刊《棒球》杂志以及一摞像贝比·鲁斯这样的作家的书籍。房间里弥漫着淡淡的葡萄味，据说那是口香糖的味道。我研读排版书籍，就像研究口香糖卡片上的击球率一样认真，一遍又一遍地阅读着同一句包含所有字母的简洁句子，用不同大小和字体呈现，比如“敏捷的棕色狐狸跳过了懒惰的睡狗”，或者它更有趣的变体：“把我的箱子装满五打酒壶”。通过这些观察，我对几个世纪以来排版师和印刷师在罗马字母形式上取得的微妙变化，以及这些形式如何影响作者的情感意图，产生了强烈的感受。

So subjective a process might seem hard to describe in writing, but many printers and designers have done it. One of them was the British typographer Beatrice Warde:

如此主观的过程似乎很难用文字描述，但许多印刷商和设计师都做过。其中一位就是英国排版师比阿特丽斯·沃德：

[My first generalization] is that before any question of physical or literary suitability must come the question of whether the face itself is tolerable or intolerable as a version of the Roman alphabet. If a single letter is warped or snub; if the letters, however pretty in themselves, do not combine automatically into words; if the fourth consecutive page begins to dazzle and irk the eye, and in general if the pages cannot be read with subconscious but very genuine pleasure, that type is intolerable, and that is all there is about it. There are bad types and good types, and the whole science and art of typography begins after the first category has been set aside.

我的第一个概括是，在考虑字体在物理或文学上的适用性之前，必须先考虑字体本身作为罗马字母的变体是否能够被接受。如果单个字母变形或歪斜；如果字母本身再漂亮，也无法自然地组合成单词；如果连续翻到第四页就开始让人眼花缭乱、感到不适；总而言之，如果阅读时无法获得发自内心的愉悦感，那么这种字体就是无法接受的，仅此而已。字体有好坏之分，排版这门科学和艺术的精髓，正是在排除了坏字体之后才得以展开。

The second generalization is, briefly, that the thing is worth doing. It does genuinely matter that a designer should take trouble and take delight in his choice of typefaces. The trouble and delight are taken not merely “for art’s sake” but for the sake of something so subtly and intimately connected with all that is human that it can be described by no other phrase than “the humanities.” If “the tone of voice” of a typeface does not count, then nothing counts that distinguishes man from the other animals. The twinkle that softens a rebuke; the martyr’s super-logic and the child’s intuition; the fact that a fragment of moss can pull back into the memory a whole forest—these are proofs that there is reality in the imponderable, and that not only notation but connotation is part of the proper study of mankind.

第二个概括简而言之就是：这件事值得去做。设计师认真挑选字体，并从中获得乐趣，这的确意义非凡。这种用心和乐趣并非仅仅“为了艺术”，而是为了某种与人类本质微妙而紧密相连的东西，这种东西只能用“人文”来概括。如果字体的“语调”不重要，那么人类与其他动物的区别也就不重要了。轻柔的责备中透出的光芒；殉道者超凡的逻辑和孩童的直觉；一小片苔藓就能唤起人们对整片森林的记忆——这些都证明了在不可估量的事物中蕴含着真实，而对人类的恰当研究不仅包括符号，还包括内涵。

The best part of typographic wisdom lies in this study of connotation, the suitability of form to content. People who love ideas must have a love of words, and that means, given a chance, they will take a vivid interest in the clothes which words wear. The more they like to think, the more they will be shocked by any discrepancy between a lucid idea and a murky typesetting. They will become ritualists and dialecticians. They will use such technically indefensible words as “romantic,” “chill” and “jaunty” to describe different type faces. If they are wise, they will always admit that they are dealing with processes of the subconscious mind, mere deft servants of the goddess Literature.

排版智慧的精髓在于对内涵的研究，即形式与内容的契合。热爱思想的人必然热爱文字，这意味着，只要有机会，他们就会对文字的“外衣”产生浓厚的兴趣。他们越是喜欢思考，就越会对清晰的思想与晦涩的排版之间的任何差异感到震惊。他们会成为仪式主义者和辩证法专家。他们会用诸如“浪漫的”、“轻松的”和“轻快的”这类在技术上站不住脚的词语来描述不同的字体。如果他们足够睿智，他们终究会承认，他们所面对的是潜意识的运作，只不过是文学女神的得力仆人罢了。

Remember connotation, therefore, if you write about the visual arts; there’s almost always more to looking at art than meets the eye. Memory and imagination, for instance, are powerfully at work in how we process what we see, as the English novelist Aldous Huxley points out in The Art of Seeing , a book in which he describes his “visual re-education” from a condition that had left him almost blind by the age of twenty-five:

因此，如果你要撰写关于视觉艺术的文章，请记住内涵；欣赏艺术几乎总是比表面所见的更丰富。例如，记忆和想象力在处理我们所见事物的过程中发挥着强大的作用，正如英国小说家奥尔德斯·赫胥黎在《观看的艺术》一书中指出的那样，他在书中描述了自己如何从一种使他25岁时几乎失明的疾病中“重新接受视觉教育”：

The capacity for perception depends upon the amount, the kind and the availability of past experiences. But past experiences exist for us only in the memory. Therefore it is true to say that perception depends upon memory. Closely related to memory is imagination, which is the power of recombining memories in novel ways, so as to make mental constructions different from anything actually experienced in the past.

感知能力取决于过往经验的数量、种类和可获得性。但过往经验对我们而言只存在于记忆中。因此，可以说感知依赖于记忆。与记忆密切相关的是想象力，它是一种将记忆以新颖的方式重组的能力，从而构建出与过去实际经验截然不同的心理结构。

The extent to which perception and, consequently, vision are dependent on memory and imagination is a matter of everyday experience. We see familiar things more clearly than when we see objects about which we have no stock of memories. The old seamstress, who cannot read without glasses, can see to thread her needle with the naked eye. Why? Because she is more familiar with needles than with print. A man who can work all day at the office without undue fatigue of the eyes is worn out by an hour at the museum and comes home with a splitting headache. Why? Because at the office he is following a regular routine and looking at words and figures, the like of which he looks at every day; whereas in the museum everything is strange, novel and outlandish.

感知，进而视觉，在多大程度上依赖于记忆和想象，是我们日常生活中常见的现象。我们看熟悉的事物比看不清那些我们毫无记忆的事物要清晰得多。那位老裁缝，不戴眼镜就看不清字，却能用肉眼穿针引线。为什么？因为她对针的熟悉程度远胜于对文字的熟悉程度。一个在办公室工作一整天眼睛都不会感到过度疲劳的人，在博物馆待一个小时就会精疲力竭，回家后头痛欲裂。为什么？因为在办公室里，他遵循着固定的工作流程，看着那些他每天都会看到的文字和数字；而在博物馆里，一切都是陌生的、新奇的、奇异的。

Or take the case of the lady who is terrified of snakes and who mistakes what to everyone else is obviously a length of rubber tubing for an enormous viper. Her vision, as tested on the eye chart, is normal. Why, then, does she see what isn’t there? Because her imagination had been in the habit of using old memories of snakes to construct alarming images of them, and under the influence of her imagination her mind misinterpreted the sensa connected with the rubber tubing in such a way that she vividly “saw” a viper.

再举个例子，一位女士非常害怕蛇，她把别人眼中显而易见的橡胶管误认为是一条巨大的蝰蛇。她的视力经视力表测试显示正常。那么，她为什么会看到根本不存在的东西呢？因为她的想象力习惯于利用过去关于蛇的记忆来构建可怕的蛇的形象，在这种想象力的影响下，她的大脑错误地解读了与橡胶管相关的感官信息，以至于她清晰地“看到”了一条蝰蛇。

I’ll give the last word to E. H. Gombrich, the eminent art historian, not only because of his eminence but because one premise of this book is that the sciences and the humanities are more inseparable than we like to think. The following passage, though ostensibly about art, is as good an example of science writing as you’ll find in these pages—clear, vivid, elegant and always grounded in details we recognize from our own experience. It’s from a book whose title is as provocative as the passage itself—A rt and Illusion: A Study in the Psychology of Pictorial Representation .

最后，我想引用著名艺术史学家E·H·贡布里希的话，这不仅是因为他的卓越成就，更因为本书的一个前提是：科学与人文的联系远比我们想象的更加紧密。以下这段文字，表面上是关于艺术的，却是本书中难得一见的科学写作典范——清晰、生动、优雅，并且始终立足于我们自身经验中可辨识的细节。这段文字出自一本书，书名与文字本身一样引人深思——《艺术与错觉：图像表征心理学研究》。

What we get on the retina, whether we are chickens or human beings, is a welter of dancing light points stimulating the sensitive rods and cones that fire their messages into the brain. What we see is a stable world. It takes an effort of the imagination and a fairly complex apparatus to realize the tremendous gulf that exists between the two.

无论我们是鸡还是人，视网膜上看到的都是无数闪烁的光点，它们刺激着敏感的视杆细胞和视锥细胞，并将信息传递到大脑。我们看到的是一个稳定的世界。要意识到这两者之间存在的巨大鸿沟，需要丰富的想象力和相当复杂的生理机制。

Consider any object, such as a book or a piece of paper. When we scan it with our two eyes it projects upon our two retinas a restless, flitting pattern of light of various wave lengths and intensities. This pattern will hardly ever repeat itself exactly—the angle at which we look, the light, the size of our pupils, all these will have changed. The white light that a piece of paper reflects when turned toward the window is a multiple of what it reflects when turned away. It is not that we do not notice some change; indeed, we must if we want to form an estimate of the illumination.

想想任何物体，比如一本书或一张纸。当我们用双眼扫视它时，它会在我们的视网膜上投射出一个不断变化、闪烁的光斑，这些光斑具有不同的波长和强度。这种光斑几乎不会完全重复——我们观察的角度、光线、瞳孔大小，所有这些都会发生变化。一张纸朝向窗户时反射的白光，是它背对窗户时反射白光的倍数。这并不是说我们没有注意到这种变化；事实上，如果我们想要估算光照强度，就必须注意到这种变化。

But we are never conscious of the objective degree of all these changes unless we use what psychologists call a “reduction screen,” in essence a peephole that makes us see a speck of color but masks off its relationships. Those who have used this magic instrument report the most striking discoveries. A white handkerchief in the shade may be objectively darker than a lump of coal in the sunshine. We rarely confuse the one with the other because on the whole the lump of coal will be the blackest patch in our field of vision, the handkerchief the whitest, and it is relative brightness that matters and that we are aware of. The coding process begins while en route between the retina and our conscious mind.

但除非我们使用心理学家所谓的“简化屏”，否则我们永远无法意识到所有这些变化的客观程度。这种简化屏本质上是一个窥视孔，它让我们看到一个色点，却掩盖了它与其他颜色之间的关系。那些使用过这种神奇工具的人报告了最惊人的发现。一块阴凉处的白色手帕可能比阳光下的一块煤炭颜色更深。我们很少会将两者混淆，因为总体而言，煤炭是我们视野中最黑的区域，手帕是最白的区域，而真正重要的是相对亮度，也是我们能够感知到的。编码过程始于视网膜和我们意识之间的传输过程中。

The term which psychology has coined for our relative imperviousness to the dizzy variations that go on in the world around us is “constancy.” The color, shape and brightness of things remain to us relatively constant, even though we may notice some variation with the change of distance, illumination, angle of vision, and so on. Our room remains the same room from dawn to midday to dusk, and the objects in it retain their shape and color. Only when we are faced with special tasks involving attention to these matters do we become aware of uncertainties. We would not judge the color of an unfamiliar fabric in artificial light, and we step into the middle of the room if we are asked whether a picture hangs straight on the wall.

心理学用“恒常性”一词来描述我们对周围世界纷繁复杂的变化相对麻木的现象。即使我们可能会注意到距离、光照、视角等因素的变化，事物的颜色、形状和亮度对我们来说仍然相对恒定。从黎明到正午再到黄昏，我们的房间始终如一，房间里的物品也保持着它们原有的形状和颜色。只有当我们面临需要关注这些方面的特殊任务时，我们才会意识到其中的不确定性。我们不会用人造光来判断一块陌生布料的颜色，如果有人问我们一幅画是否挂在墙上，我们会走到房间中央仔细查看。

Otherwise our capacity to make allowances, to infer from relationships alone, is astounding. We all know the experience at the cinema when we are ushered to a seat very far off-center. At first the screen and what is on it look so distorted and unreal that we feel like leaving. But in a few minutes we have learned to take our position into account, and the proportions right themselves. And as with shapes, so with colors. A faint light is disturbing at first, but with the aid of the physiological adaptation of the eye we soon get the feel of relationships, and the world assumes its familiar face.

否则，我们仅凭关系就能做出调整、进行推断的能力就令人惊叹。我们都经历过这样的情况：在电影院里，我们被安排到一个偏离中心很远的座位上。起初，银幕和上面的画面看起来如此扭曲、如此不真实，以至于我们想要离开。但几分钟后，我们就学会了将自己的位置考虑在内，画面比例也自然而然地恢复了正常。颜色也是如此。微弱的光线起初会让人感到不适，但借助眼睛的生理适应，我们很快就能感受到光线与周围环境的关系，世界也恢复了它熟悉的面貌。

Without this faculty of man and beast alike to recognize identities across the variations of difference, to make allowance for changed conditions, and to preserve the framework of a stable world, art could not exist.

如果没有人类和动物都具备的这种能力，即能够识别差异中的身份，适应变化的环境，并维护一个稳定世界的框架，艺术就不可能存在。

# ↩

8. The Natural World

8. 自然世界

On May 23, 1987, the New York Times ran a long obituary of Archie Carr, a zoologist who spent his entire fifty-five-year career studying the giant sea turtle. I had never heard of Professor Carr, but I enjoyed reading the story of his life. Operating mainly from a field camp in Costa Rica, he reestablished turtle populations in many countries where they had been almost exterminated for their food, developed tagging techniques that partly solved the mystery of their breeding cycle and their 1,200-mile migrations, and wrote eleven books that created a popular understanding of the work he and his colleagues were doing to save the species. (His academic base for all fifty-five years was the University of Florida at Gainesville.) Several of the books won literary awards and one of them, The Windward Road , inspired the formation of the Caribbean Conservation Corporation, a group that coordinates the research and rescue efforts that Professor Carr set in motion.

1987年5月23日，《纽约时报》刊登了一篇长篇讣告，悼念动物学家阿奇·卡尔。卡尔毕生致力于研究巨型海龟，长达55年。我之前从未听说过卡尔教授，但读了他的生平故事后，我感到非常欣慰。卡尔主要在哥斯达黎加的一个野外营地开展工作，他帮助许多国家重建了海龟种群——这些海龟曾因食用而被几乎灭绝；他研发的标记技术部分解开了海龟繁殖周期和1200英里迁徙路线的谜团；他还撰写了11本书，让大众了解他和同事们为拯救这一物种所做的工作。（他55年的学术生涯都以佛罗里达大学盖恩斯维尔分校为基地。）他的几本书荣获文学奖，其中一本《迎风之路》促成了加勒比海保护公司的成立。该公司负责协调卡尔教授发起的海龟研究和救援工作。

At first I found it incredible that a man would devote his whole life to one animal. But then I thought of my father, who died at ninety-one with his love undiminished for a business that made one product—the shellac business, William Zinsser & Co., that his German immigrant grandfather founded in 1849 and that was even nearer to extinction than the sea turtle when my father left college in 1909 to save it. To him the life cycle of the lac bug, spinning its resinous cocoon onto the twigs of trees north of Calcutta, was as romantic as the turtle’s cycle obviously was to Archie Carr, and he brought to his work an enthusiasm and a passion for quality that made his business prosper. Seeing how much he enjoyed his work and how good he was at it, I learned at an early age what has been an important principle to me ever since—that what we want to do we will do well.

起初，我难以置信一个人竟会将一生奉献给一种动物。但后来我想到了我的父亲，他享年九十一岁，却始终对一家只生产一种产品的企业——威廉·津瑟公司（William Zinsser & Co.）——充满热爱。这家公司由他的德国移民祖父于1849年创立，在我父亲1909年辍学投身拯救紫胶虫时，紫胶虫的生存状况甚至比海龟还要岌岌可危。对他而言，紫胶虫在加尔各答北部树枝上吐丝结茧的生命周期，如同海龟的生命周期对阿奇·卡尔（Archie Carr）一样充满浪漫情怀。他对工作的热情和对品质的执着，使他的企业蓬勃发展。看到他如此热爱自己的工作，并且做得如此出色，我从小就明白了一个对我影响至深的重要原则——只要我们想做，就能做好。

That principle would surely apply to Archie Carr, I thought, and I went out and got one of his books, So Excellent a Fishe: A Natural History of Sea Turtles . Its title comes from an act that was passed in 1620 by the Bermuda Assembly to stop “sundrye lewd & impvident psons who in their continuall goinges out to sea snatch & catch up indifferentlye all kinds of Tortoyses both yonge and old,” thereby risking the extinction of “so excellent a fishe.” I was delighted by the coincidence that delivered Professor Carr to me just as I was wondering what writers to include in a chapter on the natural world, though it really wasn’t luck. Somebody said—I’m quite sure it wasn’t me; it must have been Lord Chesterfield—that chance favors the prepared mind, and certainly it’s true that writers, in some corner of their conscious or subconscious brain, are always working. A writer should always be ready to be lucky.

我想，这条原则肯定也适用于阿奇·卡尔，于是我出门买了一本他的书——《如此优秀的鱼：海龟自然史》。书名源于1620年百慕大议会通过的一项法案，旨在阻止“那些粗俗无知的人不断出海，肆意捕捞各种幼龟和老龟”，以免“如此优秀的鱼”灭绝。我正琢磨着该在关于自然世界的章节里收录哪些作家的作品，却意外地找到了卡尔教授，这让我欣喜不已，尽管这并非偶然。有人说过——我敢肯定不是我说的；一定是切斯特菲尔德勋爵——机会总是眷顾有准备的人，这话一点没错，作家们在意识或潜意识的某个角落里，总是在创作。作家应该时刻准备着迎接好运。

Enthusiasm, which I knew I would find in Archie Carr’s book, is crucial to writing well. One reason I believe in writing-across-the-curriculum programs is that they encourage students to write about subjects that interest them, thus bringing them the surprising news that writing can be useful in their lives. It’s astonishing how quickly high school students can learn to write if they want to get into college and need to compose an essay telling the admissions office why they are so desirable. All the aimlessness of their school papers—the lazy thinking, the clogged passages—is for one shining moment made tidy. Motivation clears the head faster than a nasal spray.

热情，正如我在阿奇·卡尔的书中看到的那样，对写作至关重要。我相信跨学科写作项目的原因之一，就是它鼓励学生写作自己感兴趣的主题，从而让他们惊喜地发现写作在生活中也能发挥作用。高中生如果想上大学，需要写一篇文书向招生办公室阐述自己的优势，那么他们学习写作的速度之快令人惊叹。他们学校作文中那些漫无目的的写作——懒散的思考、冗长的段落——在写作的那一刻都变得清晰明了。写作的动力比鼻腔喷雾剂更能让人头脑清醒。

In Archie Carr’s So Excellent a Fishe I was quickly caught up in the two central wonders of the sea turtle’s life. One is that it is “among the spectacular animal travelers of the world,” journeying with uncanny precision between Ascension Island and various Caribbean beaches by navigational methods that are still an enigma to science. The other is that at breeding time the three-hundred-pound female leaves the familiar safety of the sea and comes ashore to lay her eggs on hostile land. There she is both too ponderous and too preoccupied to put up a fight. “Once the nesting has started,” Dr. Carr writes, “she will go on doggedly through the hour-long ceremony with a pack of dogs digging out her nest beneath her or with drunken Indians drumming on her back.”

在阿奇·卡尔的《如此卓越的鱼》一书中，我很快就被海龟生命中的两大奇观所吸引。其一是它是“世界上最壮观的动物旅行者之一”，能够以惊人的精准度往返于阿森松岛和加勒比海的各个海滩之间，其导航方式至今仍是科学界的谜团。其二是到了繁殖季节，重达三百磅的雌性海龟会离开熟悉的、安全的海洋，来到陆地上产卵。在那里，它既笨重又忙于其他事情，无暇反抗。“一旦筑巢开始，”卡尔博士写道，“它就会执着地完成长达一个小时的仪式，一群狗会在它身下挖出巢穴，或者醉醺醺的印第安人在它背上敲鼓。”

The number of eggs that she deposits under such discouraging conditions is itself one of nature’s supreme measuring acts:

在如此不利的条件下，她产下的卵的数量本身就是大自然最伟大的衡量标准之一：

When a green turtle comes ashore she lays roughly a hundred eggs. Compared to the number of eggs laid by wholly aquatic animals such as mackerel or lobsters, a hundred is not very many; but it is more than a lizard lays or a setting hen sets on. The biology [of that figure] is still mostly unknown, but it is clearly there. The whole race and destiny of the creature are probably balanced at the edge of limbo by the delicate weight of that magic number of eggs. One marvel of the number is how great it is; but another is, how small.

绿海龟上岸后，大约会产下100枚卵。与鲭鱼或龙虾等完全水生动物的产卵数量相比，100枚卵并不算多；但比蜥蜴或母鸡产卵的数量要多。这个数字背后的生物学原理至今仍不甚明了，但它的存在是显而易见的。或许，整个物种的命运都维系于这神奇的卵数之上，仿佛徘徊在生死边缘。这个数字的奇妙之处在于它的数量之多，而另一个奇妙之处在于它的数量之少。

I like the casual purity of that sentence. It says everything it needs to say, and the word “marvel” gives it emotional weight, telling us that something remarkable is going on here. I know management consultants who can’t talk about numbers without using the phrase “order of magnitude”; a six-pack of beer costs on an order of magnitude of five dollars.

我喜欢这句话的简洁纯粹。它表达了所有需要表达的意思，“奇迹”一词赋予了它情感分量，告诉我们这里正在发生一些非凡的事情。我认识一些管理顾问，他们一谈到数字就离不开“数量级”这个词；一箱六瓶装啤酒的价格大概在五美元左右。

When you think of the unpromising future that confronts a turtle egg and the turtle hatchling that comes out of it, you wonder why sea turtles don’t give up their stubborn, reckless old ways of leaving their new generation on shore, and instead carry one big, well-tended egg in a pouch or release myriads of turtle larvae to join the plankton, and swamp the laws of chance with millions of largely expendable progeny. The answer, of course, is that the turtles have hit on the formula for outwitting predators, or at least for surviving in spite of them. The formula is simply one hundred turtle eggs….

当你想到海龟蛋和孵化出来的小海龟所面临的渺茫未来时，你会疑惑，为什么海龟不放弃它们固执而鲁莽的旧习——把新一代留在岸上——而是把一枚精心呵护的大蛋放在育儿袋里，或者释放无数幼龟加入浮游生物，用数百万个几乎可以牺牲的后代来打破命运的法则。答案当然是，海龟已经找到了战胜捕食者，或者至少是在捕食者威胁下生存下来的秘诀。这个秘诀很简单：一百枚海龟蛋……

If you were able to get a complete list of the animals that prey on turtle eggs and young it would surely include most of the carnivores and omnivores, both vertebrate and invertebrate, that live near a turtle-nesting beach. The predators range in size from ants and crabs to bears. Some of them live along the beach itself, some in the coastal scrub. Some come from far back in the interior, showing up for the turtle season as the Siquirres dogs at Tortuguero used to do [Tortuguero is the site of Professor Carr’s camp] and as the Rancho Nuevo coyotes do to this day.

如果能找到一份完整的以海龟蛋和幼龟为食的动物清单，那肯定会包括生活在海龟筑巢海滩附近的绝大多数食肉动物和杂食动物，无论是脊椎动物还是无脊椎动物。这些捕食者的体型大小不一，从蚂蚁、螃蟹到熊都有。有些就生活在海滩边，有些则生活在沿海灌木丛中。还有一些来自内陆深处，会在海龟产卵季出现，就像托尔图格罗的西基雷斯犬（托尔图格罗是卡尔教授的营地所在地）过去常有的捕食行为，以及兰乔努埃沃的郊狼至今仍然如此。

At Tortuguero nowadays the most important non-human predators on the beach are dogs and buzzards. The dogs are the worst. They move in on a laying female and take the eggs as they are laid or prevent her from covering them. They are stronger at digging than buzzards are, too, though buzzards dig better than many people might imagine. Most people, in fact, probably don’t imagine that buzzards dig at all. The other regular turtle eaters are opossums, the few domestic pigs that range the northernmost miles, and the ravening hosts of wari, or white-lipped peccaries, [which] sometimes travel out to the beach from the inland forest at nesting time and hatching time. This is of course a catastrophe, especially if it happens in early October when in hundreds of nests the little turtles rest in tight bundles in little cavities only an inch or less beneath the surface, waiting for the time that seems to them proper for bursting out into the unknown world. Wari are so devastating that when I am asked why the green turtle chooses Turtle Bogue to cling to, out of all the thousands of miles of Caribbean shore that look like good turtle beach, I think first of saying: because peccaries find it hard to get there across the lagoon….

如今在托尔图格罗海滩，最重要的非人类捕食者是狗和秃鹰。狗尤其可怕。它们会靠近正在产卵的雌龟，抢走刚产下的卵，或者阻止雌龟掩埋卵。狗的挖掘能力也比秃鹰强，尽管秃鹰的挖掘能力可能比许多人想象的要好。事实上，大多数人可能根本想象不到秃鹰会挖洞。其他经常捕食海龟的动物还有负鼠、少数生活在最北端的家猪，以及成群的白唇西貒（wari）。白唇西貒有时会在筑巢和孵化期从内陆森林来到海滩。这当然是一场灾难，尤其是在十月初，那时数百个巢穴里的小海龟们紧紧地蜷缩在距离海面仅一英寸甚至更浅的小洞穴中，等待着它们认为合适的时机破壳而出，奔向未知的世界。瓦里鱼的破坏力如此之大，以至于当有人问我，为什么绿海龟在加勒比海数千英里的海岸线上，偏偏选择龟岛（Turtle Bogue）作为依附点时，我首先想到的回答是：因为西貒很难穿过泻湖到达那里……

When [the hatchlings] do come out they waste no time about it. Their trip across the sand to the surf is both fast and direct. So for the turtles of each nest, this time of maximum peril in the whole life of the species is not really a long time at all. It is only a minute or two, or a little longer if the way to the sea should be blocked by many obstacles. Still it seems to a human observer a foolhardy violation of common sense to leave your young ones far back from the sea on the hungry shore, behind dunes or debris which (chances are) cut off the way to the sea and hide it from view. The little turtles come out into a world anxious to eat them. They have simply got to go fast and straight toward the ocean even though they can’t see it, never saw it before, and know of its existence only as a set of signals to react to instinctively.

小海龟破壳而出后，便会迅速奔向大海。它们穿过沙滩直奔海浪，速度极快，路线也十分直接。因此，对于每个巢穴中的海龟来说，这段它们一生中最危险的时期其实并不长。通常只有一两分钟，如果通往大海的道路被重重障碍阻挡，时间或许会稍长一些。然而，在人类观察者看来，将幼小的海龟留在远离大海、饥肠辘辘的海岸边，躲在沙丘或碎石堆后（这些障碍很可能阻断了通往大海的道路，使它们无法看到大海），这似乎是一种愚蠢的、违背常理的行为。小海龟来到一个渴望吞噬它们的世界。它们必须快速而笔直地奔向大海，即使它们看不到大海，以前从未见过大海，它们对大海的存在也只是依靠本能的反应信号。

That’s pleasant writing; we’re there on the beach at Tortuguero, rooting for the turtles and hoping they won’t meet a wari on their crawl to the surf. But the writing couldn’t survive on charm alone; it works because it’s grounded in scientific observation and fact. What sticks in our mind is the hundred eggs, the digging buzzards, the returning coyotes, the signaling sea. In fact, by the end of So Excellent a Fishe I knew more about sea turtles than I ever thought I wanted to know. I also enjoyed the trip, partly because the turtle ultimately gave up very few of its secrets—to Professor Carr or anyone else. Far from wondering how somebody could devote his whole life to one animal, I realized that it would take the fifty-five-year careers of platoons of scientists to determine how the turtle finds its way so unerringly across vast expanses of ocean.

这段文字读来令人愉悦；我们仿佛置身于托尔图格罗海滩，为海龟们加油鼓劲，祈祷它们在爬向海浪的途中不会遇到瓦里鸟。但光靠魅力是不够的；它的成功在于其科学的观察和事实。那些令人印象深刻的画面是：上百枚海龟蛋、挖掘海龟壳的秃鹰、归来的郊狼，以及大海的召唤。事实上，读完《如此优秀的鱼》之后，我对海龟的了解远超我的预期。我也乐在其中，部分原因在于海龟最终几乎没有透露任何秘密——无论是对卡尔教授还是其他人。我并没有疑惑为何有人会将一生奉献给一种动物，而是意识到，要弄清海龟如何在浩瀚的海洋中如此精准地找到方向，需要无数科学家耗费五十五年的时间。

I was also reminded that science in the hands of a good writer will have an unexpected human dimension. In this case the link is the tag that gets fastened to the turtle, requesting the finder to send it back to the University of Florida and to say where and when it was caught. Who are those finders? Professor Carr gives us a sampling of their replies. Most of them are fishermen and other coastal dwellers in remote villages and islands—people not in the habit of writing to professors of zoology. Yet they somehow understand the importance of what the man in Florida is trying to find out and are eager not to botch their brief role. The graciousness of their letters is one of the ornaments of the book:

这也让我意识到，在一位优秀作家的笔下，科学会展现出意想不到的人文情怀。在这个例子中，维系科学的纽带是系在海龟身上的标签，标签上写着：请发现者将海龟寄回佛罗里达大学，并告知捕获地点和时间。这些发现者是谁呢？卡尔教授摘录了他们的一些回信。他们大多是渔民和其他居住在偏远村庄和岛屿上的沿海居民——这些人通常不会给动物学教授写信。然而，他们却理解佛罗里达大学那位科学家想要探究的问题的重要性，并且渴望尽力完成他们短暂的使命。他们来信中的谦逊和礼貌，也成为了本书的一大亮点。

After saluting you affectionately I permit myself to communicate to you having captured a turtle with a metallic plaque which…

在向您致以亲切的敬礼之后，我谨告知您，我捕获了一只带有金属铭牌的乌龟……

I am a Miskito Indian from a small village named Dakura along the Miskito coast, to be able to remit this to you I was forced to come 15 miles to Puerto Cabezas, the closest point of communication…

我是一名来自米斯基托海岸达库拉小村庄的米斯基托印第安人，为了能把这笔钱汇给你，我不得不跋涉15英里来到最近的通讯点——卡贝萨斯港……

I am very glad to be the one that found this tyrtle drifting down to the Nicaraguan’s water it was found in the Pear Lagoon bar on thursday 18 of August at 6:00 o’clock in the morning. I wish that I have explained every thing the right way…

我很庆幸自己发现了这件漂流到尼加拉瓜水域的物品。它是在8月18日星期四早上6点在梨子泻湖的沙洲附近被发现的。我希望我已经把一切都解释清楚了……

I am pleased to tell you that this turtle was catch at Marroon Cay by setting nets. I caught it on the 17 of Octobre of the passed year at 9:00 a.m. Nothing else for the moment, except I would like to keep in touch…

我很高兴地告诉您，这只海龟是在马龙礁用网捕获的。我是去年10月17日上午9点捕获的。目前没有其他消息，只是希望保持联系……

Atentively I direct myself to you to send you a plaque that I found encrusted on a turtle that I caught on the coast of Cojoro Venezuela. This demands that it be sent to your Institute. Receive a cordial embrace…

我特意前来，想寄给您一块我在委内瑞拉科霍罗海岸捕获的海龟身上发现的牌匾。这块牌匾必须寄到您的研究所。谨致以诚挚的问候……

Unlike Archie Carr, who dropped into this book out of the blue, Charles Darwin is someone I knew I wanted to have along on the ride. The odds that he wouldn’t be a good writer struck me as small—someone who gives the frontiers of knowledge an immense push is a good bet to be someone who can express his ideas clearly. Writing is the handmaiden of leadership; Abraham Lincoln and Winston Churchill rode to glory on the back of the strong declarative sentence. I can’t claim, however, that my theory is watertight; it gets shipwrecked, for instance, on the rocky prose of Buckminster Fuller, and Fuller is by no means the only innovative thinker whose thoughts spill out in majestic disarray.

与突然出现在这本书里的阿奇·卡尔不同，查尔斯·达尔文是我早就想邀请他一同参与的。他不太可能不是一位优秀的作家——一个极大地拓展了知识疆界的人，想必也能够清晰地表达自己的思想。写作是领导力的得力助手；亚伯拉罕·林肯和温斯顿·丘吉尔都凭借铿锵有力的陈述句走向了辉煌。然而，我不敢说我的理论万无一失；例如，它就因为巴克敏斯特·富勒晦涩难懂的文风而遭遇了挫折，而富勒绝非唯一一位思想表达方式略显混乱却又充满创新精神的思想家。

Fortunately, Darwin didn’t let me down. Two pages were enough to prove my hunch. I bought a copy of his The Voyage of the Beagle and started right in:

幸好，达尔文没有让我失望。仅仅两页就足以证实我的预感。我买了一本他的《贝格尔号航行记》，然后立刻开始阅读：

After having been twice driven back by heavy south-western gales, Her Majesty’s ship Beagle , a ten-gun brig, under the command of Captain Fitz Roy, R. N., sailed from Devonport on the 27th of December, 1831. The object of the expedition was to complete the survey of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego, commenced under Captain King in 1826 to 1830—to survey the shores of Chile, Peru, and some islands in the Pacific—and to carry a chain of chronometrical measurements round the world. On the 6th of January we reached Teneriffe, but were prevented landing, by fears of our bringing the cholera: the next morning we saw the sun rise behind the rugged outline of the Grand Canary island, and suddenly illumine the Peak of Teneriffe, whilst the lower parts were veiled in fleecy clouds. This was the first of many delightful days never to be forgotten. On the 16th of January, 1832, we anchored at Porto Praya, in St. Jago, the chief island of the Cape de Verd archipelago.

在两次被强劲的西南风暴逼退后，英国皇家海军的十门炮双桅帆船“比格尔号”于1831年12月27日在皇家海军菲茨·罗伊上校的指挥下从德文波特起航。此次探险的目的是完成巴塔哥尼亚和火地岛的勘测工作（这项工作始于1826年至1830年，由金上校负责），勘测智利、秘鲁和太平洋部分岛屿的海岸线，并携带一套环球测年数据链。1月6日，我们抵达特内里费岛，但由于担心我们携带霍乱，未能登陆。第二天清晨，我们看到太阳从大加那利岛崎岖的轮廓后升起，突然照亮了特内里费岛的山峰，而山脚下则笼罩在轻柔的云层中。这是众多令人难忘的美好日子中的第一天。 1832 年 1 月 16 日，我们在佛得角群岛的主岛圣地亚哥的普拉亚港抛锚。

The many delightful days would stretch to four years and nine months before the Beagle would touch England again, and the voyage would revolutionize man’s view of his position in the natural order. But here Charles Darwin is just a young man, twenty-two years old, who signed on as ship’s naturalist because he thought it would be an opportunity for “collecting, observing and noting anything worthy to be noted in natural history.”

在“贝格尔号”再次抵达英国之前，这段漫长而美好的时光将持续四年零九个月，而这次航行也将彻底改变人类对自身在自然秩序中地位的看法。然而，此时的查尔斯·达尔文还只是个二十二岁的年轻人，他之所以报名成为船上的博物学家，是因为他认为这将是一个“收集、观察和记录任何值得在自然史上记载的事物”的机会。

His first paragraph did the necessary work of telling us why the expedition was formed. The second one lets us know instantly that this is no ordinary observer:

他的第一段就交代了探险队成立的原因。第二段则立刻让我们明白，这绝非一位普通的观察员：

The neighborhood of Porto Praya, viewed from the sea, wears a desolate aspect. The volcanic fires of a past age, and the scorching heat of a tropical sun, have in most places rendered the soil unfit for vegetation. The country rises in successive steps of table-land, interspersed with some truncate conical hills, and the horizon is bounded by an irregular chain of more lofty mountains. The scene, as beheld through the hazy atmosphere of this climate, is one of great interest; if, indeed, a person, fresh from the sea, and who has just walked, for the first time, in a grove of cocoa-nut trees, can be a judge of anything but his own happiness.
