In order to have a complete description of the motion, we must specify how the body alters its position with time; i.e . for every point on the trajectory it must be stated what time the body is situated there.

为了完整地描述运动，我们必须具体说明物体如何随时间改变其位置；也就是说，对于轨迹上的每个点，都必须说明物体在该点上的时间。

So we are off on Einstein’s great journey, which is no less epochal than Darwin’s, and though I don’t pretend to understand the formulations that he presents in subsequent chapters, never having taken a course in physics, I think I understand the general nature of his achievement and the thinking that took him there. I understand them because the writing and the reasoning remain orderly throughout.

于是，我们踏上了爱因斯坦的伟大征程，其意义丝毫不亚于达尔文。虽然我从未系统地学习过物理，所以不敢妄称自己完全理解他在后续章节中提出的各种理论，但我认为我理解他成就的总体本质以及他取得这些成就的思路。我之所以能够理解，是因为他的行文和论证始终保持着条理清晰的逻辑。

Along the way Einstein also demystifies himself, continuing to talk to me as a teacher talks to a student, using the written language as a step-by-step method of instruction. He even pauses occasionally—still the kind uncle of the cover photograph—to coddle us over leaps he knows we don’t want to make: “The non-mathematician is seized by a mysterious shuddering when he hears of ‘four-dimensional’ things, by a feeling not unlike that awakened by thoughts of the occult. And yet there is no more commonplace statement than that the world we live in is a four-dimensional space-time continuum.”

在此过程中，爱因斯坦也逐渐揭开了自己的神秘面纱，他像老师教学生一样与我交谈，用书面语言一步一步地进行讲解。他甚至偶尔会停下来——依然是封面照片上那位慈祥的叔叔——耐心地引导我们，避免我们做出他知道我们不想做的跳跃：“非数学家一听到‘四维’的概念，就会感到一种莫名的恐惧，这种感觉与思考神秘事物时产生的恐惧非常相似。然而，我们所生活的世界是一个四维时空连续体，这却是再平常不过的说法了。”

Tearing myself away from Albert Einstein—a parting I never imagined would be sweet sorrow—I’ll add a final plea to all scientists and science students: Go, and do thou likewise. Follow Einstein’s example and Thoreau’s advice (“Simplify! Simplify!”). Reduce your discipline—whatever it is—to a logical sequence of clearly thought sentences. You will thereby make it clear not only to other people but to yourself. You will find out whether you know your subject as well as you thought you did. If you don’t, writing will show you where the holes are in your knowledge or your reasoning.

依依不舍地告别爱因斯坦——我从未想过离别竟会如此甜蜜而伤感——我最后想对所有科学家和理科学生说：去吧，也这样做。效仿爱因斯坦的榜样，听从梭罗的忠告（“简化！简化！”）。将你的学科——无论是什么——简化成一系列逻辑清晰、思路缜密的句子。这样，你不仅能让别人明白，也能让自己明白。你会发现，你对这门学科的了解是否真如你以为的那样透彻。如果并非如此，写作会让你发现知识或推理中的漏洞。

Such instructional uses are by no means the only literary ends that disciplines like physics and chemistry can aspire to. Every science has its unique romance, and a writer who can capture that romance enables the rest of us to glimpse what it is about the field that makes it exciting to those who love it. It’s one of the best gifts that science writing can confer.

诸如此类的教学用途绝非物理和化学等学科所能追求的唯一文学目标。每门科学都有其独特的魅力，而能够捕捉到这种魅力的作家，则能让我们这些普通人得以一窥这门学科究竟有何魅力，令热爱它的人为之倾倒。这正是科学写作所能带来的最佳馈赠之一。

No book has so put me inside the head and heart of a chemist as The Periodic Table , by Primo Levi, an Italian chemist who survived Auschwitz and wrote three powerful books about that experience. The Periodic Table , which was published in this country several years ago to great acclaim (in a superb translation by Raymond Rosenthal), takes its title from the structure of its chapters, each of which is named for a chemical element that played a memorable role at some moment in Levi’s life. (He died in 1987.) Chapter 1, for instance, called “Argon,” begins like this:

没有哪本书能像普里莫·莱维的《元素周期表》那样，让我如此深刻地体会到化学家的内心世界。莱维是一位意大利化学家，曾是奥斯维辛集中营的幸存者，并就此经历撰写了三部震撼人心的著作。《元素周期表》几年前在美国出版后广受好评（由雷蒙德·罗森塔尔出色翻译），书名源于其章节结构，每一章都以一种在莱维生命中某个重要时刻扮演过重要角色的化学元素命名。（他于1987年去世。）例如，第一章名为“氩”，开头是这样的：

There are the so-called inert gases in the air we breathe. They bear curious Greek names of erudite derivation which mean “the New,” “the Hidden,” “the Inactive,” and “the Alien.” They are indeed so inert, so satisfied with their condition, that they do not interfere in any chemical reaction, do not combine with any other element, and for precisely this reason have gone undetected for centuries. As late as 1962 a diligent chemist after long and ingenious efforts succeeded in forcing the Alien (xenon) to combine fleetingly with extremely avid and lively fluorine, and the feat seemed so extraordinary that he was given a Nobel prize. They are also called the noble gases—and here there’s room for discussion as to whether all noble gases are really inert and all inert gases are noble. And finally, they are also called rare gases, even though one of them, argon (the Inactive), is present in the air in the considerable proportion of 1 percent, that is, twenty or thirty times more abundant than carbon dioxide, without which there would not be a trace of life on this planet.

我们呼吸的空气中存在所谓的惰性气体。它们有着源自希腊语的奇特名称，意为“新的”、“隐藏的”、“不活跃的”和“异类”。它们确实非常惰性，非常安于现状，不参与任何化学反应，也不与其他元素结合，正因如此，几个世纪以来一直未被发现。直到1962年，一位勤奋的化学家经过长期而巧妙的努力，才成功地使“异类”（氙）与极其活泼的氟短暂结合，这一壮举如此非凡，以至于他获得了诺贝尔奖。它们也被称为稀有气体——这里存在一个值得探讨的问题：所有稀有气体是否真的惰性，以及所有惰性气体是否都是稀有的。最后，它们也被称为稀有气体，尽管其中一种气体——氩气（惰性气体）——在空气中的含量高达 1%，是二氧化碳的 20 到 30 倍，如果没有氩气，地球上就不会有生命的痕迹。

I don’t know many books that begin with such intellectual gusto. The sentences, like Einstein’s, just flow from point to point, pulling us along with their enjoyment of the story and the language. Words that we don’t expect to meet in science writing—“satisfied,” “avid,” “lively,” “noble”—refresh us with their humanity.

我很少见到有哪本书能像这本书一样，以如此饱满的求知欲开篇。书中的句子如同爱因斯坦的文笔一般流畅自然，引人入胜，带领我们一同沉浸于故事和语言的魅力之中。那些我们意想不到会在科学写作中出现的词汇——“满意的”、“热切的”、“活泼的”、“高尚的”——却以其人文关怀让我们耳目一新。

One of my favorite chapters, “Tin,” recalls a period in the author’s twenties when he and his equally destitute friend Emilio were doing chemical odd jobs at home to make ends meet.

我最喜欢的章节之一“锡”回忆了作者二十多岁时的一段时光，当时他和同样贫困的朋友埃米利奥在家做些化学零工来维持生计。

There are friendly metals and hostile metals. Tin was a friend—not only because, for some months now, Emilio and I were living on it, transforming it into stannous oxide to sell to the manufacturers of mirrors, but also for other, more recondite reasons: because it marries with iron, transforming it into mild tin plate; because the Phoenicians traded in it and it is to this day extracted, refined, and shipped from fabulous and distant countries; because it forms an alloy with copper to give us bronze, the respectable material par excellence, notoriously perennial and well established; because it melts at a low temperature, almost like organic compounds, that is, almost like us; and finally, because of two unique properties with picturesque, hardly credible names, never seen or heard (that I know) by human eye or ear, yet faithfully handed down from generation to generation by all the textbooks—the “weeping” of tin and tin pest.

金属有友善的，也有敌对的。锡是我的朋友——这不仅是因为几个月来，我和埃米利奥一直靠锡为生，把它提炼成氧化亚锡卖给镜子制造商，还有其他一些更为深奥的原因：因为它能与铁结合，制成低合金镀锡板；因为腓尼基人曾进行锡的贸易，而且直到今天，人们仍然从遥远而神秘的国度开采、提炼和运输锡；因为它能与铜形成合金，制成青铜，这种卓越的材料以其经久耐用和稳固性而闻名；因为它熔点低，几乎像有机化合物一样，也就是说，几乎像我们一样；最后，还因为它具有两种独特的性质，其名称奇特而难以置信，据我所知，人类从未见过或听过，却被所有教科书忠实地代代相传——锡的“哭泣”和锡虫。

That paragraph is the sort of thing I had in mind when I said that every science has its romance. It gives me a sense of the affection that chemists presumably feel for the elements that constitute their universe, each one a friend with idiosyncrasies that are—in the manner of friends—both lovable and annoying. I’m glad to know this about chemists and I’m grateful to Primo Levi for giving me a window into their world. His story continues:

我之前说“每门科学都有其浪漫之处”，指的就是这段话。它让我感受到化学家们对构成他们宇宙的各种元素所怀有的深厚情感，每一种元素都像一位朋友，有着各自独特的怪癖——就像朋友之间那样——既可爱又烦人。我很高兴了解化学家的这一面，也感谢普里莫·莱维让我得以窥见他们的世界。他的故事还在继续：

Emilio had managed to carve a lab out of his parents’ apartment…. When they let him take over their bedroom they had not foreseen all the consequences…. Now the hallway was a storeroom jammed with demijohns full of concentrated hydrochloric acid, the kitchen stove (outside of mealtime) was used to concentrate the stannous chloride in beakers and six-liter Erlenmeyer flasks, and the entire apartment was invaded with our fumes…. Everywhere, on the terrace and in the apartment, was scattered an incredible amount of junk, so old and battered as to prove almost unrecognizable: only after a more attentive examination could you distinguish the professional objects from the domestic ones.

埃米利奥竟然把父母的公寓改造成了一个实验室……当初父母让他占用自己的卧室时，并没有预料到会造成如此严重的后果……如今，走廊变成了堆满浓盐酸大玻璃瓶的储藏室，厨房的炉灶（除了吃饭时间）被用来在烧杯和六升的锥形瓶中浓缩氯化亚锡，整个公寓都弥漫着浓烈的气味……露台上和公寓里到处散落着数量惊人的杂物，这些杂物又旧又破，几乎难以辨认：只有仔细观察才能分辨出哪些是专业用品，哪些是家用物品。

In the middle of the lab was a large ventilation hood of wood and glass, our pride and our only protection against death by gasing. It is not that hydrochloric acid is actually toxic: it is one of those frank enemies that come at you shouting from a distance, and from which it is therefore easy to protect yourself. It has such a penetrating odor that whoever can wastes no time in getting out of its way; and you cannot mistake it for anything else, because after having taken in one breath of it you expel from your nose two short plumes of white smoke, like the horses in Eisenstein’s movies, and you feel your teeth turn sour in your mouth, as when you have bitten into a lemon. Despite our quite willing hood, acid fumes invaded all the rooms: the wallpaper changed color, the doorknobs and metal fixtures became dim and rough, and every so often a sinister thump made us jump: a nail had been corroded through and a picture, in some corner of the apartment, had crashed to the floor.

实验室中央摆放着一个木质和玻璃制成的大型通风橱，它是我们的骄傲，也是我们免遭毒气毒死的唯一屏障。盐酸本身并没有什么毒性：它就像那种从远处就大声叫嚣着扑向你的敌人，因此很容易就能躲开。它的气味极其刺鼻，凡是能躲开的人都会毫不犹豫地逃离；而且你绝对不会把它错认成别的什么东西，因为只要吸一口，你的鼻子就会像爱森斯坦电影里的马一样，喷出两缕短促的白烟，嘴里也会感到酸涩，就像咬了一口柠檬一样。尽管我们很小心地戴着通风橱，酸气还是弥漫了所有房间：墙纸变色了，门把手和金属部件变得暗淡粗糙，时不时还会传来一声令人毛骨悚然的闷响：可能是钉子被腐蚀穿了，也可能是公寓某个角落里的一幅画掉到了地上。

So we were dissolving tin in hydrochloric acid. Then the solution had to be concentrated to a particular specific weight and left to crystallize by cooling. The stannous chloride separated in small, pretty prisms, colorless and transparent. Since the crystallization was slow, it required many receptacles, and since hydrochloric acid corrodes all metals, these receptacles had to be glass or ceramic. In the period when there were many orders, we had to mobilize reserve receptacles, in which for that matter Emilio’s house was rich: a soup tureen, an enameled iron pressure cooker, an Art Nouveau chandelier, and a chamber pot.

于是我们把锡溶解在盐酸里。然后，溶液必须浓缩到特定的比重，冷却后使其结晶。氯化亚锡析出成细小漂亮的棱柱状晶体，无色透明。由于结晶过程缓慢，需要很多容器，而盐酸会腐蚀所有金属，所以这些容器必须是玻璃或陶瓷的。在订单很多的那段时间，我们不得不动用备用容器，埃米利奥家里的备用容器可谓琳琅满目：汤盅、搪瓷铁制压力锅、新艺术风格的吊灯，甚至还有便壶。

The morning after, the chloride is gathered and set to drain, and you must be very careful not to touch it with your hands or it saddles you with a truly disgusting smell. This salt, in itself, is odorless, but it reacts in some manner with the skin, perhaps reducing the keratin’s disulfide bridges and giving off a persistent metallic stench that for several days announces to all that you are a chemist. It is aggressive but also delicate, like certain unpleasant sports opponents who whine when they lose: you can’t force it, you have to let it dry out in the air in its own good time. If you try to warm it up, even in the mildest manner, for example, with a hair dryer or on the radiator, it loses its crystallization water, becomes opaque, and foolish customers no longer want it. Foolish because it would suit them fine: with less water there is more tin and therefore more of a yield; but that’s how it is, the customer is always right, especially when he knows little chemistry, as is precisely the case with mirror manufacturers.

第二天早上，收集氯化物并沥干，务必小心，切勿用手接触，否则会沾染上一股令人作呕的气味。这种盐本身无味，但会与皮肤发生某种反应，或许会还原角蛋白的二硫键，散发出一种挥之不去的金属臭味，持续数日，仿佛在向所有人宣告你是一位化学家。它既强势又脆弱，就像某些输了就抱怨连连的讨厌对手：你不能强迫它，只能让它在空气中自然风干。如果你试图加热它，哪怕是最温和的方式，例如用吹风机或暖气片，它也会失去结晶水，变得浑浊，愚蠢的顾客也就不再想要它了。他们愚蠢，因为这东西其实很适合他们：水少了，锡就多了，因此产量也更高；但事实就是如此，顾客永远是对的，尤其是在他对化学知之甚少的情况下，就像镜子制造商的情况一样。

That’s the literature of chemistry with a capital L , proof that in sensitive hands any scientific subject can be made to soar. Unfortunately, I have to get back to earth and back to basics. In fact, I should put up a sign: PEDAGOGY AHEAD .

这就是化学领域的经典著作，证明只要运用得当，任何科学学科都能蓬勃发展。可惜，我得回归现实，回归基础。事实上，我应该立个牌子：前方教学讲解。

The premise of this book, as its title says, is that writing is how we think our way into a discipline, organize our thoughts about it and generate new ideas. I’ve left the premise largely unspoken, not wishing to repeat the same obvious point—that Darwin, for instance, was helped to arrive at a coherent theory about the Amblyrhynchus cristatus by putting his observations on paper, or that Rachel Carson clarified her hunches about “the sunless sea” by writing her way down into “these deep, dark waters, with all their mysteries and unsolved problems.” Only in the chapter called “Writing Mathematics” did I document the learning process with classroom examples.

正如书名所示，本书的前提是：写作是我们思考进入某一学科、整理相关思路并产生新想法的方式。我并未过多赘述这一前提，以免重复那些显而易见的观点——例如，达尔文正是通过将观察记录下来才得以构建关于灰背蜻蜓（Amblyrhynchus cristatus）的连贯理论；又如，蕾切尔·卡森正是通过写作深入“这片深邃黑暗的水域，探寻其中的奥秘和未解之谜”，从而澄清了她对“无光之海”的种种猜想。只有在题为“数学写作”的章节中，我才用课堂实例记录了这一学习过程。

I want to do that one more time, taking chemistry as my model. I’ve chosen it partly to humor my sense of symmetry: This book originated with a phone call from a chemistry professor, and it opens with my heretical failure to learn the subject as a boy. But mainly I’ve chosen chemistry because it’s typical of all the sciences that use numbers, signs and symbols as a language and therefore don’t seem to lend themselves to writing.

我想再做一次这样的尝试，这次以化学为范例。我选择化学，部分原因是为了迎合我的对称感：这本书的缘起是一位化学教授打来的电话，而开篇也讲述了我小时候学习化学的“异端”失败经历。但主要原因在于，我选择化学是因为它代表了所有以数字、符号和标记作为语言的科学，因此似乎并不适合用文字来表达。

Writing, however, is one of the most powerful tools that science education possesses; a student can reason his way with words toward the solution of a problem and his teacher can watch him do it, or not do it. Although the following examples come from chemistry, you can adapt them to physics, biology, engineering, psychology and every other discipline where laboratory experiment and observation are a big part of the learning process. Just change the terminology to fit your field.

然而，写作是科学教育中最强大的工具之一；学生可以运用文字进行推理，逐步找到问题的解决方法，而老师则可以观察他如何解决问题，或者不解决问题。虽然以下示例来自化学领域，但您可以将其应用于物理、生物、工程、心理学以及其他任何以实验和观察为重要学习环节的学科。只需根据您所在的领域更改术语即可。

How does someone write chemistry? Here are two explanations that I like, taken from The Journal of Chemical Education . Chemistry teachers are now beginning to insist on writing from their students, and these two women are obviously leaders of the trend.

化学论文应该怎么写？以下是我个人比较喜欢的两种解释，摘自《化学教育期刊》。现在越来越多的化学老师开始要求学生用文字作答，而这两位老师显然是这一趋势的引领者。

The first professor, Estelle K. Meislich, of Bergen Community College, Paramus, New Jersey, begins her article by raising the most common bugaboo that science teachers worry about: “Is there some way of requiring good writing from students that will not diminish the science content?” The concern behind the question is twofold: that teaching writing will take time away from teaching chemistry, and that writing in the sciences is “not the same” as writing in the humanities.

第一位教授，来自新泽西州帕拉姆斯卑尔根社区学院的埃斯特尔·K·梅斯利希，在文章开头提出了科学教师最常担心的问题：“有没有办法既能要求学生具备良好的写作能力，又不会削弱科学内容？”这个问题背后的担忧有两个方面：一是教授写作会占用教授化学的时间；二是科学写作与人文写作“并不相同”。

Tackling the question, Professor Meislich writes: “Here is a method I have used successfully for the past eight years in courses for both chemistry majors and nonmajors. On every examination I ask at least one and often several questions that require a written response. Students are told that their answers must be written in ‘acceptable’ English for credit. If I decide that a scientifically correct response is poorly written, the student cannot get credit for the correct answer until it is rewritten in correct English.

针对这个问题，梅斯利希教授写道：“过去八年来，我在化学专业和非专业学生的课程中都成功运用了以下方法。每次考试，我都会至少提出一个，通常是几个需要书面回答的问题。我会告诉学生，他们的答案必须用‘合格的’英语书写才能获得分数。如果我认为一个科学上正确的答案写得不好，那么学生必须用正确的英语重新书写，才能获得分数。”

“The student has one week to return the rewritten paper for credit. During this time students are encouraged to meet with a writing instructor for help in rewriting. (I send the writing instructor a copy of the examination with correctly written answers to prepare him or her for students’ requests for help.) Of course incorrect answers, no matter how well written, cannot be rewritten for credit.

学生有一周时间提交重写的论文以获得分数。在此期间，我们鼓励学生与写作指导老师会面，寻求重写方面的帮助。（我会将一份带有正确答案的试卷发送给写作指导老师，以便他们为学生的求助做好准备。）当然，错误的答案，无论写得多么好，都不能重写以获得分数。

“A paper that requires a rewritten answer will have two grades. The first one is for the originally submitted examination. The second grade, shown in parentheses, is the one that the student will receive if an acceptable rewritten answer is returned on time…. Once students accept the fact that correct but poorly written answers are unacceptable, most of them write more carefully. Eventually very few of them have to rewrite at all. In this way, writing becomes an integral part of the course without diminishing the chemical content.”

“需要重写的试卷将有两个成绩。第一个成绩是针对最初提交的试卷。第二个成绩（括号内所示）是学生按时提交合格重写答案后获得的成绩……一旦学生接受了正确但写得不好的答案是不可接受的这一事实，他们中的大多数人就会更加认真地写作。最终，只有极少数人需要重写。这样，写作就成为课程不可或缺的一部分，而不会降低课程的化学内容。”

Professor Meislich lists four kinds of questions that she asks on exams in her general and organic chemistry course for chemistry majors and her introductory course for nonmajors. One is a multiple-choice question with a twist: No credit is given for the right answer unless it’s accompanied by a correct explanation. Typical questions are:

梅斯利希教授列出了她在面向化学专业学生的普通化学和有机化学课程以及面向非化学专业学生的入门课程考试中提出的四种题型。其中一种是带有特殊规则的选择题：只有给出正确答案并附上正确解释才能得分。典型题型如下：

1. Which substance has a higher boiling point, CH 3 CH 2 OH or CH 3 OCH 3 ?

1. CH3CH2OH 和 CH3OCH3 哪个物质的沸点更高？

2. Which has a smaller ionization energy, Na or Cs?

2. 钠和铯哪个电离能更小？

In another kind of question she asks students to explain why a given statement is false. Two such statements are:

她提出的另一种问题是要求学生解释为什么某个陈述是错误的。以下是两个这样的陈述：

1. According to modern atomic theory, electrons travel around the nucleus in well-defined orbits.

1. 根据现代原子理论，电子围绕原子核沿明确的轨道运动。

2. As more accurate instruments are constructed, scientists will be able to measure simultaneously the exact location and momentum of an electron.

2. 随着更精确的仪器被制造出来，科学家们将能够同时测量电子的确切位置和动量。

The third type of question requires students to devise an experiment. For example:

第三类问题要求学生设计实验。例如：

How can you decide experimentally which layer in a separatory funnel is organic and which is aqueous? Describe what you would do, what you would see, and what you would conclude.

如何通过实验确定分液漏斗中哪一层是有机层，哪一层是水层？描述你的实验步骤、观察结果和结论。

The fourth type of question asks for a brief essay. A typical essay topic is:

第四种题型要求写一篇短文。一个典型的作文题目是：

Living systems are more complex than nonliving systems, yet life started and exists on this planet. Explain why the existence of life does not violate the second law of thermodynamics.

生命系统比非生命系统更复杂，但生命却起源于地球并一直存在于地球上。请解释为什么生命的存在并不违反热力学第二定律。

Summing up her principles of writing to learn, Professor Meislich says: “Multiple-choice questions are very popular ways of testing knowledge, especially in classes with large numbers of students. However, a more complete understanding is demonstrated by the ability to explain. From the written explanations we get a better idea of the depth of the students’ understanding. We can also learn about their possible misconceptions. Thus, written communication becomes an integral part of the course in a very direct way, with rapid feedback and the opportunity to correct errors in a nonpunitive manner.

梅斯利希教授总结了她关于写作学习的原则，她说：“选择题是测试知识的常用方法，尤其是在学生人数众多的课堂上。然而，更全面的理解体现在解释能力上。通过书面解释，我们可以更好地了解学生理解的深度，也能发现他们可能存在的误解。因此，书面交流以一种非常直接的方式成为课程不可或缺的一部分，它能提供快速反馈，并有机会以非惩罚性的方式纠正错误。”

“The ability to write well is a skill that students should be prepared to use in all courses. That is why I do not accept poorly written English in my chemistry classes.” Nor, I might add, does she accept it from herself.

“良好的写作能力是学生在所有课程中都应该掌握的技能。正因如此，我的化学课上绝不接受糟糕的英语写作。” 我还要补充一点，她自己也同样不接受糟糕的英语写作。

The second professor, Naola VanOrden, of Sacramento City College, in California, notes that the inability of science students to write is a loss both to them and to society. Because science students gradually lose their freshman writing skills, she says, “employers complain that science graduates are technically competent but can’t communicate. They are able to make reams of calculations but they can’t explain the purpose for, or the significance of, those calculations.” The problem was addressed by a recent national meeting of the American Chemical Society, which concluded that it had to be solved by chemistry departments, not by English departments.

第二位教授，来自加州萨克拉门托城市学院的娜奥拉·范奥登指出，理科学生写作能力的不足对他们自身和社会都是一种损失。她说，由于理科学生会逐渐丧失大一时的写作技能，“雇主抱怨理科毕业生技术能力强，但沟通能力差。他们能做出大量的计算，却无法解释这些计算的目的或意义。”美国化学学会最近召开的一次全国性会议也讨论了这个问题，并得出结论：这个问题必须由化学系解决，而不是英语系。

“To motivate chemistry students to practice writing skills,” Professor VanOrden says, “we must convince them that chemical writing is important. Writing assignments must be more than the usual end-of-chapter questions, which can be answered by copying the appropriate sentences from the chapter. They must require a synthesis of the concept fragments taught in the chapter.” Above all, those assignments should have reality. “Just as we find that chemical calculations are more meaningful to students if they are related to the real world, so are chemical writing assignments more valuable if they illustrate real-life problems.”

“为了激励化学专业的学生练习写作技巧，”范奥登教授说，“我们必须让他们认识到化学写作的重要性。写作作业不能仅仅是章节末尾的习题，因为这些习题只需复制章节中的相应句子即可作答。写作作业必须要求学生综合运用章节中讲解的概念片段。” 最重要的是，这些作业应该与现实生活紧密相关。“正如我们发现，如果化学计算与现实世界联系起来，对学生来说就更有意义一样，如果化学写作作业能够阐明实际问题，它们也会更有价值。”

Where can such vignettes be found? Professor VanOrden reports that after years of searching she hit upon a type of brief writing assignment that succeeds because her students consider it an important part of her course. “These assignments are always related to the text concepts being studied,” she says, “and many of them are examples of practical applications of chemical concepts. Students must first solve a chemical problem; then they must explain, discuss or apply their results.”

哪里可以找到这样的案例呢？范奥登教授表示，经过多年的摸索，她最终找到了一种短篇写作作业，这种作业之所以成功，是因为学生们认为它是课程的重要组成部分。“这些作业总是与正在学习的课文概念相关，”她说，“其中很多都是化学概念的实际应用案例。学生们必须先解决一个化学问题；然后，他们必须解释、讨论或应用他们的结果。”

At first her students are less than delighted by this prospect. “They complain that the assignments require too much time,” Professor VanOrden says, “and also that ‘this is a chemistry class, not an English class.’ But by the third or fourth assignment they realize that how they write really does matter. Since most of my students are very serious and competitive, their writing quickly improves and many of them become quite creative. Perhaps the best evaluation of all is that, near the end of the semester, students bring me questions for future writing assignments. They have caught some of the vision of what education is trying to accomplish.”

起初，她的学生们对这种前景并不热衷。“他们抱怨作业太费时间，”范奥登教授说，“还说‘这是化学课，不是英语课’。但到了第三四次作业，他们就意识到写作方式确实很重要。由于我的学生大多非常认真且好胜，他们的写作水平很快就提高了，许多人也变得很有创造力。也许最好的评价是，临近学期末，学生们会向我提出一些关于未来写作作业的问题。他们已经领悟到教育的真谛。”

What kind of assignment would provoke a “quite creative” response? Here’s one of Professor VanOrden’s:

什么样的作业会激发出“极富创造力”的回应？以下是范奥登教授布置的其中一项作业：

You are the manager of River City Pet Store. A customer is very distraught because the fish in her backyard fish pond are dying. When she brings you a sample of the water, you find out that the pH of the water is 8.2, but this species of fish lives best in water of 6.8. (1) Select a good buffer system for a fish pond. (2) Calculate the quantities of buffer components that should be added to the pond to maintain the pH at 6.8. (3) Write a letter to the customer telling her how to treat her fish pond. (Make sure the buffer chemicals do not kill the fish.)

你是河城宠物店的经理。一位顾客非常沮丧，因为她家后院鱼塘里的鱼正在死亡。她给你带来了一份水样，你发现水的pH值为8.2，但这种鱼最适宜生活在pH值为6.8的水中。(1) 为鱼塘选择合适的缓冲系统。(2) 计算需要添加到鱼塘中的缓冲剂的用量，以将pH值维持在6.8。(3) 写一封信给这位顾客，告诉她如何处理她的鱼塘。（确保缓冲剂不会杀死鱼。）

One student’s response, as described by Professor VanOrden, took this form: “She selected the dihydrogen phosphate-monohydrogen phosphate buffer system and calculated the mole ratio necessary for a buffer of pH 6.8. Then she calculated the quantity of buffer components necessary to maintain the pH of five gallons of the pond water constant at pH 6.8. Next the student ‘prepared’ a product containing enough buffer for 1000 gallons of pond water. Then she ‘marketed’ the product under the trade name ‘Aqua-lock.’ The letter she wrote to her customer is as follows:”

范奥登教授描述了一位学生的应对方法：“她选择了磷酸二氢盐-磷酸一氢盐缓冲体系，并计算了pH值为6.8所需的缓冲溶液的摩尔比。然后，她计算了维持5加仑池塘水pH值恒定在6.8所需的缓冲溶液组分的量。接下来，这位学生‘配制’了一种含有足够1000加仑池塘水使用的缓冲溶液的产品。然后，她以‘Aqua-lock’的商品名‘销售’了该产品。她写给客户的信如下：”

Dear Mrs. Frame:

尊敬的弗雷姆夫人：

The completed analysis of your pond water indicates that a pH adjustment is needed to provide an adequate environment for your fish. Fortunately, this problem can be easily corrected with one of our products, Aqua-lock, pH 6.8. Aqua-lock is available in one-gallon jugs for only $25.95. I recommend that 5.5 quarts of the product be used immediately on your pond and once a month thereafter. Periodic maintenance thereafter could be cut down if you measure your pH and add the product only when the pH changes. Accordingly, I also recommend that you purchase Wardleys’ Jr. pH Kit (instructions included) for only $14.98.

您的池塘水质分析结果显示，需要调整 pH 值才能为您的鱼儿提供适宜的生存环境。幸运的是，我们的产品 Aqua-lock（pH 6.8）可以轻松解决这个问题。Aqua-lock 以一加仑装出售，售价仅为 25.95 美元。我建议您立即在池塘中使用 5.5 夸脱（约 5.4 升）的 Aqua-lock，之后每月使用一次。如果您定期测量 pH 值，并在 pH 值发生变化时才添加产品，则可以减少后续维护的次数。因此，我还建议您购买 Wardleys 的 Jr. pH 值测试套装（内含使用说明），售价仅为 14.98 美元。

River City is committed to customer service. If we can be of further help, please feel free to call on us at any time.

River City致力于提供优质的客户服务。如果您需要任何帮助，请随时联系我们。

Sincerely,

真挚地，

Valerie Ayala, Manager

经理 Valerie Ayala

As for the fear that teaching writing will take time away from teaching chemistry, Professor VanOrden says she makes no effort to teach grammar but does note errors of construction—sentences, for instance, that are ambiguous or awkward. “Help is available in the English writing lab,” she points out, “but until I began grading writing assignments my students didn’t take the time to get help because they didn’t consider writing to be important to chemistry. Many of them still need help with the mechanics of sentence construction. We hope to solve this problem by establishing a drop-in writing lab just for science students.”

至于有人担心写作课会占用化学课的教学时间，范奥登教授表示，她并不刻意教授语法，但会指出一些句子结构上的错误——例如，含义模糊或表达生硬的句子。“英语写作中心可以提供帮助，”她指出，“但在我开始批改写作作业之前，我的学生们并不重视写作，因为他们认为写作对化学学习并不重要。他们中的许多人仍然需要提高句子结构方面的知识。我们希望通过设立一个专门面向理科学生的写作辅导中心来解决这个问题。”

But what Professor VanOrden is ultimately after is something that goes well beyond grammar or syntax, and the two sentences in her article that I liked most were these:

但范奥登教授最终追求的远不止语法或句法，她文章中我最喜欢的两句话是：

“I believe that writing is an effective means of improving thinking skills because a person must mentally process ideas in order to write an explanation. Writing also improves self-esteem because mentally processed ideas then belong to the writer and not just to the teacher or the textbook author.”

我认为写作是提高思维能力的有效途径，因为一个人必须经过思维加工才能写出解释性的文章。写作还能提升自尊心，因为经过思维加工的想法属于写作者本人，而不仅仅是属于老师或教科书作者。

With the word “self-esteem” Professor VanOrden put her finger on one of the most painful elements in writing. I recalled what Professor Gover told me when I asked him why even the science faculty at Gustavus Adolphus College had so strongly supported a writing-across-the-curriculum program. “Those of us who teach science and other technical subjects,” he said, “have always felt insecure about writing. We knew we could deal well with ideas, but somehow when it came to putting words on paper it never came out right, and we heard about it, usually from our English teacher.”

范奥登教授用“自尊”一词，一针见血地指出了写作中最令人痛苦的因素之一。我回想起戈弗教授曾对我说过的话。当时我问他，为什么古斯塔夫·阿道夫学院的理科教师们如此大力支持跨学科写作项目。“我们这些教科学和其他技术科目的人，”他说，“一直对写作缺乏自信。我们知道自己能很好地处理想法，但不知为何，一旦要把文字写在纸上，就总是写不好，而且我们经常会听到别人的批评，通常是我们的英语老师。”

Who of us doesn’t recognize that lament in some form from our own school days? Being made to feel dumb is not conducive to learning.

我们当中谁没有在学生时代经历过类似的抱怨呢？被嘲笑愚蠢不利于学习。

I believe, however, that writers often conspire in their own insecurity. (By “writers” I also mean every student of high school age and older who writes a paper of any kind.) Teachers of writing are dismally aware of the inclination of writers to equate the worth of their writing with the worth of who they are. The equation goes: “You think this is a terrible paper, therefore you must think I’m a terrible person.”

然而，我认为，写作者常常会因为自身的不安全感而自相矛盾。（我这里说的“写作者”也包括所有高中及以上年龄段、撰写任何类型文章的学生。）写作教师们都深知，写作者往往会将自己作品的价值与自身价值划等号。这种等式是：“你觉得这篇文章很糟糕，所以你肯定觉得我这个人也很糟糕。”

The thought is natural, perhaps almost inevitable: when we write we put some part of our self on paper for other people to judge. But finally that thought is a self-indulgence. Writers who think they are being criticized when only their writing is being criticized are beyond a teacher’s reach. Writing can only be learned when a writer coldly separates himself from what he has written and looks at it with the objectivity of a plumber examining a newly piped bathroom to see if he got all the joints tight.

这种想法很自然，或许几乎是不可避免的：写作时，我们把一部分自我写在纸上，任由他人评判。但归根结底，这种想法是一种自我放纵。如果作家误以为自己受到了批评，而实际上批评的只是他们的写作本身，那么老师就无能为力了。写作的精髓在于，作家能够冷静地将自己与作品区分开来，像水管工检查新装好的浴室管道是否严丝合缝那样，客观地审视自己的作品。

Do I hear a gasp? How dare I compare writing to plumbing? I dare. Both of them are crafts, with their own set of tools, which will do the jobs they were designed to do if they are used correctly.

我听到有人倒吸一口凉气了吗？我怎么敢把写作和管道维修相提并论？我就是敢。它们都是技艺，都有各自的工具，只要使用得当，就能完成它们各自的工作。

So I would say this to everyone who feels that his main aptitude is for science or technology, or for any other field that lies outside the humanities, and that therefore he can’t write:

所以，我想对那些认为自己主要擅长科学、技术或其他任何非人文领域的学生说：

Learn to use the tools without fear. They are not some kind of secret apparatus owned by the English teacher or any other teacher. They are simple mechanisms for putting your thoughts on paper. Enjoy finding out how they work. Take as much pleasure in what an active verb will do for you as in what a mathematical formula will do, or a computer, or a centrifuge. The self-esteem will then take care of itself. Any time you reason your way through a complex scientific idea and put it in writing so that it’s clear to somebody else, you can feel as good as Norman Mailer—and you should.

学会无所畏惧地使用这些工具。它们并非英语老师或其他老师的秘密武器，而只是将你的想法记录在纸上的简单机制。享受探索它们运作方式的过程。像享受数学公式、电脑或离心机带来的乐趣一样，享受动词的表达带来的成就感。如此一来，自信心自然会油然而生。每当你理清一个复杂的科学概念，并将其清晰地写下来，让其他人也能理解时，你就能像诺曼·梅勒一样感到无比自豪——而且你也应该如此。

# ↩

12. Worlds of Music

12. 音乐世界

In 1975 when I wrote my book On Writing Well I had a definite model in mind—a book I hoped mine might resemble. The model, however, wasn’t about writing. It was Alec Wilder’s American Popular Song , a book about music, which had been published a year or two earlier. Ordinarily a nonfiction writer takes as his model (if he takes one at all) a work that’s related to his subject. American Popular Song made me realize that the subject—what a book is about—isn’t as important as the qualities of mind or personality that the writer brings to it.

1975年，我写《写作之道》时，心中有一个明确的范例——我希望自己的作品能与之媲美。然而，这个范例并非关于写作本身，而是亚历克·怀尔德的《美国流行歌曲》，一本关于音乐的书，比我早一两年出版。通常，非虚构类作家会选择一本与主题相关的作品作为范例（如果他们真的会选择范例的话）。《美国流行歌曲》让我意识到，主题——一本书的内容——远不如作者赋予它的思维方式或人格特质重要。

I wasn’t surprised that I liked Wilder’s book. I already knew him as a composer of classical pieces and of songs like “While We’re Young” that were fixtures in the repertory of cabaret singers. I had also read many interviews that caught the broad range of his musical intelligence. But the reason why his book appealed to me had far older roots. To explain why, I have to make one last trip back to my childhood—to the teacher who gave me what has been my single most enjoyable body of information.

我喜欢怀尔德的书，这并不让我感到意外。我早就知道他是一位古典音乐作曲家，也创作过像《当我们年轻时》这样脍炙人口的歌曲，这些歌曲曾是歌舞厅歌手的保留曲目。我还读过许多关于他的访谈，从中领略了他广博的音乐才华。然而，这本书吸引我的原因却远不止于此。要解释个中缘由，我必须最后一次回到我的童年——回到那位给予我人生中最宝贵知识的老师身边。

Her name was Editha Messer, and she was the typical music teacher who came once a week to give piano lessons. Except that she wasn’t typical; she had a perfect ear and she could—and would—play any kind of music. What really made her untypical, however, was that she knew when to throw away the rules of how music ought to be taught.

她名叫伊迪莎·梅塞尔，是一位典型的每周来上一次钢琴课的音乐老师。但她又不寻常；她拥有极佳的乐感，能够——而且也愿意——演奏任何类型的音乐。然而，真正让她与众不同的是，她懂得何时应该打破音乐教学的固有规则。

I was probably ten or eleven when my lessons began. They consisted of the standard pedagogical fare: Hanon’s horrible scales, Diller and Quaile’s dreary little children’s tunes, the great composers’ chestnuts like MacDowell’s “To a Wild Rose,” a work as hard to get rid of as the flower that it extols. I hated them all and hated having to learn and memorize them. I especially hated trying to read music. It was so much easier to ask Mrs. Messer to play the song and then try to fake it by ear.

我大概十岁或十一岁的时候开始上课。课程内容都是些老套的教学曲目：哈农那可怕的音阶，迪勒和奎尔那些枯燥乏味的儿歌，还有一些伟大作曲家的经典之作，比如麦克道尔的《致野玫瑰》，这首曲子就像它所赞美的野玫瑰一样，让人难以忘怀。我讨厌所有这些曲子，讨厌学习和背诵它们。我尤其讨厌识谱。还不如让梅塞尔太太弹奏一遍，然后自己凭耳朵模仿来得容易得多。

Fakery didn’t fool Editha Messer; she heard my every circumvention. But she also heard something else—a boy with a natural ear trying to disentangle himself from MacDowell’s wild rose and other such strangling vines. She knew her student well, and one day she said, in effect, “You’re never going to learn to read music, so I’m going to teach you the chords. Once you know the principles of harmony you’ll be able to play anything you hear.” She took out a little brown notebook that I can still picture and wrote out C-E-G and a few other fundamental chords in the key of C. She played them so that I could hear them and see what they looked like. Then she explained how they functioned within the key of C and in relation to the other major and minor keys. Suddenly I was in a world that I never knew existed but that seemed inevitable as soon as I heard it. Suddenly music lessons became fun. I loved how elegant the system was. Countless harmonies were waiting for me in those eighty-eight keys. All I had to do was find them.

弄虚作假骗不了伊迪莎·梅塞尔；她听出了我所有的障眼法。但她也听出了别的东西——一个天生乐感的男孩正努力摆脱麦克道尔笔下那些缠绕着他的野玫瑰和其他类似藤蔓的束缚。她很了解她的学生，有一天，她实际上是这样说的：“你永远也学不会识谱，所以我教你和弦。一旦你掌握了和声的原理，你就能演奏任何你听到的曲子。”她拿出一个我至今仍能想起的棕色小笔记本，写下了C-E-G以及C大调中的其他几个基本和弦。她弹奏出来，让我能听到并看到它们的样子。然后她解释了这些和弦在C大调中的作用，以及它们与其他大小调的关系。突然间，我进入了一个我从未了解过的世界，但当我听到这些和弦时，它似乎又不可避免地出现了。音乐课突然变得有趣起来。我喜欢这套体系的精妙之处。那八十八个调里蕴藏着无数的和声，我所要做的就是找到它们。

So began a lifetime of sitting where I could watch the hands of jazz pianists and listening to their records and appropriating chords that excited me with their texture and their tension. Editha Messer had given me the tools to be my own teacher, and for a long time that sufficed—until the day at Yale when I first heard Willie Ruff’s partner, Dwike Mitchell. The harmonies coming out of his piano were incredibly rich cousins of the ones I had begged, borrowed and stolen and thought were good enough. I knew it was time to go back to school, and Mitchell has been my teacher ever since.

于是，我开始了漫长的爵士钢琴学习生涯：坐在能观察爵士钢琴家手部动作的地方，聆听他们的唱片，并借鉴那些质感和张力令我心动的和弦。伊迪莎·梅塞尔教会了我如何自学，很长一段时间，这对我来说就足够了——直到在耶鲁大学的那一天，我第一次听到了威利·拉夫的搭档德威克·米切尔的演奏。他钢琴中流露出的和声，与我苦苦钻研、借用甚至“偷师”过的、自认为已经足够好的和声，有着无比丰富的层次。我知道是时候重返校园了，而米切尔从此成为了我的老师。

That relationship has taught me as much about writing as it has about music. I found that the lives of Mitchell and Ruff—both as artists and as teachers—interested me on so many levels that I began to write about them, first in the New Yorker piece about their trip to introduce jazz to China (described in Chapter 3) and eventually in an entire book, Willie and Dwike . My vocation and my avocation merged—one of the best things that can happen to a writer. Writing about music also made me a better musician. The need to write clearly about an art form that the reader can never see or hear, one that evaporates with the playing of every note, forced me to think harder about the structure of music—about what I was trying to learn.

这段经历教会我的写作技巧和音乐知识一样多。我发现米切尔和拉夫的生活——无论是作为艺术家还是教师——都深深吸引着我，于是我开始写关于他们的文章。最初是在《纽约客》上发表了一篇关于他们前往中国推广爵士乐的文章（第三章有详细描述），最终写成了一整本书——《威利和德威克》。我的职业和爱好合二为一——这对于一个作家来说，无疑是最美好的事情之一。写作也让我成为了一名更优秀的音乐家。由于读者永远无法看到或听到这种艺术形式，它随着每一个音符的演奏而消逝，因此我需要清晰地描述它，这迫使我更深入地思考音乐的结构——思考我究竟想要学习什么。

Was it possible, for instance, to convey something of what happens in a music lesson—what that transaction is like? Here’s a paragraph in which I tried:

例如，是否有可能描述一下音乐课上发生的事情——那种互动是什么样的？以下是我尝试描述的一段话：

I hear chords coming out of Mitchell’s piano that make me quiver. No matter how many complex chords I already knew or have since learned, there is no end of new ones: chords that I never imagined and would never be able to find by myself. When I learn a new chord on Mitchell’s piano I still can’t believe that it will also exist on my piano, and I hurry home to try it out. But every discovery raises new questions. Having learned a chord that’s exactly right for a certain song in a certain key, I’m eager to own it in every other key, and I start by transposing it up a halftone, or down, and it disappears: a shift of only half a tone has robbed it of whatever made it unique. I bring this mystery to Mitchell and he says, “That chord only works in D flat.” His ear knows what every chord sounds like in every key at every register. “It’s the vibrations,” he says. “How the notes vibrate against each other is always different.” He talks a lot about vibrations. When he and I analyze chords we are like two lepidopterists poring over a tray of brilliant butterflies, delighting in their infinite variety and their subtle gradations of color. Mitchell also talks a lot about pressure: the pressure of the fingers on the keys. I’ve begun to hear how a chord can sound wrong in any number of ways, even when the notes are correct, and how Mitchell’s chords always sound right. He also talks about posture—the stillness of Horowitz is a marvel to him. Most of all, he talks about feeling. He often mentions some pianist who was technically flawless but who “might as well have not played at all.” Emotion, to him, is the crucial ingredient, and music is a total commitment. In his conversation and his concerns I glimpse what it is to be an artist and not just a musician.

我听到米切尔的钢琴里传出和弦，它们让我心潮澎湃。无论我之前知道多少复杂的和弦，或者后来又学到了多少，新的和弦总是层出不穷：有些和弦我从未想象过，也永远不可能自己找到。每当我在米切尔的钢琴上学到一个新和弦，我仍然难以置信它竟然也存在于我的钢琴上，于是我迫不及待地回家尝试。但每一次发现都会引发新的疑问。当我学会一个和弦，它完美契合某首歌在某个调上的演奏时，我渴望把它运用到其他所有调上。我尝试将它向上或向下移调半音，结果它就消失了：仅仅半音的移动就剥夺了它原本的独特之处。我把这个谜团告诉米切尔，他却说：“这个和弦只适用于降D调。”他的耳朵对每个和弦在每个调、每个音区听起来都了如指掌。“关键在于振动，”他说。 “音符之间的振动方式总是千差万别。”他经常谈到振动。我和他一起分析和弦时，就像两位蝴蝶学家仔细观察一盘色彩斑斓的蝴蝶，为它们无穷无尽的种类和微妙的色彩渐变而欣喜不已。米切尔也经常谈到力度：手指在琴键上的压力。我开始明白，即使音符本身正确，和弦也可能因为各种各样的原因而听起来不对劲，而米切尔的和弦听起来总是那么完美。他还谈到姿势——霍洛维茨的静止状态令他惊叹。最重要的是，他谈到感觉。他经常提到一些技术完美无瑕的钢琴家，但他们的演奏“仿佛根本没演奏过”。对他来说，情感是至关重要的因素，音乐是一种全身心的投入。在他的谈话和思考中，我得以窥见成为一名艺术家，而不仅仅是一名音乐家的意义所在。

What to play, as distinct from how to play, was never a problem: I’m a show tune addict. I got hooked at an early age when my parents went to Cole Porter musicals like Anything Goes and brought home and played the sheet music of “You’re the Top,” “I Get a Kick Out of You” and other “gems from the score.” I was a small boy with three big older sisters; whatever sophistication existed in the family stopped with them. Porter’s songs didn’t turn me into Maurice Chevalier overnight. But they opened a window into a world of “clever” grownups. I was dazzled by Porter’s lyrics—by the urbane rhymes and the continental allusions, the ironies and the languors. So that’s what it meant to be “sophisticated.”

演奏什么曲子，而不是如何演奏，从来都不是问题：我痴迷于音乐剧。小时候，父母经常去看科尔·波特的音乐剧，比如《万事皆宜》（Anything Goes），然后把《你是最棒的》（You're the Top）、《我为你着迷》（I Get a Kick Out of You）以及其他“乐谱中的瑰宝”的乐谱带回家演奏，我从小就迷上了音乐剧。我当时还是个小男孩，有三个比我大很多的姐姐；家里所有所谓的“世故”都止步于她们。波特的歌曲并没有让我一夜之间变成莫里斯·切瓦利埃（Maurice Chevalier，美国著名歌唱家）。但它们为我打开了一扇窗，让我得以窥见一个“聪明”的成年人的世界。波特的歌词让我着迷——那些优雅的韵律、欧陆风情的典故、讽刺的意味和慵懒的节奏。原来，这就是“世故”的含义。

Soon after that, Fred Astaire put it all together for me. Six Astaire movies rapidly came along, for which some of America’s best songwriters wrote some of their best songs: Swing Time (Jerome Kern and Dorothy Fields); Top Hat, Follow the Fleet and Carefree (Irving Berlin), and Shall We Dance and Damsel in Distress (George and Ira Gershwin). The songs included, for instance, Kern and Fields’s “The Way You Look Tonight” and “A Fine Romance,” Berlin’s “Cheek to Cheek” and “Let’s Face the Music and Dance,” and the Gershwins’ “A Foggy Day” and “They Can’t Take That Away From Me.”

不久之后，弗雷德·阿斯泰尔为我安排好了一切。六部阿斯泰尔电影接踵而至，美国一些最优秀的作曲家也为它们创作了他们最经典的歌曲：《摇摆时代》（杰罗姆·科恩和多萝西·菲尔兹）；《礼帽》、《随舰队》和《无忧无虑》（欧文·柏林）；以及《谈谈情，跳跳舞》和《落难佳人》（乔治·格什温和艾拉·格什温）。这些歌曲包括科恩和菲尔兹创作的《你今晚的样子》和《美好的浪漫》，柏林创作的《脸贴脸》和《让我们面对音乐跳舞》，以及格什温兄弟创作的《雾蒙蒙的一天》和《他们无法夺走我的爱》。

What inspired the writers to reach such heights was that they were writing for Astaire. They knew that nobody would ever sing those songs quite so well again, and they were right—the Brunswick records that Astaire made of the twenty-eight numbers from those films are a B.A. education in the art of writing and singing songs. Listening to them over and over, I learned from Astaire about such intangibles as timing and taste. But what anchored his achievement was his respect for the melody and the lyric—what the writers were trying to say. The result, it seemed to me, was nothing less than perfection. To this day (the songs are now on an LP album) I wouldn’t want a single note or a single word of those songs to be written or sung differently.

激励词曲作者们达到如此高度的，是因为他们为阿斯泰尔创作歌曲。他们知道，没有人能像他那样完美地演绎这些歌曲，而他们的预感是正确的——阿斯泰尔为布伦瑞克唱片公司录制的28首电影歌曲，堪称歌曲创作和演唱艺术的典范。一遍又一遍地聆听，我从阿斯泰尔身上学到了诸如节奏和品味等难以捉摸的技巧。但真正奠定他成就的，是他对旋律和歌词的尊重——他对词曲作者想要表达的内容的深刻理解。在我看来，最终的成果堪称完美。时至今日（这些歌曲现在已收录在LP唱片中），我仍然希望这些歌曲的每一个音符、每一个字都保持原样，无需任何改动。

From that launching pad I began going to Broadway musicals myself, starting with the buoyant Rodgers and Hart shows of the late thirties and early forties—shows like Babes in Arms, Too Many Girls and Pal Joey , which yielded such songs as “My Funny Valentine,” “I Didn’t Know What Time It Was” and “Bewitched”—and going to all the terrible Hollywood musicals for which Harold Arlen was writing a string of American classics like “Blues in the Night.” After that the American musical theater turned its famous corner, generating shows whose songs actually advanced the plot or developed character, and I saw them all: Kurt Weill and Ira Gershwin’s Lady in the Dark , Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Oklahoma!, Carousel, South Pacific and The King and I , Frank Loesser’s Guys and Dolls , Jule Styne and Stephen Sondheim’s Gypsy , and many more.

从此，我开始亲自去看百老汇音乐剧，最初是上世纪三十年代末四十年代初罗杰斯和哈特创作的那些欢快的作品——比如《娃娃兵》（Babes in Arms）、《太多女孩》（Too Many Girls）和《帕尔·乔伊》（Pal Joey），这些剧目诞生了《我的滑稽情人》（My Funny Valentine）、《我不知道现在几点了》（I Didn't Know What Time It Was）和《着魔》（Bewitched）等经典歌曲——以及哈罗德·阿伦为之创作的一系列糟糕的好莱坞音乐剧，其中不乏像《夜色蓝调》（Blues in the Night）这样的美国经典之作。之后，美国音乐剧迎来了它著名的转折点，开始创作一些歌曲真正推动剧情发展或塑造人物的作品，而我也都看过：库尔特·魏尔和艾拉·格什温的《黑暗中的女士》（Lady in the Dark）、罗杰斯和哈默斯坦的《俄克拉荷马！》（Oklahoma!）、《旋转木马》（Carousel）、《南太平洋》（South Pacific）和《国王与我》（The King and I）、弗兰克·洛瑟的《红男绿女》（Guys and Dolls）、朱尔·斯泰恩和斯蒂芬·桑德海姆的《吉普赛》（Gypsy），等等。

By then I had all the earmarks of a crazed hobbyist, buying every album that reconstructed the score of a bygone show, listening to the records of such custodial singers as Frank Sinatra, Judy Garland and Ella Fitzgerald, who, like Astaire, revered these songs and sang them impeccably. As a result, the music and lyrics of at least a thousand songs from this vast American literature are cross-indexed in my brain, more instantly retrievable than any other information stored in that crowded data base.

那时，我已然成了个狂热的业余爱好者，买遍了所有重现昔日剧目配乐的专辑，反复聆听弗兰克·辛纳屈、朱迪·嘉兰和艾拉·菲茨杰拉德等经典歌手的唱片。他们和阿斯泰尔一样，对这些歌曲推崇备至，并将它们演绎得无可挑剔。结果，至少有一千首来自浩瀚美国音乐宝库的歌曲的旋律和歌词，在我的大脑中形成了交叉索引，比我那拥挤的数据库中存储的任何其他信息都更容易检索。

What every collector wants, of course, is someone who shares his passion, preferably someone of greater erudition. For me that someone was Alec Wilder; American Popular Song was a book I had been waiting for all my life. Its theme is in its subtitle: “The Great Innovators, 1900–1950.” To write his book Wilder examined the sheet music of seventeen thousand songs. From those he selected three hundred in which he felt that the composer pushed into new territory, or at least “maintained the high level of sophisticated craftsmanship” that earlier innovators had established. His focus is on the music, not the lyrics, though he cites the lyrics if necessary, and usually he also provides the music of the passage he is writing about—often just three or four measures where the composer did something he finds unusual or somehow touching. For instance, discussing George and Ira Gershwin’s “A Foggy Day,” Wilder writes:

当然，每位收藏家都渴望找到一位与自己志同道合的人，最好是学识渊博之人。对我而言，这个人就是亚历克·怀尔德；《美国流行歌曲》这本书我期待已久。它的主题就体现在副标题中：“伟大的创新者，1900-1950”。为了撰写此书，怀尔德研究了一万七千首歌曲的乐谱。从中，他挑选了三百首他认为作曲家开拓了新领域，或者至少“保持了早期创新者所建立的高超技艺”的作品。他关注的是音乐而非歌词，尽管如有必要，他也会引用歌词，而且通常还会提供他所论述段落的音乐——通常只是三四个小节，其中作曲家运用了一些他认为不同寻常或令人感动的技巧。例如，在讨论乔治·格什温和艾拉·格什温的《雾蒙蒙的一天》时，怀尔德写道：

It’s extraordinary how constant is [George] Gershwin’s use of repeated notes. They are more usually to be found in his rhythm songs, but are seldom absent, even in a tender ballad like this. For example, the very first three notes are repeated. And the notes accompanying “I viewed the” and “the British” are repeated.

格什温对重复音符的运用之频繁令人惊叹。虽然在他的节奏歌曲中更为常见，但即使在像这样一首柔情似水的民谣中，也几乎从未缺席。例如，开头的三个音符就重复出现。“我观看了”和“英国人”这两个词的伴奏音符也同样重复。

In any type of song but a romantic ballad, Gershwin’s angularity may produce the most effective result. But the proof that there are no hard and fast rules is “A Foggy Day.” For in it there is no step-wise writing, and there are many leaps of fourth and fifth intervals. Yet it remains a most tender and moving, a far from aggressive, song.

除了浪漫情歌之外，格什温的棱角分明的旋律风格在任何类型的歌曲中都可能产生最有效的效果。但《雾都孤儿》这首歌证明了音乐创作并没有绝对的规则。因为这首歌没有采用级进式的谱写，而是运用了大量的四度和五度跳跃。然而，它仍然是一首极其温柔动人、毫不咄咄逼人的歌曲。

I should make it clear that I do not view the repeated notes with alarm. “A Foggy Day,” for instance, has a heartbreak quality, not one note of which would I change. Right away I am captured by the e flat accompanying the word “day.” [The song is in the key of F.] And I am given, as a dividend, the avoidance of the cliché of the diminished chord. Instead, Gershwin uses a minor sixth chord, which is much more winning. And he remains consistent, by moving up another minor third in the melody in his second phrase, to a flat, and also up a fifth again at the end of the phrase.

我必须澄清，我并不对重复的音符感到担忧。例如，《雾蒙蒙的日子》（A Foggy Day）这首歌就有一种令人心碎的特质，而我不会改变其中任何一个音符。我立刻就被伴随“day”这个词的降E音所吸引。[这首歌是F大调。] 更令人惊喜的是，它避免了使用老套的减和弦。格什温用的是小六和弦，这更加动听。而且，他始终保持着这种一致性：在第二乐句中，旋律向上移动了一个小三度，然后降了一个小三度，最后在乐句结尾又向上移动了五度。

At the end of the B section (the song is A-B-A-C ), the drop to the d in the cadence is truly gentle and loving. It’s as personal as the revelation of a secret.

在B段结尾（歌曲的和弦进行是A-B-A-C），音符从高音降到d，这一变化真挚而温柔，如同揭开一个秘密般私密动人。

This is followed by the truly chilling wedding of the word “suddenly” with the two f ’s and the d .

接下来是“突然”这个词与两个 f 和一个 d 之间真正令人不寒而栗的结合。

He then winds it up by extending the last section two measures longer than is customary, in the course of which he writes a pastoral, vulnerable, childlike phrase to go with the beautifully resolving lyric.

然后，他将最后一部分延长了两个小节，以此来结束这首曲子。在这两个小节中，他写了一个田园牧歌式的、脆弱的、孩子气的乐句，与优美的结尾相呼应。

As Ira Gershwin wrote in a different connection, who could ask for anything more? Not I. To have a musical sensibility so finely tuned analyzing three hundred finely wrought songs was as rich a gift as I could have received. Wilder had written his way down into the most minute essence of his subject—down to the individual note. It’s an immensely hard kind of writing, combining a scholar’s precision with an artist’s wonder, and in bringing it off Wilder is both learner and teacher. As a learner he used the act of writing to capture and possess what it is about these songs that sets them apart, and in telling me what he discovered he gave me many new insights into these old friends I thought I knew so well.

正如艾拉·格什温在另一篇文章中所写，还有什么比这更令人满足的呢？反正我并不奢求。能拥有如此敏锐的音乐感知力，去分析三百首精雕细琢的歌曲，这对我来说是莫大的恩赐。怀尔德的写作深入到了他所研究对象的最细微之处——甚至细致到每一个音符。这是一种极其艰辛的写作方式，它融合了学者般的严谨和艺术家般的惊奇，而怀尔德在做到这一点的过程中，既是学习者，也是老师。作为学习者，他通过写作来捕捉并掌握这些歌曲的独特之处；而当他与我分享他的发现时，我对这些我以为早已熟知的老朋友有了全新的认识。

But even that doesn’t explain why I took American Popular Song as my model for On Writing Well . What lingered with me after reading Wilder’s book was his total commitment to his enthusiasms. His book is deeply personal. It’s as if he were saying, “These are some of my likes and dislikes; take ’em or leave ’em. This isn’t a definitive study—it’s just one man’s book.”

但即便如此，也无法解释我为何选择《美国流行歌曲》作为我创作《写作之道》的范本。读完怀尔德的书后，最令我印象深刻的是他对自身爱好的全然投入。他的书充满了浓厚的个人色彩。仿佛他在说：“这些是我的一些喜好和厌恶；信不信由你。这并非权威研究——这只是一个人的书。”

I loved the fact that it was so overwhelmingly one man’s book. I loved its confidence and its prejudices. I also loved Wilder’s pleasure in presenting excellence to his readers; he doesn’t include poor songs in order to shoot them down. That policy connected with my own belief in not teaching by bad example. Except for a few scraps of jargon and pomposity that I put in my books to warn against the prevailing bloatage, I don’t deal in junk. If writing is learned by imitation, I want every learner to imitate the best.

我喜欢这本书完全是作者的个人风格。我喜欢他的自信和偏见。我也喜欢怀尔德乐于向读者呈现佳作；他不会为了贬低而收录劣质歌曲。这种做法与我“不以恶人为榜样”的理念不谋而合。除了为了警示世人如今作品的臃肿而偶尔在书中穿插一些晦涩难懂的术语和故作高深的辞藻之外，我从不堆砌垃圾。如果写作是通过模仿来学习的，我希望每个学习者都能模仿最优秀的作品。

Thus I saw from American Popular Song that it might be possible to write a book about writing that would be just one man’s book. I would write confidently from my own convictions and experiences—take ’em or leave ’em—and to illustrate my points I would present passages by writers I admired. Wilder’s book was infinitely generous; that was worth trying to remember.

因此，我从《美国流行歌曲》一书中意识到，或许可以写一本完全属于一个人的关于写作的书。我会自信地从自己的信念和经验出发进行写作——信不信由你——为了阐明我的观点，我会引用我所敬仰的作家的段落。怀尔德的书内容极其丰富，这一点值得我们铭记。

I don’t mean that Wilder was a man without peeves. We wouldn’t value his loves so highly if he didn’t admit that certain famous songs leave him cold. He is depressed, for instance, by the “forced good cheer” of Vincent Youmans’s “Rise ’n’ Shine.” “The injunction of ‘Rise ’n’ Shine’ to grin and bear it,” he writes, “is almost like a Christian Science recruiting song.” By contrast, discussing a Howard Dietz-Arthur Schwartz number later in the book, he writes:

我并非认为怀尔德是个毫无怨言的人。如果他不承认某些名曲让他无动于衷，我们也不会如此珍视他的爱好。例如，文森特·尤曼斯的《Rise ’n’ Shine》中那种“强颜欢笑”的氛围就让他感到沮丧。他写道：“《Rise ’n’ Shine》中那种强颜欢笑、忍耐到底的训诫，几乎就像一首基督教科学派的招募歌曲。” 与之形成鲜明对比的是，在本书后文讨论霍华德·迪茨和阿瑟·施瓦茨的一首歌曲时，他写道：

“A Shine on Your Shoes” is another powerful swinger. If I’m to be cheered up, I’d prefer to try this musical accompaniment than to be exhorted to “Rise ’n’ Shine.” For there is wit as well as a sinewy strength to this song. And, besides, it swings; it’s looser and less instructive than the other, not just lyrically, but musically.

《擦亮你的鞋》是另一首节奏强劲的摇摆乐。如果要振奋精神，我宁愿听听这首歌，也不愿听人劝我“起床啦，精神抖擞”。因为这首歌既诙谐幽默，又充满活力。而且，它节奏欢快，比起其他歌曲，无论是歌词还是旋律，都更加轻松随意，少了些说教意味。

I like the point that instructiveness in writing is a drag. If you want to preach, disguise it as entertainment. “A Shine on My Shoes,” as sung by Fred Astaire in The Bandwagon , is an affirmation of happiness.

我赞同“说教式写作令人厌烦”的观点。如果你想说教，那就把它伪装成娱乐。弗雷德·阿斯泰尔在电影《篷车队》中演唱的《擦亮我的鞋子》是对幸福的肯定。

The verse is extremely fine. It starts out whap! and never quits. In the sixth measure the singer has to practically use clarinet keys to make it. But that kind of vocal work is fun. Take a look at the “straight ahead” verve of this verse. [He provides the first eight measures.]

这段歌词写得极好。开头就酣畅淋漓，而且一气呵成。到了第六小节，歌手几乎要用单簧管的按键才能唱出来。不过这种演唱技巧很有意思。仔细听听这段歌词“直奔主题”的活力。[他提供了前八小节。]

All I need to know I’m home is this verse. But if you need more to convince you, I think the first four measures of the chorus should do it….

我只需要这句歌词就知道我到家了。但如果你还需要更多证据，我想副歌的前四小节应该就足够了……

Another crotchet of Wilder’s that I liked because it took me by surprise turns up in his analysis of Berlin’s “Let’s Face the Music and Dance.” He concedes that it’s “a very well written song, that the lyric is particularly ‘civilized,’ that it is uncluttered, makes every point it sets out to make, indeed, deserves high praise.” That’s a scholar’s objective judgment. But we also like our scholars to be human, and Wilder adds: “Yet I must admit to irritation in the presence of this form of minuscule melodrama. I call it Mata Hari or canoe music.”

怀尔德的另一段话也让我眼前一亮，因为它出乎我的意料。这段话出自他对柏林的《让我们面对音乐和舞蹈》的分析。他承认这首歌“写得非常好，歌词尤其‘文明’，简洁明了，表达的观点都清晰明了，的确值得高度赞扬。”这是学者客观的评价。但我们也希望学者们能有人情味，怀尔德补充道：“然而，我必须承认，面对这种微不足道的煽情之作，我感到有些恼火。我称之为‘玛塔·哈里’或‘独木舟音乐’。”

Here’s an Irving Berlin song, however, that gets full devotion—in a paragraph that could apply to any of the arts in what it says about simplicity:

然而，这里有一首欧文·柏林的歌曲，它获得了充分的赞誉——这段文字所阐述的简洁之美，也适用于任何艺术领域：

“It’s a Lovely Day Tomorrow” is a pure, hymn-like melody recalling Kern at his purest or Arlen in “My Shining Hour.” For some it might seem just a degree too innocent to the point of being studied simplicity. I don’t find it so, perhaps because I’m a musician and I know how enormously difficult it is to write a bone-simple song, within the range of an octave and employing neither artifice nor cleverness. Frankly, if this had been the melody of “God Bless America,” I’d have been far more inclined to favor it over “The Star-Spangled Banner.”

《明天是个好日子》的旋律纯净如赞美诗，让人想起科恩最纯粹的作品，或是阿伦的《我的闪耀时刻》。对某些人来说，它或许显得过于纯真，甚至有些刻意追求简单。但我并不这么认为，或许是因为我本身就是一名音乐家，深知创作一首极简的歌曲有多么困难——音域在一个八度之内，既不矫揉造作，也不故弄玄虚。坦白说，如果这首歌的旋律是《天佑美国》，我肯定会更喜欢它，而不是《星条旗永不落》。

Another kind of music that was in my ear at an early age was classical music. New York’s German-Americans were long the self-appointed caretakers of Europe’s musical culture in the new world, and my grandmother, Frida Zinsser, a second-generation product of that didactic tradition, saw to it that my father played the piano and the violin long after he had lost interest in those instruments and that my sisters and I got taken to Carnegie Hall and the Metropolitan Opera House. I heard the great basso Ezio Pinza as Boris Godunov long before I heard him as Emile de Becque in South Pacific. “Etwas bleibt hängen ,” my grandmother would say, using the least punitive of her many German maxims, as she played Brahms and Schubert at our piano after Sunday lunch when I wanted to be out playing baseball. It means “something remains,” or “something sticks,” and it’s as good an educational credo as I know. Many melodies and leitmotifs that are still in my head were put there by Frida Zinsser’s Germanic faith in the gods of self-improvement.

另一种在我幼年时期就萦绕耳畔的音乐是古典音乐。纽约的德裔美国人长期以来自诩为新大陆欧洲音乐文化的守护者，而我的祖母弗里达·津瑟（Frida Zinsser）正是这种音乐教育传统的第二代传承者。她坚持让我的父亲在对钢琴和小提琴失去兴趣之后仍然继续演奏，并带我和我的姐妹们去卡内基音乐厅和大都会歌剧院欣赏演出。早在听到伟大的男低音歌唱家埃齐奥·平扎（Ezio Pinza）在《南太平洋》中饰演埃米尔·德·贝克之前，我就听过他饰演的鲍里斯·戈杜诺夫。“Etwas bleibt hängen，”祖母会这样说，这是她众多德语格言中最温和的一句。每当周日午餐后，当我只想出去打棒球时，她就会在我们家的钢琴旁弹奏勃拉姆斯和舒伯特。这句话的意思是“有些东西会留下来”，或者“有些东西会留下来”，在我看来，这是一条非常优秀的教育信条。弗里达·津瑟对自我提升之神的日耳曼式信仰，将许多旋律和主题植入我的脑海，至今仍萦绕其中。

Unlike listening to classical music, writing about it was a process I had never thought much about. Then I went to work for the New York Herald Tribune and got to know Virgil Thomson. The “Trib” in those postwar years was the best-written and best-edited newspaper in the country, and I could hardly believe my luck at being a young reporter there. We all had our desks in one room, the city room, which was as big as a city block and just as grimy. The desks were encrusted with coffee stains and the air was foul with the smell of cigarettes and cigars; during the summer it was stirred sluggishly by ancient fans with dangling electric cords that looked like the wires you see lying on the street after an ice storm. There was no airconditioning, but we were conditioned to bad air because we were newspapermen. In the middle of the room the city editor, L. L. Engelking, a terrifying giant from Texas who was obsessed by his quest for the grail of perfection, bellowed his wrath at his imperfect help. I thought it was the most beautiful room in the world.

与聆听古典音乐不同，撰写古典音乐评论对我来说是件从未认真思考过的事情。后来，我去了《纽约先驱论坛报》工作，并结识了维吉尔·汤姆森。在战后那些年里，《论坛报》是全美文笔和编辑水平最高的报纸，我简直不敢相信自己能成为那里的一名年轻记者。我们所有人的办公桌都集中在一个房间里，那就是城市新闻编辑室，它像一个街区那么大，也同样脏乱不堪。办公桌上满是咖啡渍，空气中弥漫着香烟和雪茄的刺鼻气味；夏天，老式电扇缓慢地搅动着空气，垂挂的电线就像冰暴过后街上散落的电线一样。虽然没有空调，但因为我们是新闻工作者，所以早已习惯了糟糕的空气。房间中央，城市编辑L·L·恩格尔金——一个来自德克萨斯、令人畏惧的巨人，他痴迷于追求完美——正对他的不完美助手咆哮着。我觉得那是世界上最美的房间。

But there was one corner whose occupants didn’t fit the journalistic image—the drama and music department. The most startling of its denizens was the legendary fop Lucius Beebe, whose column about “café society” was written in a style that was baroque, or, at the latest, rococo. Beebe came to work in a derby, attired like Beau Brummell, in raiment that except on him hadn’t survived beyond Edwardian London. The next desk belonged to Walter Terry, the dance critic, who, when he stood up to stretch, often stood in Fourth Position, and beyond him sat various skittish young men and women whom the chief music critic had hired to cover the lesser concerts and recitals that he wouldn’t be covering. One of them was the composer and writer Paul Bowles, who not long afterward moved to Tangier and never came back, perhaps driven by the squalor of the Herald Tribune to seek the purifying austerity of the desert, which his subsequent novels, like The Sheltering Sky , so vividly caught.

但有一个角落里的人们却与新闻界的形象格格不入——戏剧和音乐部门。其中最引人注目的是传奇花花公子卢修斯·比比，他那篇关于“咖啡馆社交圈”的专栏文章，文风华丽，至少也是洛可可式的。比比上班时头戴圆顶礼帽，打扮得像博·布鲁梅尔，身上的服饰除了他以外，恐怕在爱德华时代的伦敦就销声匿迹了。隔壁的桌子属于舞蹈评论家沃尔特·特里，他站起来伸展身体时，常常摆出芭蕾舞第四把位的姿势。特里身后坐着一群略显紧张的年轻男女，他们是首席音乐评论家雇来报道那些他自己不打算报道的小型音乐会和独奏会的。其中一位是作曲家兼作家保罗·鲍尔斯，不久之后他搬到了丹吉尔，再也没有回来，或许是受《先驱论坛报》的肮脏环境驱使，去寻求沙漠的净化和清苦，他后来的小说，如《遮蔽的天空》，生动地捕捉到了这一点。

At the center of this small world, as oblivious of the surrounding chaos as the Buddha he slightly resembled, sat the chief critic himself—a short, somewhat round man with mirthful eyes and a look of total assurance that he belonged right where he was. Virgil Thomson was then midway through his fourteen-year reign as the preeminent music critic in America. I knew of him mainly as a composer—in particular, of Four Saints in Three Acts , the opera he wrote with Gertrude Stein. What I didn’t know was what qualities of mind had gone into making him the preeminent music critic in America. His writing style, of course, was velvet-smooth; any reader could tell that much. But who was he? I got a chance to find out in 1948 when I became drama editor of the Herald Tribune , responsible for the Sunday section that included theater, movies, music, dance, art and, eventually, an upstart medium called television. It was a perfect spot for Thomson-watching, and I identified three qualities that gave his work unusual strength.

在这个小世界的中心，如同他略似的佛陀一般，对周围的喧嚣浑然不觉，端坐着首席评论家本人——一个身材矮小、略显圆润的男人，眼神中带着一丝笑意，神态自信满满，仿佛他理所当然地属于这里。当时，维吉尔·汤姆森正处于他长达十四年的美国顶级音乐评论家统治时期。我对他的了解主要来自他作为作曲家的身份——尤其是他与格特鲁德·斯坦共同创作的歌剧《三幕四圣》。但我并不知道，究竟是什么样的精神特质造就了他作为美国顶级音乐评论家的地位。当然，他的文笔流畅优美，任何读者都能感受到这一点。但他究竟是谁呢？1948年，我终于有机会去了解他，当时我成为了《先驱论坛报》的戏剧编辑，负责周日版的内容，涵盖戏剧、电影、音乐、舞蹈、艺术，以及后来兴起的电视媒体。这里是观察汤姆逊作品的绝佳地点，我发现了他的作品具有非凡力量的三个特质。

First, he was fearless. During Virgil Thomson’s tenure no sacred cow could safely graze. He had the most impressive enemies of any critic in town—the board members and managers who ran establishment organizations like the New York Philharmonic, which had become parochial and smug. When Artur Rodzinski resigned as the Philharmonic’s conductor, alleging interference by its autocratic manager, Arthur Judson, who was also president of Columbia Concerts, a firm that sold soloists to the orchestra he was manager of, Thomson wrote a strong column condemning the conflict of interest. Judson replied that he was “now more than ever” Thomson’s enemy and “would remain so.” Thomson took this as good news; he said he saw it as his duty to expose the “manipulators” who controlled the musical scene and “to support with all the power of my praise every artist, composer, group or impresario whose relation to music was based only on music and the sound it makes.”

首先，他无所畏惧。在维吉尔·汤姆森的时代，任何神圣不可侵犯的事物都无法安然无恙。他拥有城里所有评论家中最令人敬畏的敌人——那些掌控着纽约爱乐乐团等老牌机构的董事会成员和经理们，这些机构已经变得目光短浅、自鸣得意。当阿图尔·罗津斯基辞去爱乐乐团指挥一职，指控其专横跋扈的经理亚瑟·贾德森干预时，汤姆森撰写了一篇措辞强烈的专栏文章，谴责这种利益冲突。贾德森同时也是哥伦比亚音乐会公司的总裁，该公司向他所管理的乐团出售独奏家。贾德森回应说，他“现在比以往任何时候都更加”是汤姆森的敌人，“而且永远如此”。汤姆森对此感到欣慰；他说，他认为自己有责任揭露那些控制音乐界的“操纵者”，并“全力支持每一位艺术家、作曲家、团体或演出经纪人，只要他们与音乐的关系仅仅基于音乐及其所产生的声音。”

To lob such a well-aimed grenade over the crenellated walls of the Philharmonic might seem satisfaction enough for one twelve-month period. But Thomson ended that same year with a scuffle that was no less piquant. Describing it some years later in his autobiography, Virgil Thomson , he wrote:

向爱乐音乐厅的城垛墙外投掷这样一枚精准的手榴弹，或许足以让汤姆森在一年内获得满足。但同年年底，汤姆森又卷入了一场同样精彩的冲突。几年后，他在自传《维吉尔·汤姆森》中这样描述这场冲突：

In November the Pope’s encyclical on art and music, Mediator Dei , had been published in Rome, and our bureau chief sent it to me. It encouraged the liturgical use of modern styles in both music and art. Naturally I wrote about it, translating from an Italian text such passages as dealt specifically with music. A flurry of querulous letters from priests editing Catholic papers hinted that the American clergy would have liked to bury the encyclical. And that is what their papers eventually did. I remembered that the American bishops had waited twenty years to implement the century’s earlier encyclical about music, Pius X’s Motu Proprio , of 1903. If now they showed a similar reluctance, that need not surprise. Nor need it stop my cheering. The Pope was news; modern music was my faith; their union was almost too good to believe.

11月，教宗关于艺术和音乐的通谕《天主中保》（Mediator Dei）在罗马出版，我们的分社社长把它寄给了我。通谕鼓励在礼仪中使用现代风格的音乐和艺术。我自然要写篇文章来评论，并从意大利语原文翻译了其中专门论述音乐的段落。一些天主教报纸编辑神父们纷纷来信抱怨，暗示美国神职人员想把这份通谕束之高阁。而他们的报纸最终也确实这么做了。我记得，美国主教们为了落实本世纪早些时候庇护十世于1903年颁布的关于音乐的通谕——《教宗诏书》（Motu Proprio），等了二十年。如果他们现在表现出类似的犹豫，这并不奇怪。但这也不应该阻止我欢呼雀跃。教宗是新闻；现代音乐是我的信仰；两者的结合简直美好得令人难以置信。

Any critic who opens hostilities on both the New York Philharmonic and the Catholic Church in one year is not a man suffering from a failure of nerve.

任何批评家如果一年之内既对纽约爱乐乐团又对天主教会发起攻击，那他绝不是胆小鬼。

Second, Virgil Thomson was no snob. Before him, chief music critics didn’t stray far from their aisle seat at Carnegie Hall and the Met; they might get hit by a piece of jazz while crossing the street. Thomson’s antennae were out everywhere in the American air. Here’s a partial list of what he covered during his first year on the job as the Herald Tribune’s critic, in addition to the opera, the major orchestras and the standard soloists:

其次，维吉尔·汤姆森绝非势利眼。在他之前，首席乐评人几乎足不出户，只待在卡内基音乐厅和大都会歌剧院的过道座位上；他们甚至可能在过马路时被一首爵士乐“击中”。而汤姆森的触角却遍布美国各地。以下是他担任《先驱论坛报》乐评人第一年报道的部分内容，除了歌剧、主要交响乐团和知名独奏家之外：

Maxine Sullivan singing in a nightclub; Paul Bowles’s music for Twelfth Night on Broadway; Walt Disney’s Fantasia ; a student orchestra; two youth orchestras; an opera at the Juilliard School; a Bach oratorio in a church; a Broadway musical by Kurt Weill; Stravinsky’s violin concerto adapted for a ballet; several other dance performances that used modern music; Holy Thursday at St. Patrick’s cathedral; a black preacher in New Jersey who wore white frilled paper wings over his blue serge suit and played swing music on an electric guitar (that was the Easter Sunday piece); a WPA orchestra in Newark; a swing concert at the Museum of Modern Art; the Goldman Band in Central Park, and three suburban and regional orchestras.

玛克辛·沙利文在夜总会演唱；保罗·鲍尔斯为百老汇音乐剧《第十二夜》创作的音乐；沃尔特·迪士尼的《幻想曲》；学生管弦乐队；两支青年管弦乐队；茱莉亚音乐学院的歌剧；教堂里的巴赫清唱剧；库尔特·魏尔的百老汇音乐剧；斯特拉文斯基的小提琴协奏曲改编成芭蕾舞剧；其他几场使用现代音乐的舞蹈表演；圣帕特里克大教堂的圣周四演出；新泽西州一位黑人牧师，身穿蓝色斜纹西装，外罩白色褶边纸翅膀，用电吉他演奏摇摆乐（那是复活节周日的曲目）；纽瓦克的WPA管弦乐队；现代艺术博物馆的摇摆乐音乐会；中央公园的戈德曼乐队，以及三支郊区和地区管弦乐队。

That’s a man who didn’t put any fences around his notion of where good or at least interesting music might be found. Moral: Think flexibly about the field you’re writing about. Its frontiers may no longer be where they were last time you looked.

这个人对哪里能找到好音乐，或者至少是有趣的音乐，并没有设限。由此可见：写作领域需要灵活思考。它的边界可能早已面目全非。

Finally, Thomson’s style conveys great enjoyment. He’s serious but never solemn; his writing has just enough irreverence to keep us off balance. Reading him, I often think: Is he really saying that? Here’s the start of a typical Thomson review:

最后，汤姆森的文风令人愉悦。他严肃却不拘泥于形式；他的文字中恰到好处的戏谑，让我们始终保持着一种微妙的平衡。读他的文章，我常常会想：他真的在说这些吗？以下是一篇典型的汤姆森评论的开头：

Whether one is able to listen without mind-wandering to the Seventh Symphony of Dmitri Shostakovich probably depends on the rapidity of one’s musical perceptions. It seems to have been written for the slow-witted, the not very musical and the distracted. In this respect it differs from nearly all those other symphonies in which abnormal length is part and parcel of the composer’s concept. Beethoven’s Ninth, Mahler’s Ninth and Eighth, Bruckner’s Seventh and the great Berlioz “machines” are long because they could not have been made any shorter without eliminating something the author wanted in. Their matter is complex and cannot be expounded briefly. The Shostakovich piece, on the other hand, is merely a stretching out of material that is in no way deep or difficult to understand.

能否全神贯注地聆听德米特里·肖斯塔科维奇的第七交响曲，或许取决于听众的音乐感知速度。这首交响曲似乎是为反应迟钝、缺乏音乐素养以及容易分心的人而作。在这方面，它与几乎所有其他交响曲都截然不同，后者往往将超长篇幅作为作曲家创作理念的一部分。贝多芬的第九交响曲、马勒的第九和第八交响曲、布鲁克纳的第七交响曲以及伟大的柏辽兹“机器”交响曲之所以篇幅很长，是因为如果不删减作者想要保留的内容，就无法再缩短它们的长度。它们的主题复杂深奥，无法用简短的篇幅来阐述。而肖斯塔科维奇的这首作品，仅仅是对一些并不深奥或难以理解的素材进行拉长而已。

Consider how much musical knowledge that one paragraph contains—and how entertainingly that knowledge is presented to us.

想想这短短一段话里蕴含了多少音乐知识——而且这些知识是以多么有趣的方式呈现给我们的。

Here, in another review, Thomson dutifully pays his respects to a composer he knows he should like better than he does:

在另一篇评论中，汤姆森尽职尽责地向一位他明知自己应该更喜欢的作曲家表达了敬意：

About once a year your reviewer ventures to dip an ear again into the Wagnerian stream. He thinks he ought to find out whether anything about it has changed since the last time or if anything has possibly changed in him that might provoke a reversal of judgment about it all and a return of the passionate absorption with which he used to plunge himself into that vast current of sound…

大约每年一次，笔者都会再次尝试聆听瓦格纳的作品。他觉得应该探究一下，自上次聆听以来，瓦格纳的音乐是否发生了变化，或者他自身是否也发生了某种变化，从而改变了对瓦格纳音乐的看法，并重新燃起他曾经全身心投入那浩瀚音浪的热情……

The instrumentation [of Die Walküre ] remains rich in sound and highly personal. And if it often creates its theatrical excitement by the use of mere hubbub, that excitement is still a dependable effect and the instrumental dispositions are acoustically sound. It has long seemed to me that Wagner’s original contributions to musical art are chiefly of an orchestral nature. His music-writing is more varied in quality than that of any other composer of equal celebrity, even Berlioz; but no matter what the quality, it always sounds well. It is always instrumentally interesting and infallibly sumptuous….

《女武神》的配器依然音色丰富，极具个人特色。即便它常常仅凭喧闹的声响来营造戏剧张力，这种张力依然可靠，乐器的配置也无可挑剔。我一直认为，瓦格纳对音乐艺术的原创贡献主要体现在管弦乐方面。他的音乐创作在质量上比任何一位同等声望的作曲家都更加多样化，甚至超过了柏辽兹；但无论质量如何，它听起来总是悦耳动听。它的乐器演奏总是引人入胜，而且无可挑剔地华丽壮丽……

His troublesomeness on the musical scene has always been due less to the force of his musical genius than to the fact that neither instinct nor training had prepared him to criticize his own work with the objectivity that the quality of genius in it demanded. As a result, every score is a sea beach full of jewelry and jetsam. Fishing about for priceless bits is a rewarding occupation for young musicians, just as bathing in the sound of it is always agreeable to any musical ear. But musicians are likely to find nowadays that the treasure has been pretty well combed and that the continued examination of the remnants yields little they hadn’t known was there before.

他在乐坛的麻烦之处，与其说是源于他卓越的音乐天赋，不如说是源于他既缺乏直觉，也缺乏训练，以至于无法以与其天才特质相匹配的客观视角来审视自己的作品。结果，每一份乐谱都像一片堆满珠宝和残骸的海滩。对于年轻的音乐家来说，从中寻觅无价之宝是一件乐事，正如沉浸在音乐之中对任何一位乐手来说都是一种享受。但如今的音乐家们很可能会发现，这片宝藏已被搜寻得差不多了，继续审视残存的碎片，也鲜有他们之前未曾发现的新东西。

Like his corner of the Herald Tribune’s city room, Virgil Thomson’s writing method didn’t fit the journalistic mold. As newspapermen, the rest of us knew how things had to be done: we typed our copy, double-spaced, and made sure all the pages ended with a paragraph so they could be sent to the composing room separately after each “take” was written. Thomson would come back after a concert or an opera, remove his coat, pick up a pencil and write his review in longhand on a long yellow pad, looking as unhurried as a Victorian novelist—Trollope, perhaps—setting out to describe the English countryside, though in fact he was operating under one of the most brutal of all late-night newspaper deadlines. The sentences rolled out majestically and evidently perfectly formed, for when he reached the end of a yellow sheet, even if he was in the middle of a sentence, he called for a copy boy, who took the piece of paper and dropped it down a chute to the composing room, where a linotypist familiar with Thomson’s handwriting was standing by.

就像他在《先驱论坛报》城市版编辑部的角落一样，维吉尔·汤姆森的写作方式也不符合新闻从业者的常规模式。作为报社人员，我们都知道该怎么做：我们打字，双倍行距，确保每页都以段落结尾，这样每写完一篇后就可以单独送到排版室。而汤姆森看完音乐会或歌剧回来后，会脱下外套，拿起铅笔，在一张长长的黄色便笺本上用手写的方式写下他的评论，看起来就像一位维多利亚时代的作家——或许是特罗洛普——从容不迫地描绘着英国乡村的景色，尽管事实上，他是在最残酷的深夜截稿期限之一下工作的。句子庄严地展开，显然完美无瑕。因为当他写到一张黄纸的尽头时，即使他正在写句子，他也会叫来一个校对员，校对员接过纸条，把它扔进滑槽，送到排字室。在那里，一位熟悉汤姆逊笔迹的排字工正待命。

I marveled at that seemingly casual act of writing, and I marveled again the next morning when I opened the paper and saw the narrative momentum with which one sentence followed another, the pertinent facts of the evening’s performance so elegantly or impishly noted, the arguments for or against the performers so adroitly marshaled.

我惊叹于这种看似随意的写作行为，第二天早上打开报纸时，我又一次惊叹于它流畅的叙事节奏，句子之间衔接自然，当晚演出的相关事实被优雅或诙谐地记录下来，对表演者的赞成或反对的论点被巧妙地组织起来。

Today Virgil Thomson is ninety-one and still writing with vigor. The secret of his writing, like the secret of his music, is a hymn-like simplicity. Beneath all the graces that charm us with their civility, his writing moves, finally, with sequential logic, as all good writing must. I put him with some of my favorite stylists whose writing is unfailingly an act of clear thinking, from Thoreau and Abraham Lincoln to E. B. White and Red Smith.

如今，维吉尔·汤姆森已九十一岁高龄，笔耕不辍。他写作的秘诀，如同他的音乐一样，在于其如赞歌般简洁优美的语言。在所有那些以其优雅风度吸引我们的文笔之下，他的文字最终都遵循着逻辑严密的脉络，正如所有优秀的作品一样。我将他与我最喜爱的一些文体家相提并论，他们的写作始终是清晰思考的体现，例如梭罗、亚伯拉罕·林肯、E·B·怀特和雷德·史密斯。

One reason why Alec Wilder and Virgil Thomson wrote so well about other people’s music is that they were composers themselves. Ultimately, however, every critic is an outsider, one step removed from the creative spark. I wondered to what extent writing could take us inside—to the process of actually making music. Could a singer write about how to sing, or a composer about what it means to compose? For an answer I turned to two great artists who are equally renowned as teachers: the soprano Phyllis Curtin and the composer Roger Sessions.

亚历克·怀尔德和维吉尔·汤姆森之所以能写出如此精彩的音乐评论，原因之一在于他们本身就是作曲家。然而，归根结底，每一位评论家都是局外人，与创作的火花始终隔着一层。我不禁思考，写作究竟能在多大程度上将我们带入音乐的创作过程？歌唱家能否撰写关于如何歌唱的文章？作曲家能否撰写关于作曲意义的文章？为了寻找答案，我求助于两位同样以教师身份闻名的伟大艺术家：女高音歌唱家菲利斯·柯廷和作曲家罗杰·塞申斯。

Knowing Phyllis Curtin was still another bonus of my decade at Yale. In those years she was one of the stars of the Yale School of Music; young singers came from all over the world to study voice with her. Though her own brilliant career was far from over, teaching was what nourished her most, and when she left Yale to become dean of the school of arts at Boston University it continued to be—and still is—her main fulfillment. I called her and asked whether singing, the most basic and probably most undescribable of the arts, has any accessible literature.

认识菲利斯·柯廷是我在耶鲁十年求学经历中的又一意外收获。那几年，她是耶鲁音乐学院的明星之一，世界各地的年轻歌手都慕名而来，向她学习声乐。尽管她辉煌的职业生涯远未结束，但教学才是她最热爱的事业。离开耶鲁，成为波士顿大学艺术学院院长后，教书依然是她最重要的追求，至今依然如此。我给她打了个电话，问她歌唱——这门最基础、或许也是最难以言喻的艺术——是否有任何易于理解的文献资料。

“Most of the books are so technical with all their talk about muscles,” she said, “that you can’t learn anything from them. I can only think of one book that contains the idea—the aesthetic—of what it means to be a singer. It was written by my teacher’s teacher. His name was Oscar Saenger, and his book, which was called The Oscar Saenger Course in Vocal Training , was published in 1915 by the Victor Talking Machine Company. I doubt if there’s another copy in existence, so I’ll send you mine.” She did, and when it came I stepped into a Victorian world. From the opening words of the preface, called “The Art of Song,” I felt like singing.

“大多数书都太技术性了，全是关于肌肉的讲解，”她说，“根本学不到任何东西。我只能想到一本书，它包含了成为一名歌手的理念——一种美学。这本书是我老师的老师写的。他叫奥斯卡·桑格，他的书叫《奥斯卡·桑格声乐训练教程》，1915年由维克多留声机公司出版。我估计世上应该没有第二本了，所以我把我的那本寄给你。” 她真的寄来了，书到手后，我仿佛置身于维多利亚时代的世界。从序言开篇题为“歌唱的艺术”的文字开始，我就情不自禁地想要歌唱。

Song is the noblest, the most intimate, the most complete manner of self-expression known to mankind, and in the last analysis self-expression is the great thing for which mankind is ever searching. As the power to express grows, so the higher ideals of life develop and the greatest and most subtle influences which make for culture come to have full sway.

歌曲是人类已知最高尚、最私密、最完整的自我表达方式，而归根结底，自我表达正是人类永恒追求的伟大目标。随着表达能力的增强，更高的生活理想也随之发展，构成文化的那些最伟大、最微妙的影响因素也得以充分发挥作用。

There comes into every life a time when the inner self can no longer be reached by things from without, when the soul craves that which it can supply to itself alone. Song then becomes not only a source of forgetfulness of material things and a solace, but also an inspiration. It repays the possessor for every effort that has been lavished upon it and returns a thousandfold all that it has cost.

每个人的一生中都会经历这样一个时刻：外在的一切不再能触及内心，灵魂渴望的唯有自身才能给予。此时，歌声不仅成为忘却物质烦恼、寻求慰藉的源泉，更成为灵感的源泉。它回报拥有者倾注于歌声的每一份心血，并以千倍的回报回馈其付出的一切。

In a commercial age like the present we are prone to forget much that really makes life worth living. Anything which develops a love of the beautiful is of incalculable benefit to all. Song is intended to stir us into action and into a condition where we become conscious of the presence of higher, holier things than “are dreamed of in our philosophies.” Rightly has the human voice been called “God’s own instrument.” Entrusted to the care of each human being is this instrument which, as Carlyle pointed out, has within it the power to lead us to the edge of the infinite and to enable us momentarily to gaze beyond.

在当今这样的商业时代，我们很容易忘记许多真正让生活充满意义的东西。任何能够培养我们对美的热爱的事物，都对所有人有着不可估量的益处。歌声旨在激励我们行动，使我们意识到那些比“我们哲学中所设想的”更高尚、更神圣的事物的存在。人声被誉为“上帝的乐器”，可谓名副其实。每个人都被赋予了守护这件乐器的重任，正如卡莱尔所指出的，它蕴含着引领我们抵达无限边缘、让我们得以短暂地凝视彼岸的力量。

As writing, that’s the product of a more innocent age, but as a creed for artists it’s still hard to top. Oscar Saenger’s book was intended to be read in conjunction with a set of Victor records. “Learning to sing depends largely upon a student’s ability to imitate,” he explains, “and consequently the value of good singing records for the student can scarcely be overestimated. Imitation depends upon power of concentration and sympathetic understanding, and these qualities, so essential to the artist, may be developed rapidly by careful, conscientious listening .”

作为文字，它体现了那个更纯真年代的产物，但作为艺术家的信条，它至今仍难以超越。奥斯卡·桑格的这本书原本是打算配合一套维克多唱片一起阅读的。“学习唱歌很大程度上取决于学生的模仿能力，”他解释道，“因此，好的歌唱唱片对学生的价值怎么强调都不为过。模仿取决于专注力和同理心，而这些对艺术家至关重要的品质，可以通过认真聆听迅速培养。”

I liked, needless to say, Saenger’s emphasis on providing good models. Nowhere in his book did I feel that he was trying to be a salesman for his lessons or for Victor; the only thing he was selling was the joy of singing as well as possible. The sacred grove is opened just once to profane spirits. Realizing that he was a pioneer in home instruction by ear, he includes a short chapter called “How to Use the Victrola.” “It is neither necessary nor desirable to wind the motor to its fullest possible extent,” he begins. “A better way is to wind it within a few turns of the full tension and then give the winding key a few turns between records .” That’s as high as high fidelity got in 1915.

毋庸置疑，我非常欣赏桑格强调提供优秀范例的做法。在他的书中，我丝毫感觉不到他是在推销自己的课程或维克多唱片公司；他唯一推销的，是尽其所能歌唱的乐趣。神圣的树林只向世俗的灵魂敞开过一次。意识到自己是家庭听力教学的先驱，他特意加了一章名为“如何使用留声机”的短文。“没有必要也不可取地将马达上满发条，”他开篇写道，“更好的方法是，在接近满张力时上几圈发条，然后在每张唱片之间转动几圈发条键。” 这就是1915年高保真音质所能达到的最高水平。

I asked Phyllis Curtin what her connection was to Oscar Saenger. “So much of what I do as a singer and as a teacher is related to what’s in that book,” she told me. “My teacher was an American basso named Joseph Regneas. He was in his eighties when I started studying with him in 1953, around the time of my New York debut, so he must have done his own studying with Oscar Saenger around the turn of the century. He became such an avid disciple that he changed his name, which actually was Joseph Baernstein, to Regneas, which is Saenger spelled backward. What he learned from Saenger must have had a powerful influence on his concept of tone, for at least half a dozen times in my career ‘I’ve had a singer or a vocal coach come up to me after a concert and say, ‘I’ve only heard a tone floated like that by one other singer,’ and in every case the other singer had been a student of Joseph Regneas.”

我问菲利斯·柯廷她与奥斯卡·桑格有何渊源。“我作为歌手和教师所做的很多事情都与那本书里的内容息息相关，”她告诉我。“我的老师是一位名叫约瑟夫·雷格尼亚斯的美国男低音歌唱家。1953年，我开始跟他学习，那时他已经八十多岁了，大约就在我纽约首演前后。所以他肯定在世纪之交也曾跟随奥斯卡·桑格学习过。他如此虔诚地追随桑格，甚至将自己的名字——原本是约瑟夫·巴恩斯坦——改成了雷格尼亚斯，也就是桑格名字的倒写。他从桑格那里学到的东西肯定对他的音色概念产生了深远的影响，因为在我职业生涯中，至少有六次，一位歌手或声乐教练在音乐会后走过来对我说：‘我只听过另一位歌手发出过如此飘逸的音色。’而每一次，那位歌手都是约瑟夫·雷格尼亚斯的学生。”

One of those tone detectives once asked Phyllis Curtin whether she knew Oscar Saenger’s book. She didn’t, so he sent her his copy. “As soon as I looked into it,” she said, “it was so familiar to me in all its principles.”

一位音乐风格侦探曾问菲利斯·柯廷是否读过奥斯卡·桑格的书。她不知道，于是他把自己的书寄给了她。“我一翻开这本书，”她说，“就觉得它的所有原则都非常熟悉。”

Looking into Saenger’s book myself, I was struck not only by the clarity of its instruction, but by its insistence that mechanical proficiency in a singer is never enough:

我亲自研读了桑格的书，不仅被其清晰的指导所打动，更被其坚持认为歌手的机械熟练程度远远不够的观点所震撼：

The tone should be made to focus on the back of the upper front teeth and the hard palate (roof of the mouth). As an illustration: Close your lips and try to sing the letter M . A distinct vibration will be felt in the region of the hard palate and the front teeth. That is the point on which most tones should be focused. In the case of the head tones the point of focus rises until, in the extreme high register, the sensation is that of placing the tone high in the head.

发声时，音调应集中在上门牙后侧和硬腭（口腔顶部）。举例来说：闭上嘴唇，试着唱字母“M”。你会感觉到硬腭和门牙区域有明显的振动。大多数音调都应该集中在这个位置。对于头音，音调的集中点会逐渐升高，直到极高音区，你会感觉声音仿佛位于头部高处。

It is a matter of sensation and mental concentration. The way to place the tone forward is to think it forward. That is actually the way in which the student must focus her tone. She must think it into place and put it there through the exercise of a purely mental process.

这关乎感觉和精神集中。要使音调靠前，就要在脑海中预先想好。这实际上就是学生集中音调的方式。她必须将音调预先设定好位置，并通过纯粹的心理过程练习来实现。

At that sentence I heard the connection between Phyllis Curtin and Oscar Saenger’s book click into place. I remembered auditing one of her master classes at Yale, in which she warned her students that technique would take them only so far and exhorted them to be true to their individuality. “Singing,” she said, “is an impulse to move. If your mind is only on pushing the button, there isn’t any singing. You have to keep putting the thought in front of the tone. You have to have something that you want to say.”

听到这句话，我突然明白了菲利斯·柯廷和奥斯卡·桑格的书之间的联系。我记起曾在耶鲁旁听过她的一堂大师课，她告诫学生们，技巧只能带他们走到一定程度，并鼓励他们忠于自己的个性。“唱歌，”她说，“是一种想要行动的冲动。如果你的注意力只在于按下按钮，那就不是唱歌。你必须把思想放在音调之前。你必须有话要说。”

Of all the mysteries in music, none is more profound than the mystery of composition. Still, like other abstruse disciplines—philosophy, for example, or religion—it can be written about.
