The following passage by Roger Sessions reduces a complex intellectual act to terms that are disarmingly simple. I’ve chosen it because for more than half a century Sessions, who died in 1985, at the age of eighty-nine, was not only one of America’s most prolific and adventurous composers. He was also an influential teacher, mainly at Princeton and at Berkeley, and this final chapter of Writing to Learn , though ostensibly about music, is equally—music being dependent for its nurture on men and women in every generation who freely pass along what they know—a chapter about teachers.

在音乐的所有奥秘中，没有比作曲更深奥的了。然而，如同其他深奥的学科——例如哲学或宗教——作曲也是可以书写的。罗杰·塞申斯的以下这段文字，将复杂的智力活动简化为简单易懂的语言。我之所以选择这段文字，是因为塞申斯在半个多世纪的时间里，不仅是美国最多产、最具冒险精神的作曲家之一（他于1985年去世，享年89岁），也是一位极具影响力的教师，主要在普林斯顿大学和伯克利大学任教。而《写作学习》的最后一章，虽然表面上是关于音乐的，但同样也是关于教师的——因为音乐的传承依赖于每一代人无私地传递知识。

In trying to understand the work of the composer, one must first think of him as living in a world of sounds, which in response to his creative impulse become animated with movement. The first stage in his work is that of what is generally known by the somewhat shopworn and certainly unscientific term “inspiration.” The composer, to use popular language again, “has an idea”—an idea consisting of definite musical notes and rhythms, which will engender for him the momentum with which his musical thought proceeds. The inspiration may come in a flash, or, as sometimes happens, it may grow and develop gradually. I have in my possession photostatic copies of several pages of Beethoven’s sketches for the last movement of his “Hammerklavier Sonata”; the sketches show him carefully modeling, then testing in systematic and apparently cold-blooded fashion, the theme of the fugue. Where, one might ask, is the inspiration here? Yet if the word has any meaning at all, it is certainly appropriate to this movement, with its irresistible and titanic energy of expression, already present in the theme. The inspiration takes the form, however, not of a sudden flash of music, but of a clearly-envisaged impulse toward a certain goal for which the composer was obliged to strive. When this perfection was attained, however, there could have been no hesitation—rather a flash of recognition that this was exactly what he wanted.

要理解作曲家的作品，首先必须把他想象成生活在一个声音的世界里，而他的创作灵感会赋予这些声音以生命力。他创作的第一阶段，通常被称为“灵感”，这个术语虽然有些老套，也肯定不够科学。用通俗的话来说，作曲家“有了想法”——一个由明确的音符和节奏构成的想法，它将为他的音乐创作提供动力。灵感可能瞬间迸发，也可能像有时那样，逐渐发展壮大。我手头有几页贝多芬《槌子键琴奏鸣曲》末乐章的草稿复印件；这些草稿显示，他仔细地塑造，然后以一种看似冷静、系统的方式反复推敲赋格的主题。人们不禁要问，灵感究竟在哪里呢？然而，如果“灵感”一词有任何意义，它无疑非常贴切地形容了这一乐章，其主题中已蕴含着势不可挡、气势磅礴的表达能量。然而，灵感并非灵光乍现的瞬间，而是作曲家为实现某个目标而精心构思的清晰冲动。当达到这种完美境界时，他不会有任何犹豫——而是会瞬间意识到，这正是他梦寐以求的。

For any music lover that paragraph is a treat—the composer Sessions putting himself inside the head of the composer Beethoven. (For any writer it’s also a crash course in rewriting.) There’s no trace of pedantry in the style; Sessions conveys his excitement over Beethoven’s achievement by using the tools of good English. “Titanic energy” says it all about Beethoven.

对于任何音乐爱好者来说，这段文字都是一份惊喜——作曲家塞申斯仿佛置身于作曲家贝多芬的视角。（对于任何写作者来说，这同时也是一堂速成的改写课。）文风中丝毫没有卖弄学问之嫌；塞申斯运用优美的英语，传达了他对贝多芬成就的激动之情。“泰坦尼克号般的能量”恰如其分地概括了贝多芬的特质。

After “inspiration,” Sessions goes on to explain, the composer’s principal problem is to recapture that inspiration in every phase of his work—to bring “the requisite amount of energy to bear on every detail, as well as, constantly, on his vision of the whole.” This vision of the whole is the “conception.” That brings Sessions to the third pillar of the composer’s edifice—the “execution”:

塞申斯接着解释说，在“灵感”之后，作曲家面临的主要问题是如何在创作的每个阶段重拾灵感——将“必要的精力投入到每一个细节，并始终关注他对整体的构想”。这种对整体的构想就是“构思”。这就引出了塞申斯所说的作曲家创作的第三个支柱——“执行”：

The process of execution is first of all that of listening inwardly to the music as it shapes itself; of allowing the music to grow; of following both inspiration and conception wherever they may lead. A phrase, a motif, a rhythm, even a chord, may contain within itself, in the composer’s imagination, the energy which produces movement. It will lead the composer on, through the force of its own momentum or tension, to other phrases, other motifs, other chords.

创作过程首先是聆听音乐内在的演变过程；是让音乐自然生长；是跟随灵感和构思的指引，任其自由发展。一个乐句、一个动机、一个节奏，甚至一个和弦，在作曲家的想象中，都可能蕴含着推动乐曲发展的能量。凭借自身的动量或张力，它将引领作曲家走向其他乐句、其他动机、其他和弦。

Continuing to lead us through these compositional steps, in language that is vivid and concrete, Sessions comes at last to the mystery that lies at the heart of the creative process, not just in music but in writing, painting, sculpture and every other art, as well as in mathematics, the sciences and the humanities. The mathematician, the scientist and the philosopher, thinking and writing their way toward the center of a problem, are no less immersed than the composer, the artist and the writer in an act of commitment that they can never recover or even explain. What finally impels them all is not the work they achieve, but the work of achieving it.

塞申斯继续以生动具体的语言，引领我们一步步完成这些创作步骤，最终揭示了创作过程的核心奥秘——这不仅适用于音乐，也适用于写作、绘画、雕塑以及其他所有艺术形式，甚至包括数学、科学和人文学科。数学家、科学家和哲学家在思考和写作的过程中，试图探寻问题的核心，他们与作曲家、艺术家和作家一样，都全身心地投入到一种无法回溯甚至解释的创作行为中。最终驱使他们不断前行的，并非他们最终的成果，而是创作的过程本身。

That act of commitment and discovery in every area of knowledge is the essence of this book, and I’m happy to let Roger Sessions sum it up for me and see you to the door:

在各个知识领域中，这种投入和探索的精神正是本书的精髓所在。我很高兴让罗杰·塞申斯为我总结一下，并送您到书末：

How far is the composer “conscious” while he is composing? Of what is he thinking, what are his feelings? The answer, I think, is that composition is a deed , an action, and a genuine action of any kind is, psychologically speaking, the simplest thing in the world. Is not its subjective essence intentness on the deed? The climber in the high mountains is intent on the steps he is taking, on the practical realization of those steps; if he allows his consciousness to dwell even on their implications, his foot may move the fatal half inch too far in the direction of the abyss at his side. The composer working at his music is faced with no such tragic alternatives; but his psychology is not dissimilar. He is not so much conscious of his ideas as possessed by them. Very often he is unaware of his exact processes of thought till he is through with them; extremely often the completed work is incomprehensible to him immediately after it is finished.

作曲家在创作时究竟有多“清醒”？他在想什么？他又在感受什么？我认为答案是，创作是一种行为，一种行动，而任何真正的行动，从心理学角度来说，都是世上最简单的事情。它的主观本质难道不就是专注于行动本身吗？攀登高山的登山者专注于他迈出的每一步，专注于将这些步步付诸实践；如果他让自己的意识停留在哪怕是这些步步的意义上，他的脚就可能朝着身旁的深渊多迈出致命的半英寸。作曲家在创作音乐时并没有面临如此悲剧性的选择；但他的心理状态与此并无二致。他与其说是意识到自己的想法，不如说是被这些想法所支配。很多时候，他直到完成创作才意识到自己具体的思考过程；极少数情况下，作品完成后，他自己也无法立即理解。

Why? Because his experience in creating the work is incalculably more intense than any later experience he can have from it; because the finished product is the goal of that experience and not in any sense a repetition of it. He cannot relive the experience without effort which seems quite irrelevant. And yet he is too close to it to detach himself to the extent necessary to see his work objectively and to allow it to exert its inherent power over him.

为什么？因为他在创作过程中所体验到的感受，远比之后任何从中获得的感受都要强烈得多；因为最终的成品正是那次创作体验的最终目标，而非对那次体验的重复。他无法毫不费力地重温那次体验，而这种努力似乎毫无意义。然而，他与作品的联系太过紧密，以至于无法抽离出来，客观地审视自己的作品，也无法让作品发挥其内在的力量来影响他。

For this reason I have always profoundly disagreed with the definition made by one of my most distinguished living colleagues who, elaborating Aristotle’s famous definition of art, wrote that art on the highest level is concerned with “ der Wiedergabe der inneren Natur ”—literally translated, the reproduction of inner nature. It seems to me, on the contrary, that art is a function, an activity of the inner nature—that the artist’s effort is, using the raw and undisciplined materials with which his inner nature provides him, to endow them with a meaning which they do not of themselves possess—to transcend them by giving them artistic form.

因此，我一直强烈反对我的一位在世的杰出同事对艺术的定义。他援引亚里士多德著名的艺术定义，认为最高层次的艺术关注的是“der Wiedergabe der inneren Natur”（字面翻译为“再现内在自然”）。在我看来，艺术恰恰相反，它是内在自然的一种功能和活动——艺术家的努力在于运用其内在自然赋予的未经雕琢的素材，赋予它们本身并不具备的意义——通过赋予它们艺术形式来超越它们。

Chapter 4: Writing to Learn

第四章：写作学习

53

One unspoken obstacle to a broader-based teaching of writing in American colleges is a tendency in many English departments to regard writing teachers as second-class citizens. The politics of Academia is not the province of this book; the battle will have to be fought from within. A bracing call to arms in these “Mandarin Wars” was sounded by Maxine Hairston, Professor of English at the University of Texas at Austin, in her Chair’s address to the annual convention of the Conference on College Composition and Communication in 1985.

美国高校推广写作教学的一个隐形障碍是，许多英语系倾向于将写作教师视为二等公民。学术界的政治并非本书的探讨范围；这场斗争必须在内部展开。1985年，德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校英语系教授玛克辛·海斯顿在大学写作与交流会议年会上发表主席致辞，为这场“汉语战争”发出了振奋人心的号召。

“Our experience [as writing teachers] is much like that of the women’s movement,” Professor Hairston said. “One can look at how far we have come and rejoice at our progress, or one can look at the barriers that still exist and become discouraged. A major reason we get discouraged is that our major problems originate close to home: in our own departments and within the discipline of English studies itself. And we are having trouble solving those problems precisely because they are so immediate and daily, and because we have complex psychological bonds to the people who so frequently are our adversaries in our efforts to make the writing programs in our departments as good as they should be and can be.

“我们（作为写作教师）的经历与妇女运动的经历非常相似，”海斯顿教授说道。“人们可以回顾我们取得的成就，为之欢欣鼓舞；也可以看到仍然存在的障碍，从而感到沮丧。我们感到沮丧的一个主要原因是，我们面临的主要问题往往源于自身：源于我们各自的系以及英语研究学科本身。我们之所以难以解决这些问题，恰恰是因为这些问题如此迫切且日常，也因为我们与那些经常在我们努力提升系里写作课程质量的过程中与我们作对的人之间存在着复杂的心理联系。”

“I think the time has come to break those bonds…. As rhetoricians and writing teachers we will come of age and become autonomous professionals with a discipline of our own only if we can make a psychological break with the literary critics who today dominate the profession of English studies. Until we move out from behind their shadows and no longer accept their definition of what our profession should be, we are not going to have full confidence in our own mission and our own professionalism…. But logic has long since ceased to be a consideration in this dispute. For the literary establishment, the issue is power; they do not want to relinquish their control of all of English. For us, the issue is survival. We must cut our psychological ties in order to mature.” College Composition and Communication , Vol. XXXVI, No. 3, October 1985. National Council of Teachers of English, 1111 Kenyon Road, Urbana, IL 61801.

我认为现在是时候打破这些束缚了……作为修辞学家和写作教师，只有当我们能够与如今主导英语研究领域的文学批评家们在心理上决裂时，我们才能真正成长为成熟的、拥有自身学科的独立专业人士。除非我们摆脱他们的阴影，不再接受他们对我们职业的定义，否则我们将无法对自己的使命和专业性充满信心……但在这场争论中，逻辑早已不再重要。对文学界而言，问题在于权力；他们不愿放弃对整个英语领域的控制。对我们而言，问题在于生存。我们必须斩断心理上的束缚才能走向成熟。《大学写作与交流》，第36卷，第3期，1985年10月。美国英语教师协会，地址：伊利诺伊州厄巴纳市肯扬路1111号，邮编：61801。

Chapter 7: Art and Artists

第七章：艺术与艺术家

104

At George Nelson’s memorial service in 1986, one former client spoke of the freshness of his thinking in 1940; another recalled the freshness of his thinking in 1986, the year he died. Noting this fact in a memoir in the magazine ID , the critic Ralph Caplan said: “A recent study of disorientation and memory loss among the elderly reports that people can be helped by simple exercises requiring them to think. The problem is not so much deterioration as the loss of what might be called the habit of thinking. It was a habit George Nelson never gave up, and his persistence in thinking as a design function was at the heart of his effectiveness as a design consultant.”

在1986年乔治·尼尔森的追悼会上，一位前客户回忆起他1940年思维的敏锐；另一位客户则回忆起他1986年——也就是他去世的那一年——思维的敏锐。评论家拉尔夫·卡普兰在《ID》杂志的回忆录中指出这一点，他写道：“最近一项关于老年人迷失方向和记忆力衰退的研究表明，一些简单的思考练习可以帮助人们。问题不在于衰退本身，而在于丧失了所谓的思考习惯。乔治·尼尔森从未放弃过这种习惯，他坚持将思考作为一种设计功能，这正是他作为设计顾问卓有成效的核心所在。”

167

Two books recommended by Joan Countryman for clear writing on mathematics are The Mathematical Experience , by Philip J. Davis and Reuben Hersh, Houghton Mifflin Co., 1981, and Descartes’ Dream: The World According to Mathematics , by the same authors, Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, 1986. A book that took me enjoyably and painlessly into the mind and the life work of a great mathematician is S. M. Ulam’s Adventures of a Mathematician (Scribner paperback). Several teachers have spoken admiringly of Alfred North Whitehead’s Introduction to Mathematics . Professor Keith Stewart Thomson of Yale, former dean of the Yale Graduate School, told me: “I would recommend any part, but especially the first two chapters, of Whitehead’s book. His style is perfect for his purpose—to talk about mathematics without scaring the reader.”

琼·康特里曼推荐的两本数学入门读物分别是菲利普·J·戴维斯和鲁本·赫什合著的《数学经验》（霍顿·米夫林出版社，1981年）以及同一作者合著的《笛卡尔之梦：数学眼中的世界》（哈考特·布雷斯·乔万诺维奇出版社，1986年）。S·M·乌拉姆的《数学家的冒险》（斯克里布纳出版社平装本）让我轻松愉快地走进了这位伟大数学家的思想世界和毕生事业。许多老师都对阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海的《数学导论》赞不绝口。耶鲁大学前研究生院院长、耶鲁大学教授基思·斯图尔特·汤姆森告诉我：“我推荐怀特海这本书的任何部分，尤其是前两章。他的写作风格完美契合了他的目的——用浅显易懂的方式讲解数学，而不会让读者感到畏惧。”

关于物理学研究：二十世纪最受尊敬和最具影响力的物理学家之一伊恩·伊万诺维奇·拉比于1988年1月11日逝世，享年89岁。《纽约时报》的讣告称，拉比博士认为物理学是“最崇高的学科，也是最基础的学科”，他总是努力让学生们感受到物理学的伟大。“你们正在与一位冠军较量，”他告诉他们，“你们试图探寻上帝创造世界的奥秘，就像雅各与天使摔跤一样。”

About the Author

作者简介

W ILLIAM Z INSSER is a writer, editor and teacher. He began his career with New York Herald Tribune and has since written regularly for leading magazines. His sixteen books include Writing to Learn, Mitchell & Ruff , about the jazz musicians Dwike Mitchell and Willie Ruff; and, most recently, Easy to Remember: The Great American Songwriters and Their Songs . During the 1970s, he taught writing at Yale, where he was master of Branford College. He now teaches at the New School in New York, his hometown.

威廉·津瑟是一位作家、编辑和教师。他的职业生涯始于《纽约先驱论坛报》，此后一直定期为各大知名杂志撰稿。他著有十六本书，包括《写作学习》（Writing to Learn）、《米切尔与拉夫》（Mitchell & Ruff，讲述爵士音乐家德威克·米切尔和威利·拉夫的故事）以及最近出版的《易于记忆：伟大的美国歌曲作家及其歌曲》（Easy to Remember: The Great American Songwriters and Their Songs）。20世纪70年代，他曾在耶鲁大学教授写作，并担任布兰福德学院院长。如今，他在家乡纽约的新学院任教。
